issue.body:
Bumps [@playwright/test](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright) from 1.58.2 to 1.60.0.
Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.60.0

🌐 HAR recording on Tracing

tracing.startHar() / tracing.stopHar() expose HAR recording as a first-class tracing API, with the same content, mode and urlFilter options as recordHar. The returned Disposable makes it easy to scope a recording with await using:

await using har = await context.tracing.startHar('trace.har');
const page = await context.newPage();
await page.goto('https://playwright.dev');
// HAR is finalized when `har` goes out of scope.

🪝 Drop API

New locator.drop() simulates an external drag-and-drop of files or clipboard-like data onto an element. Playwright dispatches dragenter, dragover, and drop with a synthetic [DataTransfer] in the page context — works cross-browser and is great for testing upload zones:

await page.locator('#dropzone').drop({
  files: { name: 'note.txt', mimeType: 'text/plain', buffer: Buffer.from('hello') },
});

await page.locator('#dropzone').drop({
data: {
'text/plain': 'hello world',
'text/uri-list': 'https://example.com',
},
});

🎯 Aria snapshots

  • expect(page).toMatchAriaSnapshot() now works on a Page, in addition to a Locator — equivalent to asserting against page.locator('body').
  • New boxes option on locator.ariaSnapshot() / page.ariaSnapshot() appends each element's bounding box as [box=x,y,width,height], useful for AI consumption.

🛑 test.abort()

New test.abort() aborts the currently running test from a fixture, hook, or route handler with an optional message. Use it when you have detected an unrecoverable misuse and want to fail the test right away:

test('does not publish to the shared page', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.route('**/publish', route => {
    test.abort('Tests must not publish to the shared page. Use the `clone` option.');
    return route.abort();
  });
  // ...
});

issue.title: bug: proxy middleware treats 127.0.0.1 as public domain causing redirect loop in E2E/CI
bug: Bicep emits AUTH_B2C_* but auth.ts reads AZURE_AD_B2C_* — B2C provider can never register
issue.body:
## Problem
Identified during investigation of #259.

\iac/backend/container-app.bicep\ sets container env vars named \AUTH_B2C_*\ but \^Gpps/web/src/auth.ts\ reads \AZURE_AD_B2C_*\ (following NextAuth/Auth.js convention).

Additionally, the Bicep uses \AUTH_PROVIDER_B2C_ENABLED\ as the gate variable but auth.ts checks \AUTH_PROVIDER_MICROSOFT_ENABLED\.

This means B2C provider can **never register** in production regardless of KV secret values.

## Fix
In \iac/backend/container-app.bicep\:
- Rename \AUTH_B2C_TENANT_NAME\ → \AZURE_AD_B2C_TENANT_NAME\
- Rename \AUTH_B2C_CLIENT_ID\ → \AZURE_AD_B2C_CLIENT_ID\
- Rename \AUTH_B2C_CLIENT_SECRET\ → \AZURE_AD_B2C_CLIENT_SECRET\
- Rename gate var \AUTH_PROVIDER_B2C_ENABLED\ → \AUTH_PROVIDER_MICROSOFT_ENABLED\

## Related
- #259 — production auth Configuration error (parent)
- #261 — missing b2c-tenant-name secret

issue.title: chore: restrict to squash-merge only and enable delete-branch-on-merge

labels.name: process-improvement
labels.description: Sprint retro and process improvement work

issue.body:
## Problem
All 3 merge strategies (squash, merge commit, rebase) are enabled. Produces inconsistent history.

\delete_branch_on_merge\ is \ alse\ — merged branches accumulate. Currently 40+ open PRs with stale branches.

## Fix
- \^Gllow_squash_merge: true\
- \^Gllow_merge_commit: false\
- \^Gllow_rebase_merge: false\
- \delete_branch_on_merge: true\
- \squash_merge_commit_title: PR_TITLE\
- \squash_merge_commit_message: PR_BODY\

## Impact
Clean linear history, automatic branch cleanup on merge.

issue.title: chore: enable branch protection on main - require PR and CI status check

labels.name: process-improvement
labels.description: Sprint retro and process improvement work

issue.body:
## Problem
\main\ has zero branch protection. Anyone can push directly, bypassing CI and review.

## Fix
Enable branch protection on \main\:
- Require a pull request before merging
- Require status check \ci\ to pass before merging
- Require branches to be up to date before merging
- Do not allow bypassing the above settings

## Impact
Without this, all CI is advisory-only. Broken code can land on main silently.

issue.title: chore: parallelise CI jobs — lint, typecheck, and build can fan out

labels.name: process-improvement
labels.description: Sprint retro and process improvement work

issue.body:
## Problem
\ci.yml\ runs all steps sequentially in one job. A lint failure still pays full job startup cost.

## Fix
Split into parallel jobs with explicit needs dependencies:

\\\
lint      --+
             +--> build --> db-push --> unit-tests --> e2e-smoke
typecheck --+
\\\

## Impact
1-2 min faster feedback on the most common failure modes (lint/type errors).

labels.name: process-improvement
labels.description: Sprint retro and process improvement work

issue.body:
## Problem
\^Gllow_auto_merge\ is \ alse\. Dependabot has 37 open PRs requiring manual merge even when CI is green.

## Fix
- Set \^Gllow_auto_merge: true\ on the repo
- Add a workflow that calls \gh pr merge --auto --squash\ on Dependabot PRs after CI passes

## Depends on
Branch protection must be enabled first — auto-merge only triggers after required checks pass (see related issue).

## Impact
Eliminates manual toil for all routine dependency updates.

issue.title: chore: restrict to squash-merge only and enable delete-branch-on-merge

labels.name: process-improvement
labels.description: Sprint retro and process improvement work

issue.body:
## Problem
All 3 merge strategies (squash, merge commit, rebase) are enabled. Produces inconsistent history.

\delete_branch_on_merge\ is \ alse\ — merged branches accumulate. Currently 40+ open PRs with stale branches.

## Fix
- \^Gllow_squash_merge: true\
- \^Gllow_merge_commit: false\
- \^Gllow_rebase_merge: false\
- \delete_branch_on_merge: true\
- \squash_merge_commit_title: PR_TITLE\
- \squash_merge_commit_message: PR_BODY\

## Impact
Clean linear history, automatic branch cleanup on merge.

issue.title: chore: enable branch protection on main - require PR and CI status check

labels.name: process-improvement
labels.description: Sprint retro and process improvement work

issue.body:
## Problem
\main\ has zero branch protection. Anyone can push directly, bypassing CI and review.

## Fix
Enable branch protection on \main\:
- Require a pull request before merging
- Require status check \ci\ to pass before merging
- Require branches to be up to date before merging
- Do not allow bypassing the above settings

## Impact
Without this, all CI is advisory-only. Broken code can land on main silently.

issue.body:
Bumps [@playwright/test](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright) from 1.58.2 to 1.60.0.
Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.60.0

🌐 HAR recording on Tracing

tracing.startHar() / tracing.stopHar() expose HAR recording as a first-class tracing API, with the same content, mode and urlFilter options as recordHar. The returned Disposable makes it easy to scope a recording with await using:

await using har = await context.tracing.startHar('trace.har');
const page = await context.newPage();
await page.goto('https://playwright.dev');
// HAR is finalized when `har` goes out of scope.

🪝 Drop API

New locator.drop() simulates an external drag-and-drop of files or clipboard-like data onto an element. Playwright dispatches dragenter, dragover, and drop with a synthetic [DataTransfer] in the page context — works cross-browser and is great for testing upload zones:

await page.locator('#dropzone').drop({
  files: { name: 'note.txt', mimeType: 'text/plain', buffer: Buffer.from('hello') },
});

await page.locator('#dropzone').drop({
data: {
'text/plain': 'hello world',
'text/uri-list': 'https://example.com',
},
});

🎯 Aria snapshots

  • expect(page).toMatchAriaSnapshot() now works on a Page, in addition to a Locator — equivalent to asserting against page.locator('body').
  • New boxes option on locator.ariaSnapshot() / page.ariaSnapshot() appends each element's bounding box as [box=x,y,width,height], useful for AI consumption.

🛑 test.abort()

New test.abort() aborts the currently running test from a fixture, hook, or route handler with an optional message. Use it when you have detected an unrecoverable misuse and want to fail the test right away:

test('does not publish to the shared page', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.route('**/publish', route => {
    test.abort('Tests must not publish to the shared page. Use the `clone` option.');
    return route.abort();
  });
  // ...
});

issue.title: chore(deps): Bump @microsoft/applicationinsights-web from 3.3.11 to 3.4.1 in /apps/web

issue.body:
Bumps [@microsoft/applicationinsights-web](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-JS) from 3.3.11 to 3.4.1.
Release notes

Sourced from @​microsoft/applicationinsights-web's releases.

3.4.1

This is the first full supported release of the 3.4.x version line. While a 3.4.0-beta was previously released for early testing and validation, version 3.4.0 was not released as a standard supported version — 3.4.1 is the first production-ready release in this series. The @microsoft/1ds-post-js channel is numbered 4.4.1 and requires v3.4.1.

Significant Changes (since 3.3.11)

The following are the significant changes since the previous full release (3.3.11). Some of these changes were previously included in the 3.4.0-beta release.

  • W3C Trace State Support: Added full support for managing W3C Trace State and sending headers in distributed tracing, including new distributed tracing modes AI_AND_W3C_TRACE and W3C_TRACE that enable the tracestate header to be sent with requests when trace state information is available, the existing states will continue to not send the header.

  • New Distributed Tracing Modes: Added new eDistributedTracingModes enum values:

    • AI_AND_W3C_TRACE (17): Sends Application Insights headers + W3C traceparent + W3C tracestate headers (if state value is present)
    • W3C_TRACE (18): Sends only W3C traceparent + W3C tracestate headers (if state value is present)

  • Enhanced Distributed Tracing: Refactored the distributed tracing implementation to provide better support for the W3C Trace Context specification and prepare for future OpenTelemetry Span-style API integration.

  • New W3C TraceState API: Introduced the IW3cTraceState interface that provides a mutable, ordered list of key/value pairs for trace state information with proper parent-child relationships.

  • OpenTelemetry Integration Preparation: Added foundational OpenTelemetry interfaces (IOTelSpanContext, IOTelTraceState) to provide OpenTelemetry API compatibility.

  • Additional Configuration: Added new configuration properties for W3C trace state support:

    • traceHdrMode: Controls if the SDK should look for the traceparent and/or tracestate values from service timing headers or meta tags from the initial page load (in IConfiguration)
    • Enhanced distributedTracingMode property to support the new W3C trace state modes (in ICorrelationConfig)

  • Dependencies Extension: The dependency tracking extension now includes additional logic for W3C trace state handling, which may affect custom dependency listeners or initializers. The following interfaces and functions have been enhanced with W3C trace state support:

    • IDependencyListenerDetails interface now also includes a readonly traceState along with the previous traceId, spanId, traceFlags properties
    • addDependencyListener() function now provides access to W3C trace state information through the enhanced details object
    • addDependencyInitializer() function continues to work with existing dependency telemetry processing
    • Custom dependency listeners can now access and modify W3C trace state information before requests are sent

  • Enhanced Cookie Management: Cookie values are now cached in memory when cookies are disabled instead of being lost, enabling support for consent banner workflows where cookies must be temporarily disabled until user approval. Automatic flushing occurs when cookies are re-enabled.

  • OsPlugin Reliability Improvements: Improved OsPlugin with proactive OS retrieval, unload handling, and session caching for more reliable OS detection.

  • URL Redaction Enhancements: Made URL redaction more dynamic for improved flexibility in field redaction scenarios.

Package Deprecation

The following packages have been merged into @microsoft/applicationinsights-core-js and are now deprecated. They continue to be published as backward-compatible shims (re-exporting from Core) so existing code will not break, but they are no longer used as dependencies by the main SDK packages. You should stop importing from these packages and migrate to @microsoft/applicationinsights-core-js directly.

  • @microsoft/applicationinsights-common — All exports have been merged into @microsoft/applicationinsights-core-js. The package is now a compatibility shim that re-exports from Core. See the Migration Guide for details on updating your imports. This package will be removed in a future major release (4.0.0).

  • @microsoft/1ds-core-js — All exports have been merged into @microsoft/applicationinsights-core-js. The package is now a compatibility shim that re-exports from Core. See the 1DS Core Migration Guide for class/import name changes and migration steps. Consumers should update their imports to reference @microsoft/applicationinsights-core-js directly. This package will be removed in a future major release (4.0.0).

Breaking Changes

The following is a list of known breaking changes for anyone attempting to implement the interfaces, for end-users / consumers of the existing interface this is considered to be only a potential breaking change as the existing functions are still provided and provide the same level of functionality. The breaking nature of these changes is for anyone attempting to provide their own implementation of these changes.

Interface Changes

  • The IDistributedTraceContext interface has been significantly expanded to include W3C trace state management capabilities, which may affect custom telemetry processors that interact with distributed tracing context.

... (truncated)

Bumps [jest](https://github.com/jestjs/jest/tree/HEAD/packages/jest) and [@types/jest](https://github.com/DefinitelyTyped/DefinitelyTyped/tree/HEAD/types/jest). These dependencies needed to be updated together. Updates `jest` from 29.7.0 to 30.4.2
Release notes

Sourced from jest's releases.

v30.4.2

Fixes

  • [jest-runtime] Fix named imports from CJS modules whose module.exports is a function with own-property exports (#16150)

Full Changelog: https://github.com/jestjs/jest/compare/v30.4.1...v30.4.2

v30.4.1

Features

  • [jest-config, jest-core, jest-runner, jest-schemas, jest-types] Allow custom runner configuration options via tuple format ['runner-path', {options}] (#16141)

Fixes

  • [jest-runtime] Align CJS-from-ESM default export with Node: module.exports is always the ESM default, __esModule unwrapping is no longer applied (#16143)

Full Changelog: https://github.com/jestjs/jest/compare/v30.4.0...v30.4.1

v30.4.0

Big release! 😀

Main feature is a rewrite of our custom runtime in preparation for stabilisation of native support of ESM. As part of that work require(esm) module is now supported on Node 24.9+ (still requires --experimental-vm-modules like before).

In addition we now support fake timers for the recently released Temporal API in Node v26.

React 19 is also supported properly in pretty-format, meaning snapshots of React components now work like they should.

Due to all the changes, there might be regressions that snuck in. Please report them!

Full list of changes below

Features

  • [babel-jest] Support collecting coverage from .mts, .cts (and other) files (#15994)
  • [jest-circus, jest-cli, jest-config, jest-core, jest-jasmine2, jest-types] Add --collect-tests flag to discover and list tests without executing them (#16006)
  • [jest-config, jest-runner, jest-worker] Add workerGracefulExitTimeout config option to control how long workers are given to exit before being force-killed (#15984)
  • [jest-config] Add support for jest.config.mts as a valid configuration file (#16005)
  • [jest-config, jest-core, jest-reporters, jest-runner] verbose and silent can now be set per-project; the project-level value overrides the global value for that project's tests (#16133)
  • [@jest/fake-timers] Accept Temporal.Duration in jest.advanceTimersByTime() and jest.advanceTimersByTimeAsync() (#16128)
  • [@jest/fake-timers] Accept Temporal.Instant and Temporal.ZonedDateTime in jest.setSystemTime() and useFakeTimers({now}) (#16128)
  • [@jest/fake-timers] Support faking Temporal.Now.* (#16131)
  • [jest-mock] Add clearMocksOnScope(scope) on ModuleMocker for clearing every mock function exposed on a scope object (#16088)
  • [jest-resolve] Add canResolveSync() on Resolver so callers can detect when a user-configured resolver only exports an async hook (#16064)
  • [jest-runtime] Use synchronous evaluate() for ES modules without top-level await on Node versions that support it (v24.9+), and prefer the synchronous transform path when a sync transformer is configured (#16062)
  • [jest-runtime] Support require() of ES modules on Node v24.9+ (#16074)
  • [jest-runtime] Validate TC39 import attributes (with { type: 'json' }) on ESM imports (#16127)
  • [@jest/transform] Add canTransformSync(filename) on ScriptTransformer so callers can pick the sync vs async transform path (#16062)
  • [jest-util] Add isError helper (#16076)

... (truncated)

Changelog

Sourced from jest's changelog.

30.4.2

Fixes

  • [jest-runtime] Fix named imports from CJS modules whose module.exports is a function with own-property exports (#16150)

30.4.1

Features

  • [jest-config, jest-core, jest-runner, jest-schemas, jest-types] Allow custom runner configuration options via tuple format ['runner-path', {options}] (#16141)

Fixes

  • [jest-runtime] Align CJS-from-ESM default export with Node: module.exports is always the ESM default, __esModule unwrapping is no longer applied (#16143)

30.4.0

Features

  • [babel-jest] Support collecting coverage from .mts, .cts (and other) files (#15994)
  • [jest-circus, jest-cli, jest-config, jest-core, jest-jasmine2, jest-types] Add --collect-tests flag to discover and list tests without executing them (#16006)

issue.title: bug: missing b2c-tenant-name secret breaks all Container App image updates
issue.body:
## Problem
\^Gz containerapp update --image\ fails with:
\\\
ERROR: (ContainerAppSecretRefNotFound) SecretRef 'b2c-tenant-name' defined for container 'wawkr-api' not found.
\\\
The container app template env var \AUTH_B2C_TENANT_NAME\ references secret \ 2c-tenant-name\ but that secret was removed from the container app secrets list (likely during a bootstrap reset), blocking every deploy since run #26401165073.

## Hotfix applied (needs permanent fix)
Added \ 2c-tenant-name=wawkrid\ as a literal-value secret directly on the Container App via \^Gz containerapp secret set\ to unblock deploys.

## Permanent fix required
- Update Bicep to guard the \ 2c-tenant-name\ secret behind the \ 2cEnabled\ flag (same as the env var is), so it is never orphaned
- OR remove \AUTH_B2C_TENANT_NAME\ env var entirely since \AUTH_PROVIDER_B2C_ENABLED=false\

## Impact
All \deploy-web.yml\ runs failed from 12:42 UTC today until hotfix applied (~18:30 UTC).

issue.title: bug: deploy-iac, deploy-api, and deploy-web share concurrency group causing mutual blocking
issue.body:
## Problem

Three workflows share the same concurrency group deploy-azure-REF:
- deploy-iac.yml
- deploy-api.yml  
- deploy-web.yml

With cancel-in-progress: false they queue behind each other. An infra deploy blocks web deploys and vice versa. Also, deploy-api.yml and deploy-web.yml appear to be duplicates — same trigger paths, same concurrency group, both deploying apps/web.

## Impact
- Web deploys queue behind infra deploys and each other
- Duplicate workflows waste runner minutes

## Fix
- Give each workflow its own concurrency group
- Investigate deploy-api.yml vs deploy-web.yml duplication and consolidate

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Each deploy workflow has a unique concurrency group
- [ ] No deploy workflow blocks an unrelated one  
- [ ] Duplicate web deploy workflows consolidated or differentiated

issue.title: feat: split CI into independent web and mobile platform paths with MOBILE_CI_ENABLED gate
issue.body:
## Problem

The monolithic \ci.yml\ runs lint/typecheck/build/test across all packages including mobile. Mobile builds are not yet active but block the web CI path. There is no way to independently disable mobile CI without touching workflow files.

## Solution

1. **Scope \ci.yml\ to web/shared packages only** — exclude \@wawkr/mobile\ from turbo runs using \--filter=!@wawkr/mobile\, add \paths-ignore\ for \^Gpps/mobile/**\ so pure mobile changes don't trigger web CI.
2. **Gate all mobile workflows behind \MOBILE_CI_ENABLED\ repo variable** — add \if: vars.MOBILE_CI_ENABLED == 'true'\ to every job in \mobile-ci.yml\, \mobile-build-android.yml\, \mobile-build-ios.yml\, \mobile-ota.yml\, \mobile-release.yml\, and \mobile-submit.yml\.
3. **Add \paths\ trigger to \mobile-ci.yml\** — already has path filtering; confirm it does not run on web-only changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] \ci.yml\ does not include mobile packages in lint/typecheck/build/test
- [ ] All mobile workflows skip all jobs when \MOBILE_CI_ENABLED != 'true'\
- [ ] Setting \MOBILE_CI_ENABLED=true\ re-enables mobile CI with no file changes
- [ ] Web CI and mobile CI can each trigger and pass independently
- [ ] Repo variable \MOBILE_CI_ENABLED\ is documented in \docs/\ or README

issue.title: feat: add structured auth telemetry for RCA of sign-in failures
issue.body:
## Goal
Auth failures (\?error=Configuration\, \UnknownAction\, \InvalidCheck\) are opaque in App Insights — no structured events show which provider, which step, or what env vars were in effect.

## Required telemetry
1. **Auth startup event** — log provider list, issuer URLs, and whether required env vars are present at module load (no secrets, only presence/format)
2. **Sign-in attempt event** — provider ID, timestamp, correlation ID
3. **Auth error event** — error code, error class (InvalidCheck/UnknownAction/OAuthCallbackError), provider, whether PKCE cookie was present
4. **Callback event** — provider, PKCE outcome, token issuer received vs expected
5. **Structured exception** — propagate Auth.js internal errors to App Insights \	rackException\ with provider and phase as properties

## Acceptance criteria
- App Insights \customEvents\ table shows \^Guth.startup\, \^Guth.signin.attempt\, \^Guth.signin.error\, \^Guth.callback.error\ events
- Each event has \provider\, \^[rrorCode\, \phase\ dimensions
- No secrets or PII in any telemetry property
- \?error=Configuration\ scenario is diagnosable from App Insights alone without needing container logs

Added \ 2c-tenant-name=wawkrid\ as a literal-value secret directly on the Container App via \^Gz containerapp secret set\ to unblock deploys.

- OR remove \AUTH_B2C_TENANT_NAME\ env var entirely since \AUTH_PROVIDER_B2C_ENABLED=false\

## Impact
All \deploy-web.yml\ runs failed from 12:42 UTC today until hotfix applied (~18:30 UTC).

issue.title: RCA: temporary TLS outage perception during Front Door custom-domain propagation
issue.body:
## Summary

- Users experienced site as down/untrusted on affected hostnames.

## Evidence
- Prior cutover notes show AFD cert state transitions and delayed edge propagation.

## Workaround (no fix applied in this issue)
- Communicate propagation window and hold user-facing cutover completion until cert validates end-to-end.

## Follow-up scope
- Add TLS readiness gate and explicit propagation hold window in runbook.
- Keep smoke tests with hostname fallback during transition.

issue.title: Update OIDC bootstrap for enterprise-scoped GitHub issuer
issue.body:
GitHub Actions authentication is failing with `AADSTS700211` because the enterprise-level GitHub OIDC issuer policy changed the token issuer from the default `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com` to an enterprise-scoped issuer such as `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com/ibuyspy`.

Update the bootstrap/generation scripts and any workflow templates that create or reference Entra federated identity credentials so they use the correct issuer for this enterprise setting.

### Requirements
- Detect whether the enterprise OIDC custom issuer policy is enabled.
- Use the matching issuer when creating federated credentials.
- Fix any subject formatting bugs in generated credentials.
- Keep `audience` set to `api://AzureADTokenExchange` unless a repo has a specific exception.
- Update docs/templates so generated examples match the runtime behavior.

### Notes
- Entra federated credentials must match issuer/subject/audience exactly.
- If the enterprise setting is enabled but the credential still uses the old issuer, token exchange will fail.
- If the enterprise setting is disabled but the credential uses the enterprise-scoped issuer, token exchange will also fail.

This should be tracked so the production environment can be completed and the auth configuration error can be resolved end-to-end.

Release notes

Sourced from eslint-config-next's releases.

v16.2.6

[!NOTE] This release contains security fixes and backported bug fixes. It does not include all pending features/changes on canary.

Security Fixes

The following advisories have been addressed:

High:

  • GHSA-8h8q-6873-q5fj: Denial of Service with Server Components
  • GHSA-267c-6grr-h53f: Middleware / Proxy bypass in App Router applications via segment-prefetch routes
  • GHSA-26hh-7cqf-hhc6: Middleware / Proxy bypass in App Router applications via segment-prefetch routes - Incomplete Fix Follow-Up
  • GHSA-mg66-mrh9-m8jx: Denial of Service via connection exhaustion in applications using Cache Components
  • GHSA-492v-c6pp-mqqv: Middleware / Proxy bypass through dynamic route parameter injection
  • GHSA-c4j6-fc7j-m34r: Server-side request forgery in applications using WebSocket upgrades
  • GHSA-36qx-fr4f-26g5: Middleware / Proxy bypass in Pages Router applications using i18n

Moderate:

  • GHSA-ffhc-5mcf-pf4q: Cross-site scripting in App Router applications using CSP nonces

  • GHSA-h64f-5h5j-jqjh: Denial of Service in the Image Optimization API
  • GHSA-wfc6-r584-vfw7: Cache poisoning in React Server Component responses

Low:

  • GHSA-vfv6-92ff-j949: Cache poisoning via collisions in React Server Component cache-busting
  • GHSA-3g8h-86w9-wvmq: Middleware / Proxy redirects can be cache-poisoned

Core Changes

  • fix: preserve HTTP access fallbacks during prerender recovery (#92231)
  • Fix fallback route params case in app-page handler (#91737)
  • Fix invalid HTML response for route-level RSC requests in deployment adapter (#91541)
  • Patch setHeader for direct route handlers (#93101)

Bumps [jest](https://github.com/jestjs/jest/tree/HEAD/packages/jest) and [@types/jest](https://github.com/DefinitelyTyped/DefinitelyTyped/tree/HEAD/types/jest). These dependencies needed to be updated together. Updates `jest` from 29.7.0 to 30.4.2
Release notes

Sourced from jest's releases.

v30.4.2

Fixes

  • [jest-runtime] Fix named imports from CJS modules whose module.exports is a function with own-property exports (#16150)

Full Changelog: https://github.com/jestjs/jest/compare/v30.4.1...v30.4.2

v30.4.1

Features

  • [jest-config, jest-core, jest-runner, jest-schemas, jest-types] Allow custom runner configuration options via tuple format ['runner-path', {options}] (#16141)

Fixes

  • [jest-runtime] Align CJS-from-ESM default export with Node: module.exports is always the ESM default, __esModule unwrapping is no longer applied (#16143)

Full Changelog: https://github.com/jestjs/jest/compare/v30.4.0...v30.4.1

v30.4.0

Big release! 😀

Main feature is a rewrite of our custom runtime in preparation for stabilisation of native support of ESM. As part of that work require(esm) module is now supported on Node 24.9+ (still requires --experimental-vm-modules like before).

In addition we now support fake timers for the recently released Temporal API in Node v26.

React 19 is also supported properly in pretty-format, meaning snapshots of React components now work like they should.

Due to all the changes, there might be regressions that snuck in. Please report them!

Full list of changes below

Features

  • [babel-jest] Support collecting coverage from .mts, .cts (and other) files (#15994)
  • [jest-circus, jest-cli, jest-config, jest-core, jest-jasmine2, jest-types] Add --collect-tests flag to discover and list tests without executing them (#16006)
  • [jest-config, jest-runner, jest-worker] Add workerGracefulExitTimeout config option to control how long workers are given to exit before being force-killed (#15984)
  • [jest-config] Add support for jest.config.mts as a valid configuration file (#16005)
  • [jest-config, jest-core, jest-reporters, jest-runner] verbose and silent can now be set per-project; the project-level value overrides the global value for that project's tests (#16133)
  • [@jest/fake-timers] Accept Temporal.Duration in jest.advanceTimersByTime() and jest.advanceTimersByTimeAsync() (#16128)
  • [@jest/fake-timers] Accept Temporal.Instant and Temporal.ZonedDateTime in jest.setSystemTime() and useFakeTimers({now}) (#16128)
  • [@jest/fake-timers] Support faking Temporal.Now.* (#16131)
  • [jest-mock] Add clearMocksOnScope(scope) on ModuleMocker for clearing every mock function exposed on a scope object (#16088)
  • [jest-resolve] Add canResolveSync() on Resolver so callers can detect when a user-configured resolver only exports an async hook (#16064)
  • [jest-runtime] Use synchronous evaluate() for ES modules without top-level await on Node versions that support it (v24.9+), and prefer the synchronous transform path when a sync transformer is configured (#16062)
  • [jest-runtime] Support require() of ES modules on Node v24.9+ (#16074)
  • [jest-runtime] Validate TC39 import attributes (with { type: 'json' }) on ESM imports (#16127)
  • [@jest/transform] Add canTransformSync(filename) on ScriptTransformer so callers can pick the sync vs async transform path (#16062)
  • [jest-util] Add isError helper (#16076)

... (truncated)

  • [jest-config] Add support for jest.config.mts as a valid configuration file (#16005)
  • [jest-config, jest-core, jest-reporters, jest-runner] verbose and silent can now be set per-project; the project-level value overrides the global value for that project's tests (#16133)
  • [@jest/fake-timers] Accept Temporal.Duration in jest.advanceTimersByTime() and jest.advanceTimersByTimeAsync() (#16128)
  • [@jest/fake-timers] Accept Temporal.Instant and Temporal.ZonedDateTime in jest.setSystemTime() and useFakeTimers({now}) (#16128)
  • [@jest/fake-timers] Support faking Temporal.Now.* (#16131)
  • [jest-mock] Add clearMocksOnScope(scope) on ModuleMocker for clearing every mock function exposed on a scope object (#16088)
  • [jest-resolve] Add canResolveSync() on Resolver so callers can detect when a user-configured resolver only exports an async hook (#16064)
  • [jest-runtime] Use synchronous evaluate() for ES modules without top-level await on Node versions that support it (v24.9+), and prefer the synchronous transform path when a sync transformer is configured (#16062)
  • [jest-runtime] Support require() of ES modules on Node v24.9+ (#16074)

  • [jest-util] Add isError helper (#16076)
  • [pretty-format] Support React 19 (#16123)

Fixes

  • [expect-utils] Fix toStrictEqual failing on structuredClone results due to cross-realm constructor mismatch (#15959)
  • [@jest/expect-utils] Prevent toMatchObject/subset matching from throwing when encountering exotic iterables (#15952)
  • [fake-timers] Convert Date to milliseconds before passing to @sinonjs/fake-timers (#16029)

issue.title: chore(deps): Bump @microsoft/applicationinsights-web from 3.3.11 to 3.4.1 in /apps/web

labels.name: dependencies
labels.description: Pull requests that update a dependency file

issue.body:
Bumps [@microsoft/applicationinsights-web](https://github.com/microsoft/ApplicationInsights-JS) from 3.3.11 to 3.4.1.
Release notes

Sourced from @​microsoft/applicationinsights-web's releases.

3.4.1

This is the first full supported release of the 3.4.x version line. While a 3.4.0-beta was previously released for early testing and validation, version 3.4.0 was not released as a standard supported version — 3.4.1 is the first production-ready release in this series. The @microsoft/1ds-post-js channel is numbered 4.4.1 and requires v3.4.1.

Significant Changes (since 3.3.11)

The following are the significant changes since the previous full release (3.3.11). Some of these changes were previously included in the 3.4.0-beta release.

  • W3C Trace State Support: Added full support for managing W3C Trace State and sending headers in distributed tracing, including new distributed tracing modes AI_AND_W3C_TRACE and W3C_TRACE that enable the tracestate header to be sent with requests when trace state information is available, the existing states will continue to not send the header.

  • New Distributed Tracing Modes: Added new eDistributedTracingModes enum values:

    • AI_AND_W3C_TRACE (17): Sends Application Insights headers + W3C traceparent + W3C tracestate headers (if state value is present)
    • W3C_TRACE (18): Sends only W3C traceparent + W3C tracestate headers (if state value is present)

  • Enhanced Distributed Tracing: Refactored the distributed tracing implementation to provide better support for the W3C Trace Context specification and prepare for future OpenTelemetry Span-style API integration.

  • New W3C TraceState API: Introduced the IW3cTraceState interface that provides a mutable, ordered list of key/value pairs for trace state information with proper parent-child relationships.

  • OpenTelemetry Integration Preparation: Added foundational OpenTelemetry interfaces (IOTelSpanContext, IOTelTraceState) to provide OpenTelemetry API compatibility.

  • Additional Configuration: Added new configuration properties for W3C trace state support:

    • traceHdrMode: Controls if the SDK should look for the traceparent and/or tracestate values from service timing headers or meta tags from the initial page load (in IConfiguration)
    • Enhanced distributedTracingMode property to support the new W3C trace state modes (in ICorrelationConfig)

  • Dependencies Extension: The dependency tracking extension now includes additional logic for W3C trace state handling, which may affect custom dependency listeners or initializers. The following interfaces and functions have been enhanced with W3C trace state support:

    • IDependencyListenerDetails interface now also includes a readonly traceState along with the previous traceId, spanId, traceFlags properties
    • addDependencyListener() function now provides access to W3C trace state information through the enhanced details object
    • addDependencyInitializer() function continues to work with existing dependency telemetry processing
    • Custom dependency listeners can now access and modify W3C trace state information before requests are sent

  • Enhanced Cookie Management: Cookie values are now cached in memory when cookies are disabled instead of being lost, enabling support for consent banner workflows where cookies must be temporarily disabled until user approval. Automatic flushing occurs when cookies are re-enabled.

  • OsPlugin Reliability Improvements: Improved OsPlugin with proactive OS retrieval, unload handling, and session caching for more reliable OS detection.

  • URL Redaction Enhancements: Made URL redaction more dynamic for improved flexibility in field redaction scenarios.

Package Deprecation

The following packages have been merged into @microsoft/applicationinsights-core-js and are now deprecated. They continue to be published as backward-compatible shims (re-exporting from Core) so existing code will not break, but they are no longer used as dependencies by the main SDK packages. You should stop importing from these packages and migrate to @microsoft/applicationinsights-core-js directly.

  • @microsoft/applicationinsights-common — All exports have been merged into @microsoft/applicationinsights-core-js. The package is now a compatibility shim that re-exports from Core. See the Migration Guide for details on updating your imports. This package will be removed in a future major release (4.0.0).

  • @microsoft/1ds-core-js — All exports have been merged into @microsoft/applicationinsights-core-js. The package is now a compatibility shim that re-exports from Core. See the 1DS Core Migration Guide for class/import name changes and migration steps. Consumers should update their imports to reference @microsoft/applicationinsights-core-js directly. issue.body:
Bumps [@playwright/test](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright) from 1.58.2 to 1.60.0.
Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.60.0

🌐 HAR recording on Tracing

tracing.startHar() / tracing.stopHar() expose HAR recording as a first-class tracing API, with the same content, mode and urlFilter options as recordHar. The returned Disposable makes it easy to scope a recording with await using:

await using har = await context.tracing.startHar('trace.har');
const page = await context.newPage();
await page.goto('https://playwright.dev');
// HAR is finalized when `har` goes out of scope.

🪝 Drop API

New locator.drop() simulates an external drag-and-drop of files or clipboard-like data onto an element. Playwright dispatches dragenter, dragover, and drop with a synthetic [DataTransfer] in the page context — works cross-browser and is great for testing upload zones:

await page.locator('#dropzone').drop({
  files: { name: 'note.txt', mimeType: 'text/plain', buffer: Buffer.from('hello') },
});

await page.locator('#dropzone').drop({
data: {
'text/plain': 'hello world',
'text/uri-list': 'https://example.com',
},
});

🎯 Aria snapshots

  • expect(page).toMatchAriaSnapshot() now works on a Page, in addition to a Locator — equivalent to asserting against page.locator('body').
  • New boxes option on locator.ariaSnapshot() / page.ariaSnapshot() appends each element's bounding box as [box=x,y,width,height], useful for AI consumption.

🛑 test.abort()

New test.abort() aborts the currently running test from a fixture, hook, or route handler with an optional message. Use it when you have detected an unrecoverable misuse and want to fail the test right away:

test('does not publish to the shared page', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.route('**/publish', route => {
    test.abort('Tests must not publish to the shared page. Use the `clone` option.');
    return route.abort();
  });
  // ...
});

Bumps [@playwright/test](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright) from 1.58.2 to 1.60.0.
Release notes

Sourced from @​playwright/test's releases.

v1.60.0

🌐 HAR recording on Tracing

tracing.startHar() / tracing.stopHar() expose HAR recording as a first-class tracing API, with the same content, mode and urlFilter options as recordHar. The returned Disposable makes it easy to scope a recording with await using:

await using har = await context.tracing.startHar('trace.har');
const page = await context.newPage();
await page.goto('https://playwright.dev');
// HAR is finalized when `har` goes out of scope.

🪝 Drop API

New locator.drop() simulates an external drag-and-drop of files or clipboard-like data onto an element. Playwright dispatches dragenter, dragover, and drop with a synthetic [DataTransfer] in the page context — works cross-browser and is great for testing upload zones:

await page.locator('#dropzone').drop({
  files: { name: 'note.txt', mimeType: 'text/plain', buffer: Buffer.from('hello') },
});

await page.locator('#dropzone').drop({
data: {
'text/plain': 'hello world',
'text/uri-list': 'https://example.com',
},
});

🎯 Aria snapshots

  • expect(page).toMatchAriaSnapshot() now works on a Page, in addition to a Locator — equivalent to asserting against page.locator('body').
  • New boxes option on locator.ariaSnapshot() / page.ariaSnapshot() appends each element's bounding box as [box=x,y,width,height], useful for AI consumption.

🛑 test.abort()

New test.abort() aborts the currently running test from a fixture, hook, or route handler with an optional message. Use it when you have detected an unrecoverable misuse and want to fail the test right away:

test('does not publish to the shared page', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.route('**/publish', route => {
    test.abort('Tests must not publish to the shared page. Use the `clone` option.');
    return route.abort();
  });
  // ...
});

issue.title: Update OIDC bootstrap for enterprise-scoped GitHub issuer
issue.body:
GitHub Actions authentication is failing with `AADSTS700211` because the enterprise-level GitHub OIDC issuer policy changed the token issuer from the default `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com` to an enterprise-scoped issuer such as `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com/ibuyspy`.

Update the bootstrap/generation scripts and any workflow templates that create or reference Entra federated identity credentials so they use the correct issuer for this enterprise setting.

### Requirements
- Detect whether the enterprise OIDC custom issuer policy is enabled.
- Use the matching issuer when creating federated credentials.
- Fix any subject formatting bugs in generated credentials.
- Keep `audience` set to `api://AzureADTokenExchange` unless a repo has a specific exception.
- Update docs/templates so generated examples match the runtime behavior.

### Notes
- Entra federated credentials must match issuer/subject/audience exactly.
- If the enterprise setting is enabled but the credential still uses the old issuer, token exchange will fail.
- If the enterprise setting is disabled but the credential uses the enterprise-scoped issuer, token exchange will also fail.

issue.title: Migrate web auth email flow from Nodemailer to Azure Communication Services
issue.body:
Replaced the web app’s Nodemailer-based Auth.js email flow with Azure Communication Services (ACS) Email, and aligned runtime/config/IaC so email auth can be deployed and operated via ACS end-to-end.

- **Auth provider migration (Nodemailer ➜ ACS)**
  - Added `apps/web/src/lib/email.ts` as an ACS email wrapper for Auth.js verification emails.
  - Switched `apps/web/src/auth.ts` email provider wiring to use the ACS-backed provider config.
  - Removed direct Nodemailer provider usage from auth flow.

- **Runtime config + package changes**
  - Updated `apps/web/src/lib/runtime-config.ts` email provider availability checks to ACS env pairs:
    - `ACS_EMAIL_CONNECTION_STRING` + `ACS_EMAIL_SENDER_ADDRESS`
    - `AUTH_ACS_EMAIL_CONNECTION_STRING` + `AUTH_ACS_EMAIL_SENDER_ADDRESS`
  - Added `@azure/communication-email` and removed `nodemailer` in `apps/web/package.json` (lockfile updated).

- **Config/documentation updates**
  - Updated `apps/web/.env.example` to ACS email variables and aliases.
  - Updated root `README.md` production auth provider examples to ACS email config.

- **Deployment guardrails + release checks**
  - Updated workflow auth provider validation logic to treat ACS env pairs as the email provider signal:
    - `.github/workflows/deploy-api.yml`
    - `.github/workflows/deploy-web.yml`
    - `.github/workflows/release-preflight.yml`
    - `.github/workflows/release-postcheck.yml`

- **IaC: ACS provisioning + app wiring**
  - Added `iac/communications/email-service.bicep` to provision:
    - `Microsoft.Communication/communicationServices`
    - `Microsoft.Communication/emailServices`
    - Azure-managed email domain + domain linkage
  - Updated `iac/main.bicep` to deploy ACS resources, seed ACS Key Vault secrets, and expose communication service output.
  - Updated `iac/backend/container-app.bicep` to inject ACS connection/sender secrets as runtime env for auth email.

- **Targeted email behavior coverage**
  - Added `apps/web/src/__tests__/email.test.ts` covering:
    - missing ACS config behavior
    - successful ACS verification send path via mocked `EmailClient`

```ts
// apps/web/src/lib/email.ts
const poller = await emailClient.beginSend({
  senderAddress: settings.senderAddress,
  recipients: { to: [{ address: identifier }] },
  content,
});
const response = await poller.pollUntilDone();
if (!response || response.status !== 'Succeeded') {
  throw new Error(`ACS email send failed with status: ${response?.status ?? 'Unknown'}`);
}
```

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #23.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/23
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 03/22/2026 23:41:15
Original updated: 03/25/2026 06:36:54

---

## Summary
The app currently has no telemetry or analytics instrumentation. We need to add observability to track usage, performance, and errors across both the mobile (Expo) and web (Next.js) apps.

## Scope
- **Error tracking** ΓÇö capture and report unhandled exceptions and API errors
- **Usage analytics** ΓÇö track key user actions (walks started/completed, pets added, team invites)
- **Performance monitoring** ΓÇö page load times (web), screen render times (mobile), API latency
- **Session tracking** ΓÇö active users, session duration, retention

## Considerations
- Evaluate providers: Sentry (errors), PostHog or Mixpanel (product analytics), OpenTelemetry (traces)
- Must respect user privacy ΓÇö include opt-out mechanism in Settings
- Shared telemetry utilities should live in a new `packages/telemetry` workspace package
- Mobile and web may need platform-specific adapters

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Error tracking integrated in both mobile and web apps
- [ ] Key user events are tracked
- [ ] Performance metrics are collected
- [ ] Privacy opt-out toggle in Settings screen
- [ ] Telemetry package added to `packages/`

issue.body:

Original updated: 03/25/2026 06:36:54

---

## Summary
Create a comprehensive sample data pack that populates the app with realistic test data across all entities. This makes it easy for developers and testers to exercise the full UI without manual data entry.

## Data to Include
- **Users** ΓÇö 3-5 users with different roles (owner, caretaker, walker, sitter)
- **Pets** ΓÇö 6-8 pets across species (dogs, cats, bird, custom types) with avatars, medical notes, microchip IDs
- **Walks** ΓÇö 15-20 walks in various statuses (planned, active, completed) with routes, events (pee, poop, photo, note), durations, distances
- **Teams** ΓÇö 1-2 teams with members and varied permissions
- **Reminders** ΓÇö Pre-configured reminders (bag, food, water, medication, vet, grooming) across pets
- **Walk Events** ΓÇö Realistic event timelines within walks

## Requirements

- [ ] All entity types are populated with realistic data

issue.title: Feature: Secure blob upload service

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #36.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/36
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 03/23/2026 01:05:37
Original updated: 03/25/2026 06:47:21

---

## Summary
Build a secure, production-grade blob upload service for photos, documents, and media across the app (pet photos, walk photos, walker profile pictures). The existing `POST /api/v1/upload` endpoint stores files locally ΓÇö this needs to be hardened and extended.

## Scope

### Storage Backend
- Abstract storage behind a provider interface (local disk for dev, Azure Blob / S3 for production)
- Configurable via environment variables (`STORAGE_PROVIDER`, `STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING`, `STORAGE_CONTAINER`)
- Organize blobs by type: `pets/`, `walks/`, `profiles/`, `misc/`

### Upload Security
- **File type validation** ΓÇö allowlist of MIME types (image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp, image/heic, application/pdf)
- **File size limits** ΓÇö configurable max size (default 10MB for images, 25MB for documents)
- **Virus/malware scanning** ΓÇö integration point for ClamAV or cloud-based scanning
- **Filename sanitization** ΓÇö strip special characters, generate UUIDs for stored filenames
- **Content-Type verification** ΓÇö validate magic bytes match declared MIME type, not just file extension

### Access Control
- **Signed URLs** ΓÇö generate time-limited signed URLs for blob access (default 1 hour expiry)
- **Auth-gated downloads** ΓÇö require valid session to access `/api/v1/files/[id]` endpoint
- **Ownership validation** ΓÇö users can only access blobs attached to their own pets/walks/team
- **Rate limiting** ΓÇö throttle uploads per user (e.g. 20 uploads/hour)

### API Endpoints
- `POST /api/v1/upload` ΓÇö upload a file (multipart/form-data), returns blob metadata
- `GET /api/v1/files/[id]` ΓÇö download/stream a file (auth-gated, signed URL redirect for cloud storage)
- `DELETE /api/v1/files/[id]` ΓÇö delete a file (ownership check)
- `GET /api/v1/files` ΓÇö list files for current user (optional filter by type/entity)

### Database
- Add `blobs` table: id, userId, entityType (pet/walk/profile), entityId, filename, mimeType, sizeBytes, storageKey, createdAt
- Foreign key relationships to pets, walks, users

### Mobile & Web Integration
- Image compression/resizing before upload on mobile (Expo ImageManipulator)
- Upload progress indicator in UI
- Thumbnail generation (server-side or on-upload)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Storage provider abstraction with local and cloud implementations
- [ ] File type and size validation on upload
- [ ] Content-Type magic byte verification
- [ ] Filename sanitization with UUID storage keys
- [ ] Auth-gated file access with ownership checks
- [ ] Signed URL generation for cloud storage
- [ ] Upload rate limiting
- [ ] Blobs table in database schema
- [ ] Mobile upload with compression and progress
- [ ] Delete endpoint with ownership validation

## Summary
Create GitHub Actions workflows to package the WawkR mobile app (Expo/React Native) and deploy to the Apple App Store and Google Play Store.

## Workflows

### 1. Build & Package (on tag or manual dispatch)
- Trigger on version tags (`v*.*.*`) or `workflow_dispatch`
- Run `eas build --platform ios` for iOS (.ipa)
- Run `eas build --platform android` for Android (.aab)
- Upload build artifacts to GitHub release
- Notify team on build success/failure (Slack, email, or GitHub comment)

### 2. Submit to App Stores
- Trigger manually or on successful build workflow
- **iOS**: `eas submit --platform ios` to App Store Connect (TestFlight for staging, production release for tags)
- **Android**: `eas submit --platform android` to Google Play Console (internal track for staging, production for tags)
- Support staged rollouts (e.g. 10% ΓåÆ 50% ΓåÆ 100%)

### 3. OTA Updates (non-native changes)
- Trigger on push to `master` when only JS/TS files change
- Run `eas update` to push over-the-air updates
- Channel management: `preview` for staging, `production` for live
- Skip OTA if native code changed (auto-detect via `npx expo-updates` fingerprint)

## Secrets & Configuration
- `EXPO_TOKEN` ΓÇö EAS authentication
- `APPLE_ID`, `ASC_KEY_ID`, `ASC_ISSUER_ID`, `ASC_KEY_P8` ΓÇö App Store Connect API key
- `GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY` ΓÇö Google Play service account JSON
- `KEYSTORE_BASE64`, `KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `KEY_ALIAS`, `KEY_PASSWORD` ΓÇö Android signing
- Store all in GitHub Secrets, reference in workflow

## Versioning
- Bump `app.json` version and build number in a pre-release script
- Follow semver: major.minor.patch
- Auto-generate changelog from conventional commits since last tag

## App Store Metadata
- Screenshots generated from UI spec mockups or automated via Detox/Maestro
- Store listing copy (description, keywords, categories) managed in `fastlane/metadata/` or `store/` folder
- Privacy policy and terms URLs configured

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] EAS Build workflow produces iOS and Android binaries on tag push
- [ ] Build artifacts attached to GitHub releases
- [ ] App Store submission workflow deploys to TestFlight and Play internal track
- [ ] OTA update workflow pushes JS-only changes without full rebuild
- [ ] All signing keys and credentials stored securely in GitHub Secrets
- [ ] Version bumping and changelog generation automated
- [ ] README documents the release process

## Summary
Extend the existing Pulse/Midnight theme system into a full skinning engine with multiple visual themes users can select. Each skin defines a complete color palette, typography feel, and optional decorative touches.

## Skins

### 1. 16-Bit
- Retro pixel-art inspired aesthetic
- Saturated, limited color palette (greens, magentas, cyans)
- Pixelated borders/accents, monospace or pixel font option
- Nostalgic CRT-style subtle scan-line overlay (optional)

### 2. Palm Beach
- Warm, tropical, relaxed vibe
- Coral, turquoise, sandy beige, palm green
- Light background with warm accent colors
- Soft rounded shapes, breezy feel

### 3. Forest
- Earthy, nature-inspired
- Deep greens, mossy tones, bark browns, warm amber
- Dark background with organic accent colors
- Muted, calming palette

### 4. Dark Mode
- Clean, modern dark theme
- Neutral grays and blues, high contrast text
- Distinct from Pulse/Midnight ΓÇö more conventional dark mode
- Follows system preference by default

### 5. Light Mode
- Clean, bright light theme
- White/light gray surfaces, dark text
- Accessible contrast ratios throughout
- Follows system preference by default

## Architecture

### Design Tokens (`packages/tokens`)
- Extend token package with a `skins/` directory
- Each skin exports a complete MD3-compatible token set (surface, primary, secondary, error, etc.)
- Tokens consumed by both web (CSS variables / Tailwind config) and mobile (React Native StyleSheet)

### Skin Definition Interface
\\\	ypescript
interface Skin {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  description: string;
  preview: string; // thumbnail URL
  tokens: MD3ColorTokens;
  typography?: { fontFamily?: string; monoFamily?: string; };
  effects?: { scanlines?: boolean; pixelBorders?: boolean; };
  isDark: boolean;
}
\\\`n
### Settings Integration
- Add skin selector to Settings page (web + mobile)
- Show skin preview thumbnails in a grid
- Persist selection to `userSettings.theme` (extend from pulse/midnight to skin IDs)
- System preference detection for dark/light auto-switching

### Runtime Theme Provider
- Web: CSS custom properties updated at root, Tailwind `darkMode: 'class'` strategy
- Mobile: React context provider that maps tokens to StyleSheet values
- Smooth transition when switching skins

### UI Spec Mockups
- Create skin preview cards for the settings screen
- Optional: create one sample screen (e.g. Home) per skin for the design spec

## Migration
- Pulse and Midnight become skins within the new system (backwards compatible)
- Existing `theme: 'pulse' | 'midnight'` setting maps to skin IDs

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Skin definition interface and token structure in `packages/tokens`
- [ ] 5 new skins implemented (16-bit, Palm Beach, Forest, Dark, Light)
- [ ] Pulse and Midnight migrated into the skin system
- [ ] Skin selector in Settings (web + mobile) with preview thumbnails
- [ ] Runtime theme switching without page reload
- [ ] System preference auto-detection for dark/light
- [ ] At least one UI spec mockup per new skin

issue.title: Security: Harden IaC ΓÇö Key Vault, RBAC, private networking, and config management
issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #40.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/40
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 03/23/2026 02:06:28
Original updated: 03/25/2026 06:47:11

---

## Summary
Security audit of `iac/` revealed critical gaps: plaintext secrets, missing Key Vault, no RBAC assignments, public ingress, and missing resources. All connection strings and configs must be passed as service connections or environment variables sourced from Key Vault ΓÇö never hardcoded.

## ≡ƒö┤ Critical Fixes

### 1. Remove plaintext secrets from container-app.bicep
- Cosmos DB endpoint and database name are stored as inline secret values
- **Fix:** Replace with Key Vault references using `keyVaultUrl` syntax
- All connection strings must come from Key Vault or App Configuration service connections

### 2. Secure the GitHub token in static-web-app.bicep
- `repositoryToken` param is missing `@secure()` decorator
- Visible in deployment logs and ARM outputs
- **Fix:** Add `@secure()` decorator, source from Key Vault

### 3. Remove deployment token output from static-web-app.bicep
- `output deploymentToken` exposes the SWA API key in deployment outputs
- **Fix:** Remove output, store in Key Vault instead

## ≡ƒƒá Security Gaps

### 4. Create Key Vault module (`iac/security/keyvault.bicep`)
- `parameters.bicep` defines `keyVaultName` but no module exists
- Key Vault with RBAC access model (no access policies)
- Private endpoint on the privatelink subnet
- Network ACL denying public access
- Store all secrets: Cosmos endpoint, GitHub token, SWA deploy token, future API keys
- All app config must reference Key Vault secrets, never inline values

### 5. Create RBAC role assignments (`iac/identity/role-assignments.bicep`)
- Managed identity exists but has no role assignments
- Cosmos DB reader role is defined but never assigned
- **Assign:** `Cosmos DB Built-in Data Contributor` to API managed identity
- **Assign:** `Key Vault Secrets User` to API managed identity
- **Assign:** `AcrPull` when ACR is added
- **Assign:** `Storage Blob Data Contributor` when Storage is added

### 6. Make Container App Environment internal
- Currently `internal: false` ΓÇö public access to ingress
- `allowInsecure: true` permits non-TLS traffic
- **Fix:** Set `internal: true`, set `allowInsecure: false`
- Route public traffic through Front Door or Application Gateway

### 7. Create private DNS zone resource (`iac/networking/private-dns.bicep`)
- `private-endpoint.bicep` references a DNS zone by ID but never creates it
- Deployment will fail if the zone doesn't exist
- Create DNS zone and VNet link

## ≡ƒƒí Missing Resources

### 8. Azure Container Registry (`iac/backend/acr.bicep`)
- No ACR for hosting app container images
- Premium SKU (required for private link)
- Private endpoint, admin user disabled, public network access disabled
- Managed identity pulls via AcrPull role

### 9. Front Door or Application Gateway (`iac/networking/front-door.bicep`)
- No ingress gateway ΓÇö API is either fully public or fully internal
- WAF policy for OWASP protection
- SSL termination, rate limiting
- Route to internal Container App Environment

### 10. Storage Account (`iac/data/storage.bicep`)
- Needed for blob uploads (issue #36)
- Private endpoint, RBAC access, firewall rules
- Connection via managed identity, not access keys

### 11. Log Analytics & monitoring (`iac/monitoring/log-analytics.bicep`)
- No diagnostics, Log Analytics, or Application Insights
- Required for telemetry (issue #23)
- Diagnostic settings on all resources

### 12. Main orchestrator (`iac/main.bicep`)
- No top-level file wiring modules together
- Create `main.bicep` composing all modules with parameter flow and dependencies
- Environment variables and service connections flow from Key Vault through main.bicep to consuming modules

## Config Management Principles
- **No secrets in Bicep params or outputs** ΓÇö always Key Vault
- **Connection strings as env vars** ΓÇö sourced from Key Vault references or App Configuration
- **Service connections** ΓÇö use managed identity + RBAC, never access keys
- **@secure() on all sensitive params** ΓÇö prevents logging
- **No public endpoints on data services** ΓÇö private link only

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All secrets stored in and sourced from Key Vault
- [ ] `@secure()` on all sensitive parameters
- [ ] No secrets in deployment outputs
- [ ] RBAC role assignments for all service-to-service auth
- [ ] Container App Environment set to internal
- [ ] Front Door or App Gateway for public ingress with WAF
- [ ] Private endpoints on Cosmos DB, Key Vault, ACR, Storage
- [ ] Private DNS zones created and linked to VNet
- [ ] ACR, Storage Account, and Log Analytics modules added
- [ ] `main.bicep` orchestrates all modules
- [ ] All connection strings passed as env vars from Key Vault

issue.title: bug: AUTH_SECRET not provisioned in IaC or bootstrap (NEXTAUTH_SECRET name mismatch)
issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #90.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/90
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/18/2026 10:09:30
Original updated: 05/19/2026 06:03:52

---

## Bug Description
\AUTH_SECRET\ (Auth.js v5 required env var) is never provisioned end-to-end:

1. **Variable name mismatch**: \scripts/bootstrap.sh\ and \scripts/bootstrap.ps1\ generate \NEXTAUTH_SECRET\ (Auth.js v4 name). Auth.js v5 requires \AUTH_SECRET\. Local dev environments set the wrong variable.

2. **IaC gap**: \iac/backend/container-app.bicep\ wires \cosmos-endpoint\ and \cosmos-database\ from Key Vault but never adds \^Guth-secret\. \AUTH_SECRET\ is never set as a Container App environment variable via IaC.

3. **No Key Vault provisioning**: Bootstrap scripts only write to \.env.local\. There is no step that provisions \^Guth-secret\ into Azure Key Vault for production deployments.

## Impact
- Local dev: Auth.js session signing fails silently or uses wrong variable
- Production: Container App starts without \AUTH_SECRET\ ΓåÆ \/api/auth/*\ returns 500 ΓåÆ all auth broken

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] \container-app.bicep\ references \^Guth-secret\ from Key Vault and sets \AUTH_SECRET\ env var
- [ ] \ ootstrap.sh\/\ ootstrap.ps1\ generate \AUTH_SECRET\ (not \NEXTAUTH_SECRET\) for local dev
- [ ] Bootstrap scripts provision \^Guth-secret\ to Key Vault when \--provision-azure\ flag / \AZ_KV_NAME\ env var is set
- [ ] \^Gpps/web/.env.example\ documents \AUTH_SECRET\
- [ ] Bicep validates clean; Next.js build passes

issue.title: security: remove AUTH_SECRET deployment fallback and enforce Key Vault + MI
issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #101.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/101
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 06:00:32
Original updated: 05/19/2026 07:10:18

---

## Problem
Current IaC/deploy path includes a fallback where `AUTH_SECRET` can be passed from GitHub secret into deployment parameters. This keeps deployments unblocked, but it is not the desired long-term security model.

## Why this matters
- RBAC controls **who can access** resources, not the secret value itself.
- `AUTH_SECRET` is still required as an app signing key value.
- Preferred model is: Key Vault stores secret, Container App reads via managed identity, no deployment-time secret fallback.

## Requested change
1. Remove deployment-time `authSecret` fallback parameter from IaC/workflows.
2. Enforce Key Vault-only `auth-secret` reference in Container App config.
3. Add bootstrap/preflight check to ensure `auth-secret` exists in Key Vault before deploy.
4. Fail deploy with clear message if MI/KV access is missing.
5. Document the RBAC + Key Vault provisioning path.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `iac/main.bicep` and `backend/container-app.bicep` no longer accept raw `authSecret` parameter
- [ ] `.github/workflows/deploy-iac.yml` no longer passes `secrets.AUTH_SECRET` into template params
- [ ] Deploy succeeds when KV secret + MI permissions are present
- [ ] Deploy fails fast with actionable error when KV secret is missing
- [ ] Docs updated with required RBAC roles and KV secret setup

issue.title: design(auth): tenant ID should come from App Configuration, not IaC params ΓÇö support single/multi-tenant

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #116.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/116
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 14:06:11
Original updated: 05/19/2026 18:31:20

---

## Problem

The OIDC issuer tenant ID is currently passed as an IaC parameter (\	enantId\) and baked into the container app env var (\AZURE_TENANT_ID\). This is wrong ΓÇö tenant configuration is a runtime concern, not an infrastructure concern.

## Expected

Tenant ID (and issuer URLs) should be stored in **App Configuration** so they can be changed without redeployment. This also enables:
- **Single-tenant mode**: issuer locked to one tenant ID
- **Multi-tenant mode**: issuer set to \common\ with dynamic issuer validation
- Runtime switching between modes via feature flag

## Design Considerations

1. App Configuration settings:
   - \^Guth:tenant-mode\ ΓåÆ \single\ | \multi\
   - \^Guth:tenant-id\ ΓåÆ specific tenant ID (for single-tenant)
   - \^Guth:org-issuer\ ΓåÆ computed from mode + tenant-id
   - \^Guth:personal-issuer\ ΓåÆ \consumers/v2.0\ (always)

2. Multi-tenant requires custom issuer validation in Auth.js callback (compare token issuer against allowed tenants list)

3. Feature flag: \^Guth.multi-tenant\ to toggle between modes

4. Remove \	enantId\ from IaC params once App Config handles it

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Design doc: single vs multi-tenant auth architecture
- [ ] App Configuration settings for tenant mode
- [ ] Auth.ts reads issuer from App Config at startup (with env var fallback)
- [ ] Feature flag gates multi-tenant behavior
- [ ] Remove \	enantId\ IaC param once migration complete

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #117.

Original state: CLOSED

Original updated: 05/19/2026 17:15:36

---

## Problem

No local authentication option exists. Users who want to run WawkR self-hosted or in development without OAuth provider setup have no way to sign in.

## Expected

A local credentials-based auth provider (username/password) that can be enabled via feature flag for:
- Local development without OAuth setup
- Self-hosted deployments without cloud identity providers
- Demo/staging environments

## Design

1. **Provider**: Auth.js Credentials provider with bcrypt-hashed passwords
2. **Storage**: Users table with \passwordHash\ column (nullable ΓÇö only set for local auth users)
3. **Gating**: Feature flag \^Guth.local-credentials\ (disabled in production by default)
4. **Registration**: Simple signup form when local auth is enabled
5. **Security**:
   - Rate limiting on login attempts
   - Password complexity requirements
   - Account lockout after N failed attempts
   - Feature flag MUST be explicitly enabled (never auto-enabled in prod)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Credentials provider added to \^Guth.ts\ (conditional on feature flag)
- [ ] User registration endpoint (\/api/auth/register\)
- [ ] Password hashing with bcrypt (cost factor 12+)
- [ ] Login rate limiting (max 5 attempts per minute)
- [ ] Feature flag \^Guth.local-credentials\ in App Configuration (default: false)
- [ ] Works in dev without any external provider configured
- [ ] Disabled by default in production

EACCES: permission denied, open '/app/apps/web/public/uploads/demo-avatar-demo-user-marcus.jpg'
``

## Root Cause
`blob-storage.ts` falls back to writing to `public/uploads/` when `AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING` is not set. In the container, the filesystem is read-only.

## Fix
Provision Azure Blob Storage account via IaC and set `AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING` on the container app.

type.name: Feature

issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #120.

Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 15:07:57
Original updated: 05/19/2026 17:16:10

---

## Context
WawkR needs a public landing page (marketing, features, pricing) separate from the authenticated app. Two options evaluated:

## Decision: Subdomain `app.wawkr.tld` (recommended)

### Rationale
1. **Security isolation** ΓÇö auth cookies scoped to `app.` subdomain, landing page has zero attack surface
2. **Independent deploys** ΓÇö marketing ships without touching app pipeline
3. **Simpler Next.js** ΓÇö no `basePath: '/app'` which complicates assets, images, auth callbacks
4. **Front Door routing** ΓÇö already have `wawkr-fd-dev`; add second origin group for landing
5. **Mobile deep links** ΓÇö `app.wawkr.tld/walks/123` maps cleanly

### Implementation Plan
- [ ] Landing page: Static site (Astro or Next.js export) on Azure Static Web Apps
- [ ] DNS: `wawkr.tld` ΓåÆ Static Web App, `app.wawkr.tld` ΓåÆ Container App (via Front Door)
- [ ] Update AUTH_URL to `https://app.wawkr.tld`
- [ ] Update Entra ID app registration redirect URIs
- [ ] Front Door: two endpoint/origin groups (landing + app)
- [ ] Landing page content: hero, features, screenshots, CTA ΓåÆ sign in

### Alternative Considered
Subpath `/app/` ΓÇö rejected due to coupled deploys, basePath complexity, shared cookie scope.

issue.title: feat(data): Migrate from SQLite to Azure Cosmos DB / Postgres Flexible Server

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #129.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/129
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 19:04:03
Original updated: 05/19/2026 19:34:41

---

## Problem

The web app currently uses SQLite via better-sqlite3 + Drizzle ORM with a local file (wawkr.db). This is fundamentally incompatible with production:

- **Ephemeral filesystem**: Container Apps don't persist file state across restarts/replicas
- **No shared state**: Multiple replicas can't share a SQLite file
- **No backups**: No point-in-time recovery or geo-redundancy

## Current State

- apps/web/src/db/index.ts uses better-sqlite3 with local file
- apps/web/src/db/schema.ts uses Drizzle ORM SQLite dialect (sqliteTable)
- IaC already provisions Cosmos DB (SQL API) with a service connector, but app code never uses it

## Recommendation

**Option B (Postgres Flexible Server)** - Drizzle ORM migration path is clean (sqliteTable to pgTable), and Postgres is the standard relational choice for Next.js apps.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Add Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server to IaC
- [ ] Migrate Drizzle schema from sqliteTable to pgTable
- [ ] Update apps/web/src/db/index.ts to use drizzle-orm/node-postgres
- [ ] Connection string via App Configuration or service connector
- [ ] Seed script works against Postgres
- [ ] All tests pass with Postgres backend
- [ ] Remove better-sqlite3 dependency

issue.title: bug: Front Door DNS RBAC was assigned to wrong zone (pawzo.me instead of pawzum.com)
issue.body:
## Summary
Azure Front Door's system-assigned managed identity (\wawkr-fd-dev\) had \Reader\ role on the old \pawzo.me\ DNS zone instead of \pawzum.com\. This prevented AFD from auto-validating TLS certificates and custom domain ownership for the new domain.

## Root Cause
- During the Pawzum domain migration, the Front Door DNS RBAC was manually bootstrapped pointing to \pawzo.me\
- The \ ront-door-dns-rbac.bicep\ module existed in IaC but was **not wired into \main.bicep\** — the comment said 'handled by bootstrap'
- When the domain was migrated to \pawzum.com\, the RBAC was never updated

## Impact
- AFD could not auto-validate \pawzum.com\ custom domain certificates
- TLS cert provisioning/renewal was broken for all \pawzum.com\ subdomains

## Fix
**Live hotfix (commit \9a62ba9\):**
- Removed \Reader\ from \pawzo.me\ zone (assignment \16753dbc\)
- Granted \Reader\ on \pawzum.com\ zone for FD principal \ d01e495-dee6-40b4-9497-2709c09fbb18\

**IaC fix (commit \9a62ba9\):**
- Added \dnsZoneResourceGroup\ param to \iac/main.bicep\
- Wired \ ront-door-dns-rbac.bicep\ as a cross-RG module scoped to \dnsZoneResourceGroup\
- RBAC is now fully managed by IaC — no more manual bootstrap required

**Workflow fix (commit \^G111469\):**
- Added \dnsZoneResourceGroup\ param to both \what-if\ and \deploy\ steps in \deploy-iac.yml\
- Set \DNS_ZONE_RESOURCE_GROUP=rg-core-services\ GitHub repo variable

## Lesson
Live RBAC grants that are not in IaC will drift on the next deployment. All identity/RBAC assignments must be managed as code.

issue.title: bug: /api/public/auth-providers crashes with 500 when DB unavailable — should read from env vars
issue.body:
## RCA (from App Insights trace)

\GET /api/public/auth-providers\ → \getRuntimeAuthProviderConfig()\ → unconditional DB query → pg.connect fails → 500.

Trace:
- \pg-pool.connect\ span: target \wawkr-pg-dev.postgres.database.azure.com|pawzome\, success=False
- Exception: \PostgreSQL error of type 'Error' occurred (code: UNKNOWN)\
- Query: \select id, auth_provider_toggles from app_config where id = 'global'\

## Root Cause
\getRuntimeAuthProviderConfig()\ in \^Gpps/web/src/lib/runtime-config.ts\ always hits the DB to load admin toggle overrides before computing provider availability. When the DB connection fails (DATABASE_URL secret empty/malformed), the entire function throws — crashing the public auth-providers endpoint that the login page depends on.

The DB row is only needed for **admin-managed overrides**. All provider availability is already expressible via env vars (\AUTH_PROVIDER_LOCAL_ENABLED\, \AUTH_MICROSOFT_ENTRA_ID_ID\, etc.) which are all set on the container app.

## Impact
- Login page cannot load provider list → all login buttons fail to render
- Every sign-in attempt fails with \DatabaseUnavailable\
- Cascades to: Entra sign-in, B2C sign-in, local credentials — all broken

## Fix
Wrap the DB query in try/catch. On failure, use \storedToggles = {}\ (empty) so env-var toggles drive everything. When DB recovers, admin overrides automatically resume.

Fixed in commit referencing this issue.

## Summary

Azure AD B2C is end-of-life and must be replaced with Microsoft Entra External ID (CIAM). The B2C tenant \wawkrid\ was never actually provisioned (IaC gated behind \deployB2CTenant=false\), so this is a greenfield migration.

See **[ADR-001](../docs/adr/ADR-001-entra-external-id-replaces-b2c.md)** for the full architecture decision record.

## Why

- Azure AD B2C is EOL  -  no new features, retirement timeline announced
- Entra External ID is the official successor with native Bicep/ARM support
- Unified with the Entra ecosystem (same Graph API, conditional access, MFA, passwordless)
- Simpler integration: standard OIDC, no custom provider required in NextAuth

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] \iac/identity/external-id-tenant.bicep\ deployed and CIAM tenant active (\pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com\)
- [ ] App registration created in CIAM tenant with correct redirect URIs (\https://app.pawzum.com/api/auth/callback/microsoft-entra-id\)
- [ ] \^Guth.ts\ updated  -  \MicrosoftEntraID\ provider configured with \ciamlogin.com\ issuer
- [ ] \untime-config.ts\ updated  -  provider ID \^Gzure-ad-b2c\ replaced with \^[ntra-external-id\
- [ ] Env vars: \AUTH_EXTERNAL_ID_TENANT\, \AUTH_MICROSOFT_ENTRA_ID_ID\, \AUTH_MICROSOFT_ENTRA_ID_SECRET\ set in Key Vault + container app
- [ ] Old B2C env vars removed from container app + Key Vault
- [ ] Sign-up/sign-in user flow configured (email + social: Google, Apple)
- [ ] Login works end-to-end on \^Gpp.pawzum.com\
- [ ] \.env.example\ updated

## Implementation Waves

### Wave 1  -  IaC: Provision CIAM Tenant
- Use \iac/identity/external-id-tenant.bicep\ (already created)
- Resource: \Microsoft.AzureActiveDirectory/ciamDirectories@2023-01-18-preview\
- **Deployment scope: subscription**  -  use \^Gz deployment sub create\

### Wave 2  -  App Registration
- Create app in CIAM tenant with redirect URIs + scopes
- Store in Key Vault: \^[ntra-external-id-client-id\ / \^[ntra-external-id-client-secret\
- Set GitHub secrets: \ENTRA_EXTERNAL_ID_CLIENT_ID\, \ENTRA_EXTERNAL_ID_CLIENT_SECRET\

### Wave 3  -  Auth Integration
- \^Guth.ts\: configure \MicrosoftEntraID\ with CIAM issuer (\{tenant}.ciamlogin.com\)
- \untime-config.ts\: replace B2C provider definition with \^[ntra-external-id\
- Add \AUTH_EXTERNAL_ID_TENANT\ env var

### Wave 4  -  Cleanup
- Remove \AUTH_B2C_*\ env vars and Key Vault secrets
- Archive \B2C-tenant.bicep\
- Update \.env.example\

## IaC Snippet

\\\icep
// iac/identity/external-id-tenant.bicep
resource externalIdTenant 'Microsoft.AzureActiveDirectory/ciamDirectories@2023-01-18-preview' = {
  name: 'pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com'
  location: 'United States'
  properties: {
    displayName: 'Pawzum Identity'
    domainName: 'pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com'
  }
}
// OIDC Issuer: https://pawzumid.ciamlogin.com/pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com/v2.0
\\\

## Notes

- Tenant creator requires \Tenant Creator\ role in Entra ID (elevated  -  may require manual portal step)
- Verify \pawzumid\ name availability before deployment
- If Graph Bicep extension unavailable, use post-deploy Graph API script for app registration
