issue.title: feat: Azure SRE agent with per-layer alerting, diagnostics, workbook and Copilot runbook agent

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Feature

Add a dedicated Azure SRE agent for the WawkR deployment. This is a separate IaC module (iac/sre/) that targets each infrastructure layer and wires up monitoring, alerting, diagnostic settings, and an AI-assisted incident response agent.

## Why separate

The SRE deployment references existing resources by ID/name rather than creating them. It can be applied independently after the core stack is up, upgraded without touching app infra, and scoped with minimal RBAC (Reader + Monitoring Contributor only).

## Architecture

### IaC module: iac/sre/

sre-main.bicep       -- orchestrator, accepts resource IDs for each layer
alerts.bicep         -- metric alert rules per layer (API, DB, Front Door, Container Apps)
action-group.bicep   -- notification targets (email, webhook, Teams)
diagnostic-settings.bicep -- route resource logs to Log Analytics workspace
workbook.bicep       -- Azure Monitor workbook with per-layer health dashboards

### Layers covered

| Layer | Resource type | Key signals |
|---|---|---|
| Public site | Static Web App | availability, bandwidth errors |
| API | Container App | request latency p95, 5xx rate, CPU/memory, replica count |
| Front Door | AFD | backend health probe failures, WAF blocks, total latency |
| Database | PostgreSQL Flexible | connection failures, CPU, storage, replication lag |
| Blob storage | Storage Account | 4xx/5xx errors, throttling |
| Key Vault | Key Vault | vault unavailable, secret expiry (via policy) |
| Container Apps Env | CAE | resource pressure, provisioning failures |

### Alert severity tiers

- Sev1 (Critical): API 5xx > 5%, DB connection failures, Front Door backend unhealthy
- Sev2 (High): API p95 latency > 2s, container CPU > 85%, Postgres CPU > 80%
- Sev3 (Warning): replica count at min, storage throttling, Key Vault nearing quota

### Copilot SRE agent: .github/agents/sre-agent.agent.md

An agent definition that knows:
- The full resource topology (names, resource groups, subscription)
- Common runbooks (restart container, scale out, failover DB, purge CDN cache)
- How to query Log Analytics for recent errors
- How to read and interpret Application Insights traces
- Escalation paths and on-call rotation contacts

### CI/CD

.github/workflows/deploy-sre.yml:
- Triggered on push to iac/sre/** or manually via workflow_dispatch
- Uses OIDC (no stored secrets)
- Separate from main deploy workflow so SRE config can be updated independently

## Parameters

sre-main.bicep will accept:
- resourceGroupName (where existing resources live)
- apiContainerAppId (resource ID)
- postgresServerId
- frontDoorId
- logAnalyticsWorkspaceId
- appInsightsId
- storageAccountId
- alertEmailAddresses (array)
- webhookUri (optional, for Teams/Slack/PagerDuty)
- environment (dev/staging/prod)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] iac/sre/sre-main.bicep deploys cleanly against a live stack
- [ ] All Sev1 alert rules exist and fire in test (via metric override)
- [ ] Action group routes to at least one email target
- [ ] Diagnostic settings land logs in the existing Log Analytics workspace
- [ ] Azure Monitor Workbook has one tab per layer with key metrics
- [ ] deploy-sre.yml workflow uses OIDC, has unique concurrency group
- [ ] SRE Copilot agent knows all resource names and runbook steps
- [ ] No hardcoded secrets anywhere in the IaC or workflow

`lighthouse-ci.yml` can run alongside the main CI workflow on the same PR, which allows duplicate checks to pile up.

- Matches the existing concurrency guard already used by `ci.yml`

issue.title: suggestion(basecoat): require full-pagination backlog reconciliation

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Suggestion
When reconciling issue backlogs, BaseCoat guidance should require scanning the full open set (paginated) and reporting the total issue count before classification.

## Why
A first-page-only pass can miss older or newer related issues and produce partial reconciliation outcomes.

## Proposed guardrail
- Always query all open issues (not first page only)
- Report OPEN total count in the reconciliation output
- Mark any partial pass as provisional until full-pagination pass completes

## Outcome from this repo
We corrected a 25-issue partial pass to a full 45-issue reconciliation and updated the sprint tracker accordingly.

issue.title: feat: service admin interface with instance management, federation, and white-label SaaS

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Feature

Build a service-level admin interface for managing a Pawzum deployment instance. This sits above the per-tenant admin (/settings/admin) and manages the full platform: users, content, settings, moderation, usage monitoring, and deployment instances.

## Scope

### Core UI sections (/service-admin)
- Dashboard: usage stats, active users, walk counts, storage, error rates
- Users: list all users, edit profiles, reset passwords, assign credits, suspend/ban
- Content: site-wide content overrides, feature flags, i18n strings
- Moderation: flag/remove bad walks, photos, captions, profiles
- Instances: manage deployment instances (regional, private, white-label)
- Analytics: telemetry, event counts, latency, usage over time

### Instance model
- Each deployment is an "instance" (global, regional, or private/white-label)
- Instances have their own domain, branding, user pool, feature flags
- Federation: instances can be linked so users/feeds are shared across boundaries
- Stamping: create a new private instance for a team (dog walkers, family, etc.)

### White-label SaaS
- Private instance = same app, own domain, own branding, own user pool
- Federation allows plugging one instance into another (shared walk feeds, user directory)
- Instance config stored in DB; IaC provisions the deployment separately

### API surface (/api/service-admin/*)
- Users CRUD with elevated bypass of tenant isolation
- Instances CRUD
- Analytics read endpoints
- Moderation actions (delete content, suspend user)
- Federation management (invite/accept/revoke peer)

### Access control
- New role: service-admin (superuser above owner)
- Proxy guards /service-admin/* to service-admin role only
- Separate layout with its own nav

## Schema additions
- instances table: id, name, type (global/regional/private/white-label), domain, ownerUserId, planTier, settings JSON, isActive, createdAt
- instanceMembers table: instanceId, userId, role, joinedAt
- instanceFederation table: instanceId, peerId, status (pending/active/suspended), createdAt

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] /service-admin only accessible to service-admin role
- [ ] User list with search, filter by role, suspend/unsuspend action
- [ ] Instance list with create/edit/delete
- [ ] Federation invite/accept/revoke flow
- [ ] Content override panel (same functionality as tenant admin but global scope)
- [ ] Moderation queue for flagged content
- [ ] Analytics dashboard with key metrics

issue.title: feat: multi-lingual JSON-backed content framework with admin overrides

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Feature

Add a multi-lingual, JSON-backed content framework so site copy can be managed
without redeployment. Content is stored in locale-namespaced JSON files with
optional DB overrides that admins can edit from the UI.

## Architecture

### Content layers (priority order)
1. DB overrides (admin UI editable, instant, no redeploy)
2. Locale JSON file  apps/web/content/{locale}/{namespace}.json
3. Fallback to en locale file
4. Hardcoded string as last resort

### Namespaces
- common   shared strings, buttons, errors
- nav      navigation labels (sidebar, public nav, footer)
- landing  landing page copy
- gallery  gallery page copy
- dashboard  dashboard section titles and stat labels
- walks    walk UI strings
- pets     pet UI strings
- settings settings page labels

### Schema
- contentOverrides table: locale, namespace, key (dot-notation), value, updatedBy, updatedAt
- userSettings.locale column (default en)

### API
- GET /api/public/content?locale=en&ns=landing  returns merged content, cached 5 min
- PUT /api/v1/admin/content  upsert override for locale+namespace+key

### Server helper  lib/content.ts
- getContent(namespace, locale)  reads JSON file + merges DB overrides

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Feature

Add a multi-lingual, JSON-backed content framework so site copy can be managed
without redeployment. Content is stored in locale-namespaced JSON files with
optional DB overrides that admins can edit from the UI.

## Architecture

### Content layers (priority order)
1. DB overrides (admin UI editable, instant, no redeploy)
2. Locale JSON file  apps/web/content/{locale}/{namespace}.json
3. Fallback to en locale file
4. Hardcoded string as last resort

### Namespaces
- common   shared strings, buttons, errors
- nav      navigation labels (sidebar, public nav, footer)
- landing  landing page copy
- gallery  gallery page copy
- dashboard  dashboard section titles and stat labels
- walks    walk UI strings
- pets     pet UI strings
- settings settings page labels

### Schema
- contentOverrides table: locale, namespace, key (dot-notation), value, updatedBy, updatedAt
- userSettings.locale column (default en)

### API
- GET /api/public/content?locale=en&ns=landing  returns merged content, cached 5 min
- PUT /api/v1/admin/content  upsert override for locale+namespace+key

### Server helper  lib/content.ts
- getContent(namespace, locale)  reads JSON file + merges DB overrides
- t(content, dotKey, fallback)  safe dot-notation accessor

### Client hook  hooks/useContent.ts
- useContent(namespace, locale?)  SWR against /api/public/content
- returns { t, content, isLoading }

issue.title: feat: gallery walk detail drawer - follow, share, alerts, photo feed, walk history

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Feature

Enhance the public gallery page so users can click a walk card to open a rich detail panel.

## Scope

### Walk Detail Drawer
- Slide-in drawer on card click
- Photo carousel (all photo events for the walk)
- Full stats: duration, distance, pace, calories
- Share caption / highlights
- Close button + keyboard escape

### Follow System
- Schema: \ollows\ table (followerId, followeeId, createdAt)
- \POST /api/v1/follows\  -  follow a walker
- \DELETE /api/v1/follows/[followeeId]\  -  unfollow
- \GET /api/v1/follows/[followeeId]\  -  check follow state
- Follow button in drawer walker profile (redirects to login for anon users)

### Alerts / Notifications
- Schema: \
otifications\ table (id, userId, type, title, body, entityId, entityType, readAt, createdAt)
- Triggered when a followed walker publishes a new walk
- \GET /api/v1/notifications\  -  list, with \?unread=true\ filter
- \PATCH /api/v1/notifications/[id]\  -  mark as read
- Bell icon in dashboard header with unread count badge

### Sharing
- Share button in drawer using Web Share API with clipboard fallback
- Shareable public URL: \/gallery/[id]\

### Photo Feed
- Photo tab in drawer showing all photos from the walk's events in a grid
- Click to fullscreen lightbox

### Walk History
- History tab in drawer showing this walker's last 10 published walks

### Public Gallery API
- \GET /api/public/gallery\  -  paginated, filterable, no auth required  
- \GET /api/public/gallery/[id]\  -  full walk detail with events/photos, no auth required

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Clicking a gallery card opens the detail drawer
- [ ] Drawer shows photo carousel, stats, walker profile
- [ ] Logged-in users can follow/unfollow a walker from the drawer
- [ ] Logged-in users see a notification bell in the dashboard header
- [ ] Share button copies link or opens native share sheet
- [ ] Photo tab shows all walk photos in a grid with lightbox
- [ ] History tab shows walker's last 10 published walks

issue.title: bug: 'Sign up free' button should open signup form with signup type options
issue.body:
## Bug Summary
Clicking **Sign up free** should take users to a sign-up form and explicitly capture signup type.

## Expected Behavior
- The **Sign up free** CTA navigates to a working sign-up form.
- The form shows signup type options: **hoster**, **team**, **single**.
- Selected signup type is captured and persisted with the signup submission.

## Current Behavior
- The CTA does not reliably lead to the expected sign-up flow and signup type capture is missing/unclear.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Clicking **Sign up free** from the entry page opens the sign-up form (no dead link, wrong route, or blank screen).
- [ ] The sign-up form displays signup type options: **hoster**, **team**, **single**.
- [ ] User can select exactly one signup type during signup.
- [ ] Submitted signup payload/store includes the selected signup type.
- [ ] Basic validation/error handling exists when no signup type is selected (if required by UX).
- [ ] Manual verification confirms all three signup types can be selected and submitted end-to-end.

## Notes
Issue-first triage capture for onboarding/auth + frontend signup path.

issue.title: Migrate web auth email flow from Nodemailer to Azure Communication Services
issue.body:
Replaced the web app’s Nodemailer-based Auth.js email flow with Azure Communication Services (ACS) Email, and aligned runtime/config/IaC so email auth can be deployed and operated via ACS end-to-end.

- **Auth provider migration (Nodemailer ➜ ACS)**
  - Added `apps/web/src/lib/email.ts` as an ACS email wrapper for Auth.js verification emails.
  - Switched `apps/web/src/auth.ts` email provider wiring to use the ACS-backed provider config.
  - Removed direct Nodemailer provider usage from auth flow.

- **Runtime config + package changes**
  - Updated `apps/web/src/lib/runtime-config.ts` email provider availability checks to ACS env pairs:
    - `ACS_EMAIL_CONNECTION_STRING` + `ACS_EMAIL_SENDER_ADDRESS`
    - `AUTH_ACS_EMAIL_CONNECTION_STRING` + `AUTH_ACS_EMAIL_SENDER_ADDRESS`
  - Added `@azure/communication-email` and removed `nodemailer` in `apps/web/package.json` (lockfile updated).

- **Config/documentation updates**
  - Updated `apps/web/.env.example` to ACS email variables and aliases.
  - Updated root `README.md` production auth provider examples to ACS email config.

- **Deployment guardrails + release checks**
  - Updated workflow auth provider validation logic to treat ACS env pairs as the email provider signal:
    - `.github/workflows/deploy-api.yml`
    - `.github/workflows/deploy-web.yml`
    - `.github/workflows/release-preflight.yml`
    - `.github/workflows/release-postcheck.yml`

- **IaC: ACS provisioning + app wiring**
  - Added `iac/communications/email-service.bicep` to provision:
    - `Microsoft.Communication/communicationServices`
    - `Microsoft.Communication/emailServices`
    - Azure-managed email domain + domain linkage
  - Updated `iac/main.bicep` to deploy ACS resources, seed ACS Key Vault secrets, and expose communication service output.
  - Updated `iac/backend/container-app.bicep` to inject ACS connection/sender secrets as runtime env for auth email.

- **Targeted email behavior coverage**
  - Added `apps/web/src/__tests__/email.test.ts` covering:
    - missing ACS config behavior
    - successful ACS verification send path via mocked `EmailClient`

```ts
// apps/web/src/lib/email.ts
const poller = await emailClient.beginSend({
  senderAddress: settings.senderAddress,
  recipients: { to: [{ address: identifier }] },
  content,
});
const response = await poller.pollUntilDone();
if (!response || response.status !== 'Succeeded') {
  throw new Error(`ACS email send failed with status: ${response?.status ?? 'Unknown'}`);
}
```

> [!WARNING]
>
> <details>
> <summary>Firewall rules blocked me from connecting to one or more addresses (expand for details)</summary>

## Summary
Replace Nodemailer-based email sending with Azure Communication Services (ACS) Email.

- No runtime dependency on Nodemailer remains.
- Existing email-related tests pass with ACS implementation.
- Deployment/config docs reflect ACS setup.

## Notes
Requested via: `feature: replace node mailer with azure communication services`

issue.title: RCA: temporary TLS outage perception during Front Door custom-domain propagation
issue.body:
## Summary
After domain cutover, managed certificate propagation delay at edge caused browser certificate mismatch (`ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID`) despite partial backend health.

## Impact
- Users experienced site as down/untrusted on affected hostnames.

issue.title: feat: migrate from Azure AD B2C (EOL) to Microsoft Entra External ID (CIAM)

labels.name: sprint:s1
labels.description: Sprint S1 — Entra External ID + P0 Login fixes

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Summary

Azure AD B2C is end-of-life and must be replaced with Microsoft Entra External ID (CIAM). The B2C tenant \wawkrid\ was never actually provisioned (IaC gated behind \deployB2CTenant=false\), so this is a greenfield migration.

See **[ADR-001](../docs/adr/ADR-001-entra-external-id-replaces-b2c.md)** for the full architecture decision record.

## Why

- Azure AD B2C is EOL  -  no new features, retirement timeline announced
- Entra External ID is the official successor with native Bicep/ARM support
- Unified with the Entra ecosystem (same Graph API, conditional access, MFA, passwordless)
- Simpler integration: standard OIDC, no custom provider required in NextAuth

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] \iac/identity/external-id-tenant.bicep\ deployed and CIAM tenant active (\pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com\)
- [ ] App registration created in CIAM tenant with correct redirect URIs (\https://app.pawzum.com/api/auth/callback/microsoft-entra-id\)
- [ ] \^Guth.ts\ updated  -  \MicrosoftEntraID\ provider configured with \ciamlogin.com\ issuer
- [ ] \untime-config.ts\ updated  -  provider ID \^Gzure-ad-b2c\ replaced with \^[ntra-external-id\
- [ ] Env vars: \AUTH_EXTERNAL_ID_TENANT\, \AUTH_MICROSOFT_ENTRA_ID_ID\, \AUTH_MICROSOFT_ENTRA_ID_SECRET\ set in Key Vault + container app
- [ ] Old B2C env vars removed from container app + Key Vault
- [ ] Sign-up/sign-in user flow configured (email + social: Google, Apple)
- [ ] Login works end-to-end on \^Gpp.pawzum.com\
- [ ] \.env.example\ updated

## Implementation Waves

### Wave 1  -  IaC: Provision CIAM Tenant
- Use \iac/identity/external-id-tenant.bicep\ (already created)
- Resource: \Microsoft.AzureActiveDirectory/ciamDirectories@2023-01-18-preview\
- **Deployment scope: subscription**  -  use \^Gz deployment sub create\

### Wave 2  -  App Registration
- Create app in CIAM tenant with redirect URIs + scopes
- Store in Key Vault: \^[ntra-external-id-client-id\ / \^[ntra-external-id-client-secret\
- Set GitHub secrets: \ENTRA_EXTERNAL_ID_CLIENT_ID\, \ENTRA_EXTERNAL_ID_CLIENT_SECRET\

### Wave 3  -  Auth Integration
- \^Guth.ts\: configure \MicrosoftEntraID\ with CIAM issuer (\{tenant}.ciamlogin.com\)
- \untime-config.ts\: replace B2C provider definition with \^[ntra-external-id\
- Add \AUTH_EXTERNAL_ID_TENANT\ env var

### Wave 4  -  Cleanup
- Remove \AUTH_B2C_*\ env vars and Key Vault secrets
- Archive \B2C-tenant.bicep\
- Update \.env.example\

## IaC Snippet

\\\icep
// iac/identity/external-id-tenant.bicep
resource externalIdTenant 'Microsoft.AzureActiveDirectory/ciamDirectories@2023-01-18-preview' = {
  name: 'pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com'
  location: 'United States'
  properties: {
    displayName: 'Pawzum Identity'
    domainName: 'pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com'
  }
}
// OIDC Issuer: https://pawzumid.ciamlogin.com/pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com/v2.0
\\\

## Notes

- Tenant creator requires \Tenant Creator\ role in Entra ID (elevated  -  may require manual portal step)
- Verify \pawzumid\ name availability before deployment
- If Graph Bicep extension unavailable, use post-deploy Graph API script for app registration

Removed \postgresConnector\ resource and \postgresServerId\ param from \iac/backend/service-connectors.bicep\. PostgreSQL DB connectivity is handled via the \database-url\ Key Vault secret injected as a container app secret reference  -  no service linker needed.

issue.body:
## Summary
\iac/backend/service-connectors.bicep\ defines service linkers for Cosmos, Storage, Key Vault, and App Config  -  but **PostgreSQL is completely absent**. The container app has no Service Connector to \wawkr-pg-dev\.

## Current connectors (verified via az CLI)
- cosmos_private_mi Γ£ô
- storage_private_mi Γ£ô
- keyvault_private_mi Γ£ô
- appconfig_private_mi Γ£ô
- **postgres_private_mi Γ£ù MISSING**

## Impact
- No managed service binding between \wawkr-api\ container app and \wawkr-pg-dev\
- DB connection relies entirely on password in \database-url\ KV secret
- If KV secret has empty/wrong password ΓåÆ SASL error ΓåÆ all DB-dependent routes fail
- LOGIN BROKEN: \/api/public/auth-providers\ 500s ΓåÆ login page cannot load providers

## Root Cause Chain
\database-url\ KV secret password is null/empty at runtime ΓåÆ \pg-pool.connect\ fails with \PostgreSQL error (code: UNKNOWN)\ ΓåÆ \getRuntimeAuthProviderConfig()\ throws ΓåÆ \/api/public/auth-providers\ returns 500 ΓåÆ login page broken.

## Fix
1. Add \postgresConnector\ resource to \service-connectors.bicep\ (private link, user-assigned MI)
2. Pass \postgresServerId: postgres.outputs.serverId\ in \main.bicep\
3. Verify/fix \database-url\ KV secret has correct password from \POSTGRES_ADMIN_PASSWORD\

IaC fix committed in this PR.

issue.title: bug(iac): DNS RBAC cross-RG deploy fails - GH Actions SP lacks roleAssignments/write on rg-core-services
issue.body:
## Root Cause

The GitHub Actions service principal (object id \70d600bd-...\) has Contributor on \wawkr-rg-dev\ but NOT on \g-core-services\. The \ront-door-dns-rbac\ Bicep module deploys cross-RG to \g-core-services\ and requires \Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write\  -  which requires Owner or User Access Administrator.

## Error

\\\
Authorization failed for template resource '...'. The client with object id '70d600bd-...'
does not have permission to perform action 'Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write'
at scope '.../resourceGroups/rg-core-services/providers/Microsoft.Network/dnsZones/pawzum.com/...'
\\\

## Fix Applied (commit 197ada3)

Added \deployDnsRbac bool = false\ parameter to \main.bicep\. The DNS RBAC module is now gated: only deployed when \deployDnsRbac=true\. Normal CI runs leave it false  -  the RBAC was applied manually on 2026-05-22.

## Long-term Fix Needed

Grant the GH Actions SP \User Access Administrator\ on \g-core-services\ (scoped to the DNS zone resource), then set \deployDnsRbac=true\ in the workflow to allow IaC to manage RBAC idempotently.

issue.title: chore(ci): add concurrency guard to Lighthouse CI

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Problem
`lighthouse-ci.yml` can run alongside the main CI workflow on the same PR, which allows duplicate checks to pile up.

## Proposal
Add a workflow-level `concurrency` block with `cancel-in-progress: true` so only the newest Lighthouse CI run for a given ref survives.

## Scope
- `.github/workflows/lighthouse-ci.yml`

## Why
- Keeps PR checks from stacking up
- Matches the existing concurrency guard already used by `ci.yml`

issue.title: fix(ci): enable E2E auth bypass in integration test server

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Problem
Vitest integration tests start `next dev` without the E2E auth bypass env, so the proxy rejects the synthetic test session cookie with 401 on `/api/__test/set-role`.

## Fix
Start the test server with `E2E_AUTH_BYPASS=1` in `src/__tests__/globalSetup.ts` so the proxy gate and CSRF bypass match the test harness.

## Impact
Unblocks `pnpm build` / CI test stage without weakening production auth.

issue.title: suggestion(basecoat): require full-pagination backlog reconciliation

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Suggestion
When reconciling issue backlogs, BaseCoat guidance should require scanning the full open set (paginated) and reporting the total issue count before classification.

## Why
A first-page-only pass can miss older or newer related issues and produce partial reconciliation outcomes.

## Proposed guardrail
- Always query all open issues (not first page only)
- Report OPEN total count in the reconciliation output
- Mark any partial pass as provisional until full-pagination pass completes

## Outcome from this repo
We corrected a 25-issue partial pass to a full 45-issue reconciliation and updated the sprint tracker accordingly.

issue.title: feat(separation): Wave 1 — managed identities + admin/backoffice scaffolds (#183)
issue.body:
## Summary

Closes #183 (partial — Wave 1 of the app separation work)

This PR contains the **first wave** of changes to split the monolith into 4 independent Container Apps. Subsequent waves (container IaC, Front Door routing, deploy workflows) will follow in the same PR as they complete.

## Wave 1 — What's here

### Managed identities + RBAC (iac/main.bicep)
- wawkr-web-mi — managed identity for the web frontend Container App
- wawkr-admin-mi — managed identity for the service admin Container App  
- wawkr-bo-mi — managed identity for the backoffice Container App
- L5 RBAC: each identity gets AcrPull, Storage Blob Data Reader, Key Vault Secrets User (least-privilege)
- Outputs wired for L6 consumption: webAppIdentityPrincipalId, ^GdminIdentityPrincipalId,  ackofficeIdentityPrincipalId

### apps/admin scaffold
- Next.js app at port 3001, package @wawkr/admin
- Routes: / (dashboard), /users, /content, /settings, /instances, /api/health
- Auth middleware protecting all routes except health check
- References @wawkr/types and @wawkr/tokens

### apps/backoffice scaffold

issue.title: feat: service admin interface with instance management, federation, and white-label SaaS

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Feature

Build a service-level admin interface for managing a Pawzum deployment instance. This sits above the per-tenant admin (/settings/admin) and manages the full platform: users, content, settings, moderation, usage monitoring, and deployment instances.

## Scope

### Core UI sections (/service-admin)
- Dashboard: usage stats, active users, walk counts, storage, error rates
- Users: list all users, edit profiles, reset passwords, assign credits, suspend/ban
- Content: site-wide content overrides, feature flags, i18n strings
- Moderation: flag/remove bad walks, photos, captions, profiles
- Instances: manage deployment instances (regional, private, white-label)
- Analytics: telemetry, event counts, latency, usage over time

### Instance model
- Each deployment is an "instance" (global, regional, or private/white-label)
- Instances have their own domain, branding, user pool, feature flags
- Federation: instances can be linked so users/feeds are shared across boundaries
- Stamping: create a new private instance for a team (dog walkers, family, etc.)

### White-label SaaS
- Private instance = same app, own domain, own branding, own user pool
- Federation allows plugging one instance into another (shared walk feeds, user directory)
- Instance config stored in DB; IaC provisions the deployment separately

### API surface (/api/service-admin/*)
- Users CRUD with elevated bypass of tenant isolation
- Instances CRUD
- Analytics read endpoints
- Moderation actions (delete content, suspend user)
- Federation management (invite/accept/revoke peer)

### Access control
- New role: service-admin (superuser above owner)
- Proxy guards /service-admin/* to service-admin role only
- Separate layout with its own nav

## Schema additions
- instances table: id, name, type (global/regional/private/white-label), domain, ownerUserId, planTier, settings JSON, isActive, createdAt
- instanceMembers table: instanceId, userId, role, joinedAt
- instanceFederation table: instanceId, peerId, status (pending/active/suspended), createdAt

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] /service-admin only accessible to service-admin role
- [ ] User list with search, filter by role, suspend/unsuspend action
- [ ] Instance list with create/edit/delete
- [ ] Federation invite/accept/revoke flow
- [ ] Content override panel (same functionality as tenant admin but global scope)
- [ ] Moderation queue for flagged content
- [ ] Analytics dashboard with key metrics

issue.title: feat(sre): Azure SRE agent with per-layer alerting, diagnostics, workbook (#181)
issue.body:
## Summary

Closes #181

Adds a separate IaC module for site reliability: alerting, diagnostic log routing, and an Azure Monitor workbook. Also adds a Copilot SRE runbook agent.

## Changes

### IaC (\iac/sre/\)

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| \sre-main.bicep\ | Orchestrator — references existing app stack by name, never writes to app resources |
| \^Gction-group.bicep\ | Notification routing (email, webhook, PagerDuty) |
| \^Glerts.bicep\ | 13 tiered metric + log alert rules (Sev0–Sev3) |
| \workbook.bicep\ | Azure Monitor workbook with API, DB, Storage, Front Door, Overview tabs |

### Alert coverage

| Layer | Alert | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| Container App | Zero running replicas | Sev0 |
| Container App | HTTP 5xx rate >5% | Sev1 |
| Container App | p95 latency >2s | Sev2 |
| Container App | CPU >80% | Sev2 |
| Container App | Memory >80% | Sev2 |
| Container App | Restart storm | Sev3 |
| PostgreSQL | Connection failures | Sev1 |
| PostgreSQL | Memory >90% | Sev1 |
| PostgreSQL | CPU >85% | Sev2 |
| PostgreSQL | Storage >85% | Sev2 |
| Storage | Availability <99% | Sev2 |
| Storage | Server errors | Sev2 |
| App Insights | Exceptions >10/5min | Sev1 |
| App Insights | Availability test fail | Sev1 |
| Key Vault | Unauthorized access | Sev2 |

### Workflow

- \.github/workflows/deploy-sre.yml\ — OIDC, unique concurrency group, \cancel-in-progress: false\
- Triggers on push to \iac/sre/**\ or manual \workflow_dispatch\ with environment selector

### Copilot Agent

- \.github/agents/sre-agent.agent.md\ — resource topology, incident runbooks, KQL queries for common failure modes, SLO/SLI queries

## Governance

- Separate deploy workflow with its own concurrency group (never shares with app deploy)
- OIDC only — no stored client secrets
- SRE module uses \^[xisting\ resource references only — zero write access to app resources

issue.title: feat: separate web-app, API, admin, and backoffice into independent Container Apps

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Problem

All application layers currently share a single Container App (wawkr-api). This forces coordinated deploys and prevents teams from releasing the frontend, API, admin, and backoffice independently.

## Proposed Architecture

Split into **4 separate Container Apps**, each with its own:
- Container image, deployment workflow, revision strategy
- Managed identity and RBAC scope
- Front Door origin and custom domain
- Health probe and SRE alert rules
- Independent scaling rules

| App | Container Name | Domain | Port |
|---|---|---|---|
| Web (Next.js app) | wawkr-web-app | ^Gpp.pawzum.com | 3000 |
| API (REST/Next.js routes) | wawkr-api (existing) | ^Gpi.pawzum.com | 3000 |
| Admin (service admin) | wawkr-admin | ^Gdmin.pawzum.com | 3000 |
| Backoffice (internal ops) | wawkr-backoffice | backoffice.pawzum.com | 3000 |

## Scope

### IaC changes (iac/)
- Add web-app, ^Gdmin, ackoffice container app resources to main.bicep L6 (Compute)
- Each app gets its own managed identity (wawkr-web-mi, wawkr-admin-mi, wawkr-backoffice-mi)
- Add Front Door origins and routes for each new domain
- Parameterize each app's image URI independently
- SRE alerting module updated for all 4 apps

### Deploy workflows (.github/workflows/)
- deploy-web-app.yml  -  independent deploy for web app container
- deploy-admin.yml  -  independent deploy for admin container  
- deploy-backoffice.yml  -  independent deploy for backoffice container
- Existing deploy-api.yml continues unchanged
- Each uses OIDC, unique concurrency group, cancel-in-progress: false for zero-downtime

### App scaffolding (^Gpps/)
- ^Gpps/admin/  -  new Next.js app for service admin interface (issue #179)
- ^Gpps/backoffice/  -  new Next.js app for internal operations
- Shared packages (packages/types, packages/tokens) consumed by all apps

### Database access
- All apps share the same PostgreSQL instance but connect through separate service connectors with least-privilege roles

### Rollout strategy
- Deploy new container apps alongside existing without removing the current single app
- Switch Front Door routing incrementally, verify, then decommission the old combined app

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 4 container apps deployed independently in each environment
- [ ] Each app has its own deploy workflow triggered only by changes to its ^Gpps/<name>/ path
- [ ] Zero-downtime cutover: new apps live before old app removed
- [ ] Each app has its own managed identity with least-privilege RBAC
- [ ] SRE alerts cover all 4 apps
- [ ] Turborepo pipeline correctly builds only affected apps on change

- ^Gpps/admin/  -  new Next.js app for service admin interface (issue #179)
- ^Gpps/backoffice/  -  new Next.js app for internal operations

- All apps share the same PostgreSQL instance but connect through separate service connectors with least-privilege roles

- Deploy new container apps alongside existing without removing the current single app
- Switch Front Door routing incrementally, verify, then decommission the old combined app

- [ ] 4 container apps deployed independently in each environment
- [ ] Each app has its own deploy workflow triggered only by changes to its ^Gpps/<name>/ path
- [ ] Zero-downtime cutover: new apps live before old app removed
- [ ] Each app has its own managed identity with least-privilege RBAC
- [ ] SRE alerts cover all 4 apps
- [ ] Turborepo pipeline correctly builds only affected apps on change

issue.body:
## Summary

Closes #183 (partial — Wave 1 of the app separation work)

This PR contains the **first wave** of changes to split the monolith into 4 independent Container Apps. Subsequent waves (container IaC, Front Door routing, deploy workflows) will follow in the same PR as they complete.

## Wave 1 — What's here

### Managed identities + RBAC (iac/main.bicep)
- wawkr-web-mi — managed identity for the web frontend Container App
- wawkr-admin-mi — managed identity for the service admin Container App  
- wawkr-bo-mi — managed identity for the backoffice Container App
- L5 RBAC: each identity gets AcrPull, Storage Blob Data Reader, Key Vault Secrets User (least-privilege)
- Outputs wired for L6 consumption: webAppIdentityPrincipalId, ^GdminIdentityPrincipalId,  ackofficeIdentityPrincipalId

### apps/admin scaffold
- Next.js app at port 3001, package @wawkr/admin
- Routes: / (dashboard), /users, /content, /settings, /instances, /api/health
- Auth middleware protecting all routes except health check
- References @wawkr/types and @wawkr/tokens

### apps/backoffice scaffold
- Next.js app at port 3002, package @wawkr/backoffice
- Routes: / (dashboard), /monitoring, /deployments, /data, /users, /api/health
- Auth middleware (managed identity / internal header guard)

## Waves still pending (same branch)
- sep-iac-containers — 3 new Container App resources in IaC
- sep-iac-frontdoor — Front Door origins/routes for 3 new domains  
- sep-workflows — Independent deploy workflows per app
- sep-sre-update — Alert rules for all 4 apps
- sep-cutover — Zero-downtime routing switch + old app decommission

issue.title: feat: service admin interface with instance management, federation, and white-label SaaS

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Feature

Build a service-level admin interface for managing a Pawzum deployment instance. This sits above the per-tenant admin (/settings/admin) and manages the full platform: users, content, settings, moderation, usage monitoring, and deployment instances.

## Scope

### Core UI sections (/service-admin)
- Dashboard: usage stats, active users, walk counts, storage, error rates
- Users: list all users, edit profiles, reset passwords, assign credits, suspend/ban
- Content: site-wide content overrides, feature flags, i18n strings
- Moderation: flag/remove bad walks, photos, captions, profiles
- Instances: manage deployment instances (regional, private, white-label)
- Analytics: telemetry, event counts, latency, usage over time

### Instance model
- Each deployment is an "instance" (global, regional, or private/white-label)
- Instances have their own domain, branding, user pool, feature flags
- Federation: instances can be linked so users/feeds are shared across boundaries
- Stamping: create a new private instance for a team (dog walkers, family, etc.)

### White-label SaaS
- Private instance = same app, own domain, own branding, own user pool
- Federation allows plugging one instance into another (shared walk feeds, user directory)
- Instance config stored in DB; IaC provisions the deployment separately

### API surface (/api/service-admin/*)
- Users CRUD with elevated bypass of tenant isolation
- Instances CRUD
- Analytics read endpoints
- Moderation actions (delete content, suspend user)
- Federation management (invite/accept/revoke peer)

### Access control
- New role: service-admin (superuser above owner)
- Proxy guards /service-admin/* to service-admin role only
- Separate layout with its own nav

## Schema additions
- instances table: id, name, type (global/regional/private/white-label), domain, ownerUserId, planTier, settings JSON, isActive, createdAt
- instanceMembers table: instanceId, userId, role, joinedAt
- instanceFederation table: instanceId, peerId, status (pending/active/suspended), createdAt

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] /service-admin only accessible to service-admin role
- [ ] User list with search, filter by role, suspend/unsuspend action
- [ ] Instance list with create/edit/delete
- [ ] Federation invite/accept/revoke flow
- [ ] Content override panel (same functionality as tenant admin but global scope)
- [ ] Moderation queue for flagged content
- [ ] Analytics dashboard with key metrics

issue.title: feat: separate web-app, API, admin, and backoffice into independent Container Apps

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Problem

All application layers currently share a single Container App (wawkr-api). This forces coordinated deploys and prevents teams from releasing the frontend, API, admin, and backoffice independently.

## Proposed Architecture

Split into **4 separate Container Apps**, each with its own:
- Container image, deployment workflow, revision strategy
- Managed identity and RBAC scope
- Front Door origin and custom domain
- Health probe and SRE alert rules
- Independent scaling rules

| App | Container Name | Domain | Port |
|---|---|---|---|
| Web (Next.js app) | wawkr-web-app | ^Gpp.pawzum.com | 3000 |
| API (REST/Next.js routes) | wawkr-api (existing) | ^Gpi.pawzum.com | 3000 |
| Admin (service admin) | wawkr-admin | ^Gdmin.pawzum.com | 3000 |
| Backoffice (internal ops) | wawkr-backoffice | backoffice.pawzum.com | 3000 |

## Scope

### IaC changes (iac/)
- Add web-app, ^Gdmin, ackoffice container app resources to main.bicep L6 (Compute)
- Each app gets its own managed identity (wawkr-web-mi, wawkr-admin-mi, wawkr-backoffice-mi)
- Add Front Door origins and routes for each new domain
- Parameterize each app's image URI independently
- SRE alerting module updated for all 4 apps

### Deploy workflows (.github/workflows/)
- deploy-web-app.yml  -  independent deploy for web app container
- deploy-admin.yml  -  independent deploy for admin container  
- deploy-backoffice.yml  -  independent deploy for backoffice container
- Existing deploy-api.yml continues unchanged
- Each uses OIDC, unique concurrency group, cancel-in-progress: false for zero-downtime

### App scaffolding (^Gpps/)
- ^Gpps/admin/  -  new Next.js app for service admin interface (issue #179)
- ^Gpps/backoffice/  -  new Next.js app for internal operations
- Shared packages (packages/types, packages/tokens) consumed by all apps

### Database access
- All apps share the same PostgreSQL instance but connect through separate service connectors with least-privilege roles

### Rollout strategy
- Deploy new container apps alongside existing without removing the current single app
- Switch Front Door routing incrementally, verify, then decommission the old combined app

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 4 container apps deployed independently in each environment
- [ ] Each app has its own deploy workflow triggered only by changes to its ^Gpps/<name>/ path
- [ ] Zero-downtime cutover: new apps live before old app removed
- [ ] Each app has its own managed identity with least-privilege RBAC
- [ ] SRE alerts cover all 4 apps
- [ ] Turborepo pipeline correctly builds only affected apps on change

issue.title: feat(ciam): Wave 1 - Entra External ID CIAM tenant IaC
issue.body:
## Summary

Wave 1 of the B2C → CIAM migration (#165): provisions an **Entra External ID (CIAM)** tenant via Bicep IaC.

Closes #166.
Part of epic #165.

---

## Changes

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| \iac/ciam/ciam-tenant.bicep\ | \Microsoft.AzureActiveDirectory/ciamDirectories@2023-05-17-preview\ at RG scope |
| \iac/ciam/ciam-main.bicep\ | Subscription-scope orchestrator — creates \wawkr-ciam-{env}\ RG and deploys module |
| \iac/ciam/ciam-main.bicepparam\ | Dev defaults (\	enantName=pawzum\, \^[astus2\, \Standard\ SKU) |
| \.github/workflows/deploy-ciam.yml\ | OIDC deploy workflow with what-if, KV output storage, \cancel-in-progress: false\ |

## Design notes

- \ciamDirectories\ is RG-scoped; the orchestrator runs at subscription scope to create the RG first, then deploys the module with \scope: ciamRg\
- CIAM directory \location\ param uses display name values (\'United States'\), not ARM region codes
- Outputs (tenantId, domain, loginDomain, issuerUrl) stored in \wawkr-kv-{env}\ Key Vault post-deployment
- Workflow uses \^Gzure/login@v2\ OIDC only — no client secrets stored (governance guardrail)

issue.title: feat: migrate from Azure AD B2C (EOL) to Microsoft Entra External ID (CIAM)

labels.name: sprint:s1
labels.description: Sprint S1 — Entra External ID + P0 Login fixes

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Summary

Azure AD B2C is end-of-life and must be replaced with Microsoft Entra External ID (CIAM). The B2C tenant \wawkrid\ was never actually provisioned (IaC gated behind \deployB2CTenant=false\), so this is a greenfield migration.

See **[ADR-001](../docs/adr/ADR-001-entra-external-id-replaces-b2c.md)** for the full architecture decision record.

## Why

- Azure AD B2C is EOL  -  no new features, retirement timeline announced
- Entra External ID is the official successor with native Bicep/ARM support
- Unified with the Entra ecosystem (same Graph API, conditional access, MFA, passwordless)
- Simpler integration: standard OIDC, no custom provider required in NextAuth

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] \iac/identity/external-id-tenant.bicep\ deployed and CIAM tenant active (\pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com\)
- [ ] App registration created in CIAM tenant with correct redirect URIs (\https://app.pawzum.com/api/auth/callback/microsoft-entra-id\)

issue.title: feat(separation): Wave 1 — managed identities + admin/backoffice scaffolds (#183)
issue.body:
## Summary

Closes #183 (partial — Wave 1 of the app separation work)

This PR contains the **first wave** of changes to split the monolith into 4 independent Container Apps. Subsequent waves (container IaC, Front Door routing, deploy workflows) will follow in the same PR as they complete.

## Wave 1 — What's here

### Managed identities + RBAC (iac/main.bicep)
- wawkr-web-mi — managed identity for the web frontend Container App
- wawkr-admin-mi — managed identity for the service admin Container App  
- wawkr-bo-mi — managed identity for the backoffice Container App
- L5 RBAC: each identity gets AcrPull, Storage Blob Data Reader, Key Vault Secrets User (least-privilege)
- Outputs wired for L6 consumption: webAppIdentityPrincipalId, ^GdminIdentityPrincipalId,  ackofficeIdentityPrincipalId

### apps/admin scaffold
- Next.js app at port 3001, package @wawkr/admin
- Routes: / (dashboard), /users, /content, /settings, /instances, /api/health
- Auth middleware protecting all routes except health check
- References @wawkr/types and @wawkr/tokens

### apps/backoffice scaffold
- Next.js app at port 3002, package @wawkr/backoffice
- Routes: / (dashboard), /monitoring, /deployments, /data, /users, /api/health
- Auth middleware (managed identity / internal header guard)

## Waves still pending (same branch)
- sep-iac-containers — 3 new Container App resources in IaC
- sep-iac-frontdoor — Front Door origins/routes for 3 new domains  
- sep-workflows — Independent deploy workflows per app
- sep-sre-update — Alert rules for all 4 apps
- sep-cutover — Zero-downtime routing switch + old app decommission

issue.title: feat(feed): walk feed API — publish and share walks (#174)
issue.body:
## Summary

Adds the foundation for the walk social feed: users can publish completed walks and a feed API returns them enriched with pet, walker, and photo data.

## Changes

### Schema (\^Gpps/web/src/db/schema.ts\)
- \walks\: added \isPublished\, \publishedAt\, \shareCaption\
- New \ ollows\ table: follower/followee relationship for walker subscriptions
- New \
otifications\ table: in-app notifications triggered by follows and walk publishes

### API
- \GET /api/v1/feed\ — returns published walks scoped to the authenticated user and their team, enriched with walker profile, pet names/avatars, and highlight photo. Supports \?scope=personal|team|all\ and pagination.

## Testing
- Schema additions are additive; no existing columns removed
- Feed endpoint degrades gracefully when DB unavailable

Closes #174

issue.title: Runner onboarding gap: configure shared-build-agents routing
issue.body:
## Runner triage finding
Org-wide runner readiness scan found this repository is not configured to reliably build on the current shared runner fleet.

## Observed gaps
- Missing RUNNER_DEPLOY variable
- Workflows not routed via vars.RUNNER_DEPLOY fallback
- Repo not authorized in shared-build-agents runner group
- Workflow requires macOS runners (not in current shared fleet)

## Recent workflow activity
- Last run: 05/23/2026 17:43:11
- Workflow: CodeQL

## Why this matters
Workflows may queue indefinitely or continue using GitHub-hosted runners instead of the shared fleet.

## Requested fixes (do not implement in this issue triage step)
1. Add repo variable: `RUNNER_DEPLOY=shared-build-agents`
2. Route workflows via fallback-safe selector:
   - `runs-on: ${{ vars.RUNNER_DEPLOY || ''ubuntu-latest'' }}`
3. Ensure repo is authorized in org runner group `shared-build-agents`.
4. Validate a smoke workflow run is picked up by the intended runner path.

## Acceptance criteria
- No runner-routing gaps remain for this repo.
- New workflow runs start without prolonged queue delay.
- Repo can build using the current shared runner fleet.

## Summary

Created `scripts/bootstrap-b2c.ps1` and `scripts/bootstrap-b2c.sh` to automate Azure AD B2C post-provisioning steps that were previously manual.

## What the script does

1. Registers a web app in the B2C tenant with NextAuth callback URIs
2. Creates the `B2C_1_signup_signin` user flow via Graph API
3. Generates a client secret
4. Sets `B2C_CLIENT_ID` and `B2C_CLIENT_SECRET` in GitHub Secrets
5. Optionally adds social identity providers (Google, Facebook, Apple)

## Usage

```bash
# After running bootstrap.ps1 -Mode Cloud and Deploy Infrastructure:
./scripts/bootstrap-b2c.ps1
./scripts/bootstrap-b2c.sh

# With social providers:
./scripts/bootstrap-b2c.ps1 -AddGoogle -AddFacebook
./scripts/bootstrap-b2c.sh --add-google --add-facebook
```

## Implementation

- PR #146 includes the script
- README updated with Cloud Setup & Identity section
- bootstrap.ps1 updated to reference new script instead of manual comments

- #141 (Anonymous site requires sign-in)

issue.title: bug: PostgreSQL service connector missing from IaC - no private link binding for DB

labels.name: sprint:s1
labels.description: Sprint S1 — Entra External ID + P0 Login fixes

issue.body:
## Summary
\iac/backend/service-connectors.bicep\ defines service linkers for Cosmos, Storage, Key Vault, and App Config  -  but **PostgreSQL is completely absent**. The container app has no Service Connector to \wawkr-pg-dev\.

## Current connectors (verified via az CLI)
- cosmos_private_mi Γ£ô
- storage_private_mi Γ£ô
- keyvault_private_mi Γ£ô
- appconfig_private_mi Γ£ô
- **postgres_private_mi Γ£ù MISSING**

## Impact
- No managed service binding between \wawkr-api\ container app and \wawkr-pg-dev\
- DB connection relies entirely on password in \database-url\ KV secret
- If KV secret has empty/wrong password ΓåÆ SASL error ΓåÆ all DB-dependent routes fail
- LOGIN BROKEN: \/api/public/auth-providers\ 500s ΓåÆ login page cannot load providers

## Root Cause Chain
\database-url\ KV secret password is null/empty at runtime ΓåÆ \pg-pool.connect\ fails with \PostgreSQL error (code: UNKNOWN)\ ΓåÆ \getRuntimeAuthProviderConfig()\ throws ΓåÆ \/api/public/auth-providers\ returns 500 ΓåÆ login page broken.

## Fix
1. Add \postgresConnector\ resource to \service-connectors.bicep\ (private link, user-assigned MI)
2. Pass \postgresServerId: postgres.outputs.serverId\ in \main.bicep\
3. Verify/fix \database-url\ KV secret has correct password from \POSTGRES_ADMIN_PASSWORD\

IaC fix committed in this PR.

## Summary

Azure AD B2C is end-of-life and must be replaced with Microsoft Entra External ID (CIAM). The B2C tenant \wawkrid\ was never actually provisioned (IaC gated behind \deployB2CTenant=false\), so this is a greenfield migration.

See **[ADR-001](../docs/adr/ADR-001-entra-external-id-replaces-b2c.md)** for the full architecture decision record.

## Why

- Azure AD B2C is EOL  -  no new features, retirement timeline announced
- Entra External ID is the official successor with native Bicep/ARM support
- Unified with the Entra ecosystem (same Graph API, conditional access, MFA, passwordless)
- Simpler integration: standard OIDC, no custom provider required in NextAuth

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] \iac/identity/external-id-tenant.bicep\ deployed and CIAM tenant active (\pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com\)
- [ ] App registration created in CIAM tenant with correct redirect URIs (\https://app.pawzum.com/api/auth/callback/microsoft-entra-id\)
- [ ] \^Guth.ts\ updated  -  \MicrosoftEntraID\ provider configured with \ciamlogin.com\ issuer
- [ ] \untime-config.ts\ updated  -  provider ID \^Gzure-ad-b2c\ replaced with \^[ntra-external-id\
- [ ] Env vars: \AUTH_EXTERNAL_ID_TENANT\, \AUTH_MICROSOFT_ENTRA_ID_ID\, \AUTH_MICROSOFT_ENTRA_ID_SECRET\ set in Key Vault + container app
- [ ] Old B2C env vars removed from container app + Key Vault
- [ ] Sign-up/sign-in user flow configured (email + social: Google, Apple)
- [ ] Login works end-to-end on \^Gpp.pawzum.com\
- [ ] \.env.example\ updated

## Implementation Waves

### Wave 1  -  IaC: Provision CIAM Tenant
- Use \iac/identity/external-id-tenant.bicep\ (already created)
- Resource: \Microsoft.AzureActiveDirectory/ciamDirectories@2023-01-18-preview\
- **Deployment scope: subscription**  -  use \^Gz deployment sub create\

### Wave 2  -  App Registration
- Create app in CIAM tenant with redirect URIs + scopes
- Store in Key Vault: \^[ntra-external-id-client-id\ / \^[ntra-external-id-client-secret\
- Set GitHub secrets: \ENTRA_EXTERNAL_ID_CLIENT_ID\, \ENTRA_EXTERNAL_ID_CLIENT_SECRET\

### Wave 3  -  Auth Integration
- \^Guth.ts\: configure \MicrosoftEntraID\ with CIAM issuer (\{tenant}.ciamlogin.com\)
- \untime-config.ts\: replace B2C provider definition with \^[ntra-external-id\
- Add \AUTH_EXTERNAL_ID_TENANT\ env var

### Wave 4  -  Cleanup
- Remove \AUTH_B2C_*\ env vars and Key Vault secrets
- Archive \B2C-tenant.bicep\
- Update \.env.example\

## IaC Snippet

\\\icep
// iac/identity/external-id-tenant.bicep
resource externalIdTenant 'Microsoft.AzureActiveDirectory/ciamDirectories@2023-01-18-preview' = {
  name: 'pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com'
  location: 'United States'
  properties: {
    displayName: 'Pawzum Identity'
    domainName: 'pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com'
  }
}
// OIDC Issuer: https://pawzumid.ciamlogin.com/pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com/v2.0
\\\

## Notes

- Tenant creator requires \Tenant Creator\ role in Entra ID (elevated  -  may require manual portal step)
- Verify \pawzumid\ name availability before deployment
- If Graph Bicep extension unavailable, use post-deploy Graph API script for app registration

## Root Cause

Azure Service Linker (\Microsoft.ServiceLinker/linkers\) does not support \MICROSOFT.DBFORPOSTGRESQL/FLEXIBLESERVERS\ as a target type. Attempting to create the connector fails with \TargetTypeNotSupported\.

## Error

\\\
TargetTypeNotSupported: Target resource type MICROSOFT.DBFORPOSTGRESQL/FLEXIBLESERVERS is not supported.
\\\

Seen in IaC deploy run 26318685638.

## Fix Applied (commit 197ada3)

Removed \postgresConnector\ resource and \postgresServerId\ param from \iac/backend/service-connectors.bicep\. PostgreSQL DB connectivity is handled via the \database-url\ Key Vault secret injected as a container app secret reference  -  no service linker needed.

## Status: Resolved

issue.title: bug(iac): DNS RBAC cross-RG deploy fails - GH Actions SP lacks roleAssignments/write on rg-core-services
issue.body:
## Root Cause

The GitHub Actions service principal (object id \70d600bd-...\) has Contributor on \wawkr-rg-dev\ but NOT on \g-core-services\. The \ront-door-dns-rbac\ Bicep module deploys cross-RG to \g-core-services\ and requires \Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write\  -  which requires Owner or User Access Administrator.

## Error

\\\
Authorization failed for template resource '...'. The client with object id '70d600bd-...'
does not have permission to perform action 'Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write'
at scope '.../resourceGroups/rg-core-services/providers/Microsoft.Network/dnsZones/pawzum.com/...'
\\\

## Fix Applied (commit 197ada3)

Added \deployDnsRbac bool = false\ parameter to \main.bicep\. The DNS RBAC module is now gated: only deployed when \deployDnsRbac=true\. Normal CI runs leave it false  -  the RBAC was applied manually on 2026-05-22.

## Long-term Fix Needed

Grant the GH Actions SP \User Access Administrator\ on \g-core-services\ (scoped to the DNS zone resource), then set \deployDnsRbac=true\ in the workflow to allow IaC to manage RBAC idempotently.

## Feature

Add a multi-lingual, JSON-backed content framework so site copy can be managed
without redeployment. Content is stored in locale-namespaced JSON files with
optional DB overrides that admins can edit from the UI.

## Architecture

### Content layers (priority order)
1. DB overrides (admin UI editable, instant, no redeploy)
2. Locale JSON file  apps/web/content/{locale}/{namespace}.json
3. Fallback to en locale file
4. Hardcoded string as last resort

### Namespaces
- common   shared strings, buttons, errors
- nav      navigation labels (sidebar, public nav, footer)
- landing  landing page copy
- gallery  gallery page copy
- dashboard  dashboard section titles and stat labels
- walks    walk UI strings
- pets     pet UI strings
- settings settings page labels

### Schema
- contentOverrides table: locale, namespace, key (dot-notation), value, updatedBy, updatedAt
- userSettings.locale column (default en)

### API
- GET /api/public/content?locale=en&ns=landing  returns merged content, cached 5 min
- PUT /api/v1/admin/content  upsert override for locale+namespace+key

### Server helper  lib/content.ts
- getContent(namespace, locale)  reads JSON file + merges DB overrides
- t(content, dotKey, fallback)  safe dot-notation accessor

### Client hook  hooks/useContent.ts
- useContent(namespace, locale?)  SWR against /api/public/content
- returns { t, content, isLoading }

### Pages to update
- landing/page.tsx  switch to content
- gallery/page.tsx  switch to content
- Sidebar.tsx nav labels
- PublicFooter.tsx link labels
- settings/page.tsx labels

### Admin UI
- New Content Management panel in /settings/admin
- Namespace picker, key/value list, inline edit, save per key
- Shows default value from JSON file alongside the override field

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All landing page copy driven by content/en/landing.json
- [ ] Admin can override any key from /settings/admin without redeployment
- [ ] Adding content/es/ folder enables Spanish with zero code changes
- [ ] User language preference stored in userSettings.locale
- [ ] GET /api/public/content returns 304 with proper cache headers
- [ ] DB unavailable falls back to JSON file gracefully
- [ ] Audit log entry created on every admin content override

issue.title: feat: separate web-app, API, admin, and backoffice into independent Container Apps

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Problem

All application layers currently share a single Container App (wawkr-api). This forces coordinated deploys and prevents teams from releasing the frontend, API, admin, and backoffice independently.

## Proposed Architecture

Split into **4 separate Container Apps**, each with its own:
- Container image, deployment workflow, revision strategy
- Managed identity and RBAC scope
- Front Door origin and custom domain
- Health probe and SRE alert rules
- Independent scaling rules

| App | Container Name | Domain | Port |
|---|---|---|---|
| Web (Next.js app) | wawkr-web-app | ^Gpp.pawzum.com | 3000 |
| API (REST/Next.js routes) | wawkr-api (existing) | ^Gpi.pawzum.com | 3000 |
| Admin (service admin) | wawkr-admin | ^Gdmin.pawzum.com | 3000 |
| Backoffice (internal ops) | wawkr-backoffice | backoffice.pawzum.com | 3000 |

## Scope

### IaC changes (iac/)
- Add web-app, ^Gdmin, ackoffice container app resources to main.bicep L6 (Compute)
- Each app gets its own managed identity (wawkr-web-mi, wawkr-admin-mi, wawkr-backoffice-mi)
- Add Front Door origins and routes for each new domain
- Parameterize each app's image URI independently
- SRE alerting module updated for all 4 apps

### Deploy workflows (.github/workflows/)
- deploy-web-app.yml  -  independent deploy for web app container
- deploy-admin.yml  -  independent deploy for admin container  
- deploy-backoffice.yml  -  independent deploy for backoffice container
- Existing deploy-api.yml continues unchanged
- Each uses OIDC, unique concurrency group, cancel-in-progress: false for zero-downtime

### App scaffolding (^Gpps/)
- ^Gpps/admin/  -  new Next.js app for service admin interface (issue #179)
- ^Gpps/backoffice/  -  new Next.js app for internal operations
- Shared packages (packages/types, packages/tokens) consumed by all apps

### Database access
- All apps share the same PostgreSQL instance but connect through separate service connectors with least-privilege roles

### Rollout strategy
- Deploy new container apps alongside existing without removing the current single app
- Switch Front Door routing incrementally, verify, then decommission the old combined app

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 4 container apps deployed independently in each environment
- [ ] Each app has its own deploy workflow triggered only by changes to its ^Gpps/<name>/ path
- [ ] Zero-downtime cutover: new apps live before old app removed
- [ ] Each app has its own managed identity with least-privilege RBAC
- [ ] SRE alerts cover all 4 apps
- [ ] Turborepo pipeline correctly builds only affected apps on change

issue.body:
## Feature

Build a service-level admin interface for managing a Pawzum deployment instance. This sits above the per-tenant admin (/settings/admin) and manages the full platform: users, content, settings, moderation, usage monitoring, and deployment instances.

## Scope

### Core UI sections (/service-admin)
- Dashboard: usage stats, active users, walk counts, storage, error rates
- Users: list all users, edit profiles, reset passwords, assign credits, suspend/ban
- Content: site-wide content overrides, feature flags, i18n strings
- Moderation: flag/remove bad walks, photos, captions, profiles
- Instances: manage deployment instances (regional, private, white-label)
- Analytics: telemetry, event counts, latency, usage over time

### Instance model
- Each deployment is an "instance" (global, regional, or private/white-label)
- Instances have their own domain, branding, user pool, feature flags
- Federation: instances can be linked so users/feeds are shared across boundaries
- Stamping: create a new private instance for a team (dog walkers, family, etc.)

### White-label SaaS
- Private instance = same app, own domain, own branding, own user pool
- Federation allows plugging one instance into another (shared walk feeds, user directory)
- Instance config stored in DB; IaC provisions the deployment separately

### API surface (/api/service-admin/*)
- Users CRUD with elevated bypass of tenant isolation
- Instances CRUD
- Analytics read endpoints
- Moderation actions (delete content, suspend user)
- Federation management (invite/accept/revoke peer)

### Access control
- New role: service-admin (superuser above owner)
- Proxy guards /service-admin/* to service-admin role only
- Separate layout with its own nav

## Schema additions
- instances table: id, name, type (global/regional/private/white-label), domain, ownerUserId, planTier, settings JSON, isActive, createdAt
- instanceMembers table: instanceId, userId, role, joinedAt
- instanceFederation table: instanceId, peerId, status (pending/active/suspended), createdAt

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] /service-admin only accessible to service-admin role
- [ ] User list with search, filter by role, suspend/unsuspend action
- [ ] Instance list with create/edit/delete
- [ ] Federation invite/accept/revoke flow
- [ ] Content override panel (same functionality as tenant admin but global scope)
- [ ] Moderation queue for flagged content
- [ ] Analytics dashboard with key metrics

issue.title: RCA: runtime outage from .next cache permission regression in container image
issue.body:
## Summary
A deployment introduced runtime permission mismatch (`nextjs` user could not create `.next/cache`), causing app startup/runtime failures.

## Impact
- Post-deploy availability degradation.
- Unhandled runtime errors in container logs.

issue.body:
## Work Item

**Sprint:** S1
**Wave:** 3
**Agent:** backend-dev
**Priority:** P1
**Parent issue:** #165

### Description
Update the Next.js auth configuration to use the new CIAM tenant instead of Azure AD B2C. This is the code-level switch that makes login work end-to-end once the tenant and app registration are in place.

### Dependencies
- **Blocked by:** #167 (client ID/secret must be in KV before runtime-config can reference them), #166
- **Blocks:** #168 (B2C cleanup should only happen after this is verified working)

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] \^Gpps/web/src/auth.ts\ configures \MicrosoftEntraID\ provider with issuer URL \https://{tenant}.ciamlogin.com/{tenant}.onmicrosoft.com/v2.0\
- [ ] \^Gpps/web/src/lib/runtime-config.ts\ returns an \^[ntra-external-id\ provider entry (replaces \^Gzure-ad-b2c\)
- [ ] Environment variable \AUTH_EXTERNAL_ID_TENANT\ is defined in the container app's Bicep/env config and mapped to the CIAM tenant hostname
- [ ] Signing in with a Microsoft account on \https://app.pawzum.com\ completes the full OAuth flow without errors
- [ ] \/api/auth/session\ returns a valid session object after sign-in
- [ ] No \AUTH_B2C_*\ env vars are read by this code path (they may still exist but must not be required)

### Notes
- CIAM issuer format differs from regular Entra ID  -  use \{tenant}.ciamlogin.com\ not \login.microsoftonline.com\
- NextAuth v5 provider: \import MicrosoftEntraID from 'next-auth/providers/microsoft-entra-id'\

- Test with a guest/consumer Microsoft account, not an internal Entra ID account

issue.title: bug(iac): DNS RBAC cross-RG deploy fails - GH Actions SP lacks roleAssignments/write on rg-core-services
issue.body:
## Root Cause

The GitHub Actions service principal (object id \70d600bd-...\) has Contributor on \wawkr-rg-dev\ but NOT on \g-core-services\. The \ront-door-dns-rbac\ Bicep module deploys cross-RG to \g-core-services\ and requires \Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write\  -  which requires Owner or User Access Administrator.

## Error

\\\
Authorization failed for template resource '...'. The client with object id '70d600bd-...'
does not have permission to perform action 'Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write'
at scope '.../resourceGroups/rg-core-services/providers/Microsoft.Network/dnsZones/pawzum.com/...'
\\\

## Fix Applied (commit 197ada3)

Added \deployDnsRbac bool = false\ parameter to \main.bicep\. The DNS RBAC module is now gated: only deployed when \deployDnsRbac=true\. Normal CI runs leave it false  -  the RBAC was applied manually on 2026-05-22.

## Long-term Fix Needed

Grant the GH Actions SP \User Access Administrator\ on \g-core-services\ (scoped to the DNS zone resource), then set \deployDnsRbac=true\ in the workflow to allow IaC to manage RBAC idempotently.

issue.title: bug: PostgreSQL service connector missing from IaC - no private link binding for DB

labels.name: sprint:s1
labels.description: Sprint S1 — Entra External ID + P0 Login fixes

issue.body:
## Summary
\iac/backend/service-connectors.bicep\ defines service linkers for Cosmos, Storage, Key Vault, and App Config  -  but **PostgreSQL is completely absent**. The container app has no Service Connector to \wawkr-pg-dev\.

## Current connectors (verified via az CLI)
- cosmos_private_mi Γ£ô
- storage_private_mi Γ£ô
- keyvault_private_mi Γ£ô
- appconfig_private_mi Γ£ô
- **postgres_private_mi Γ£ù MISSING**

## Impact
- No managed service binding between \wawkr-api\ container app and \wawkr-pg-dev\
- DB connection relies entirely on password in \database-url\ KV secret
- If KV secret has empty/wrong password ΓåÆ SASL error ΓåÆ all DB-dependent routes fail
- LOGIN BROKEN: \/api/public/auth-providers\ 500s ΓåÆ login page cannot load providers

## Root Cause Chain
\database-url\ KV secret password is null/empty at runtime ΓåÆ \pg-pool.connect\ fails with \PostgreSQL error (code: UNKNOWN)\ ΓåÆ \getRuntimeAuthProviderConfig()\ throws ΓåÆ \/api/public/auth-providers\ returns 500 ΓåÆ login page broken.

## Fix
1. Add \postgresConnector\ resource to \service-connectors.bicep\ (private link, user-assigned MI)
2. Pass \postgresServerId: postgres.outputs.serverId\ in \main.bicep\
3. Verify/fix \database-url\ KV secret has correct password from \POSTGRES_ADMIN_PASSWORD\

IaC fix committed in this PR.

issue.title: RCA: login outage from invalid DATABASE_URL secret after deployment
issue.body:
## Summary
Users could not log in because authentication paths depended on a DB connection that was failing due to malformed/empty `DATABASE_URL` secret material.

## Impact
- Login unavailable or intermittently failing.
- `/api/public/auth-providers` returned 500 in degraded states.

## Evidence
- Prior traces showed PG/SASL failures during auth-provider and sign-in flows.
- Deployment history indicates secret/config drift around PostgreSQL password/connector setup.

## Workaround (no fix applied in this issue)
- Keep production login-provider toggles limited to verified providers only.
- Use temporary bypass only for controlled testing windows.

## Follow-up scope
- Validate secret material pre-deploy.
- Add health gate for auth-provider endpoint before rollout complete.

issue.title: feat: separate web-app, API, admin, and backoffice into independent Container Apps

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Problem

All application layers currently share a single Container App (wawkr-api). This forces coordinated deploys and prevents teams from releasing the frontend, API, admin, and backoffice independently.

## Proposed Architecture

Split into **4 separate Container Apps**, each with its own:
- Container image, deployment workflow, revision strategy
- Managed identity and RBAC scope
- Front Door origin and custom domain
- Health probe and SRE alert rules
- Independent scaling rules

| App | Container Name | Domain | Port |
|---|---|---|---|
| Web (Next.js app) | wawkr-web-app | ^Gpp.pawzum.com | 3000 |
| API (REST/Next.js routes) | wawkr-api (existing) | ^Gpi.pawzum.com | 3000 |
| Admin (service admin) | wawkr-admin | ^Gdmin.pawzum.com | 3000 |
| Backoffice (internal ops) | wawkr-backoffice | backoffice.pawzum.com | 3000 |

## Scope

### IaC changes (iac/)
- Add web-app, ^Gdmin, ackoffice container app resources to main.bicep L6 (Compute)
- Each app gets its own managed identity (wawkr-web-mi, wawkr-admin-mi, wawkr-backoffice-mi)
- Add Front Door origins and routes for each new domain
- Parameterize each app's image URI independently
- SRE alerting module updated for all 4 apps

### Deploy workflows (.github/workflows/)
- deploy-web-app.yml  -  independent deploy for web app container
- deploy-admin.yml  -  independent deploy for admin container  
- deploy-backoffice.yml  -  independent deploy for backoffice container
- Existing deploy-api.yml continues unchanged
- Each uses OIDC, unique concurrency group, cancel-in-progress: false for zero-downtime

### App scaffolding (^Gpps/)
- ^Gpps/admin/  -  new Next.js app for service admin interface (issue #179)
- ^Gpps/backoffice/  -  new Next.js app for internal operations
- Shared packages (packages/types, packages/tokens) consumed by all apps

### Database access
- All apps share the same PostgreSQL instance but connect through separate service connectors with least-privilege roles

### Rollout strategy
- Deploy new container apps alongside existing without removing the current single app
- Switch Front Door routing incrementally, verify, then decommission the old combined app

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 4 container apps deployed independently in each environment
- [ ] Each app has its own deploy workflow triggered only by changes to its ^Gpps/<name>/ path
- [ ] Zero-downtime cutover: new apps live before old app removed
- [ ] Each app has its own managed identity with least-privilege RBAC
- [ ] SRE alerts cover all 4 apps
- [ ] Turborepo pipeline correctly builds only affected apps on change

issue.title: feat: migrate from Azure AD B2C (EOL) to Microsoft Entra External ID (CIAM)

labels.name: sprint:s1
labels.description: Sprint S1 — Entra External ID + P0 Login fixes

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Summary

Azure AD B2C is end-of-life and must be replaced with Microsoft Entra External ID (CIAM). The B2C tenant \wawkrid\ was never actually provisioned (IaC gated behind \deployB2CTenant=false\), so this is a greenfield migration.

See **[ADR-001](../docs/adr/ADR-001-entra-external-id-replaces-b2c.md)** for the full architecture decision record.

## Why

- Azure AD B2C is EOL  -  no new features, retirement timeline announced
- Entra External ID is the official successor with native Bicep/ARM support
- Unified with the Entra ecosystem (same Graph API, conditional access, MFA, passwordless)
- Simpler integration: standard OIDC, no custom provider required in NextAuth

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] \iac/identity/external-id-tenant.bicep\ deployed and CIAM tenant active (\pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com\)

issue.title: feat: separate web-app, API, admin, and backoffice into independent Container Apps

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Problem

All application layers currently share a single Container App (wawkr-api). This forces coordinated deploys and prevents teams from releasing the frontend, API, admin, and backoffice independently.

## Proposed Architecture

Split into **4 separate Container Apps**, each with its own:
- Container image, deployment workflow, revision strategy
- Managed identity and RBAC scope
- Front Door origin and custom domain
- Health probe and SRE alert rules
- Independent scaling rules

| App | Container Name | Domain | Port |
|---|---|---|---|
| Web (Next.js app) | wawkr-web-app | ^Gpp.pawzum.com | 3000 |
| API (REST/Next.js routes) | wawkr-api (existing) | ^Gpi.pawzum.com | 3000 |
| Admin (service admin) | wawkr-admin | ^Gdmin.pawzum.com | 3000 |
| Backoffice (internal ops) | wawkr-backoffice | backoffice.pawzum.com | 3000 |

## Scope

### IaC changes (iac/)
- Add web-app, ^Gdmin, ackoffice container app resources to main.bicep L6 (Compute)
- Each app gets its own managed identity (wawkr-web-mi, wawkr-admin-mi, wawkr-backoffice-mi)
- Add Front Door origins and routes for each new domain
- Parameterize each app's image URI independently
- SRE alerting module updated for all 4 apps

### Deploy workflows (.github/workflows/)
- deploy-web-app.yml  -  independent deploy for web app container
- deploy-admin.yml  -  independent deploy for admin container  
- deploy-backoffice.yml  -  independent deploy for backoffice container
- Existing deploy-api.yml continues unchanged
- Each uses OIDC, unique concurrency group, cancel-in-progress: false for zero-downtime

### App scaffolding (^Gpps/)
- ^Gpps/admin/  -  new Next.js app for service admin interface (issue #179)
- ^Gpps/backoffice/  -  new Next.js app for internal operations
- Shared packages (packages/types, packages/tokens) consumed by all apps

### Database access
- All apps share the same PostgreSQL instance but connect through separate service connectors with least-privilege roles

### Rollout strategy
- Deploy new container apps alongside existing without removing the current single app
- Switch Front Door routing incrementally, verify, then decommission the old combined app

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 4 container apps deployed independently in each environment
- [ ] Each app has its own deploy workflow triggered only by changes to its ^Gpps/<name>/ path
- [ ] Zero-downtime cutover: new apps live before old app removed
- [ ] Each app has its own managed identity with least-privilege RBAC
- [ ] SRE alerts cover all 4 apps
- [ ] Turborepo pipeline correctly builds only affected apps on change

issue.title: feat: service admin interface with instance management, federation, and white-label SaaS

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Feature

Build a service-level admin interface for managing a Pawzum deployment instance. This sits above the per-tenant admin (/settings/admin) and manages the full platform: users, content, settings, moderation, usage monitoring, and deployment instances.

## Scope

### Core UI sections (/service-admin)
- Dashboard: usage stats, active users, walk counts, storage, error rates
- Users: list all users, edit profiles, reset passwords, assign credits, suspend/ban
- Content: site-wide content overrides, feature flags, i18n strings
- Moderation: flag/remove bad walks, photos, captions, profiles
- Instances: manage deployment instances (regional, private, white-label)
- Analytics: telemetry, event counts, latency, usage over time

### Instance model
- Each deployment is an "instance" (global, regional, or private/white-label)
- Instances have their own domain, branding, user pool, feature flags
- Federation: instances can be linked so users/feeds are shared across boundaries
- Stamping: create a new private instance for a team (dog walkers, family, etc.)

### White-label SaaS
- Private instance = same app, own domain, own branding, own user pool
- Federation allows plugging one instance into another (shared walk feeds, user directory)
- Instance config stored in DB; IaC provisions the deployment separately

### API surface (/api/service-admin/*)
- Users CRUD with elevated bypass of tenant isolation
- Instances CRUD
- Analytics read endpoints
- Moderation actions (delete content, suspend user)
- Federation management (invite/accept/revoke peer)

### Access control
- New role: service-admin (superuser above owner)
- Proxy guards /service-admin/* to service-admin role only
- Separate layout with its own nav

## Schema additions
- instances table: id, name, type (global/regional/private/white-label), domain, ownerUserId, planTier, settings JSON, isActive, createdAt
- instanceMembers table: instanceId, userId, role, joinedAt
- instanceFederation table: instanceId, peerId, status (pending/active/suspended), createdAt

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] /service-admin only accessible to service-admin role
- [ ] User list with search, filter by role, suspend/unsuspend action
- [ ] Instance list with create/edit/delete
- [ ] Federation invite/accept/revoke flow
- [ ] Content override panel (same functionality as tenant admin but global scope)
- [ ] Moderation queue for flagged content
- [ ] Analytics dashboard with key metrics
