issue.title: feat: Azure SRE agent with per-layer alerting, diagnostics, workbook and Copilot runbook agent

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Feature

Add a dedicated Azure SRE agent for the WawkR deployment. This is a separate IaC module (iac/sre/) that targets each infrastructure layer and wires up monitoring, alerting, diagnostic settings, and an AI-assisted incident response agent.

## Why separate

The SRE deployment references existing resources by ID/name rather than creating them. It can be applied independently after the core stack is up, upgraded without touching app infra, and scoped with minimal RBAC (Reader + Monitoring Contributor only).

## Architecture

### IaC module: iac/sre/

sre-main.bicep       -- orchestrator, accepts resource IDs for each layer
alerts.bicep         -- metric alert rules per layer (API, DB, Front Door, Container Apps)
action-group.bicep   -- notification targets (email, webhook, Teams)
diagnostic-settings.bicep -- route resource logs to Log Analytics workspace
workbook.bicep       -- Azure Monitor workbook with per-layer health dashboards

### Layers covered

| Layer | Resource type | Key signals |
|---|---|---|
| Public site | Static Web App | availability, bandwidth errors |
| API | Container App | request latency p95, 5xx rate, CPU/memory, replica count |
| Front Door | AFD | backend health probe failures, WAF blocks, total latency |
| Database | PostgreSQL Flexible | connection failures, CPU, storage, replication lag |
| Blob storage | Storage Account | 4xx/5xx errors, throttling |
| Key Vault | Key Vault | vault unavailable, secret expiry (via policy) |
| Container Apps Env | CAE | resource pressure, provisioning failures |

### Alert severity tiers

- Sev1 (Critical): API 5xx > 5%, DB connection failures, Front Door backend unhealthy
- Sev2 (High): API p95 latency > 2s, container CPU > 85%, Postgres CPU > 80%
- Sev3 (Warning): replica count at min, storage throttling, Key Vault nearing quota

### Copilot SRE agent: .github/agents/sre-agent.agent.md

An agent definition that knows:
- The full resource topology (names, resource groups, subscription)
- Common runbooks (restart container, scale out, failover DB, purge CDN cache)
- How to query Log Analytics for recent errors
- How to read and interpret Application Insights traces
- Escalation paths and on-call rotation contacts

### CI/CD

.github/workflows/deploy-sre.yml:
- Triggered on push to iac/sre/** or manually via workflow_dispatch
- Uses OIDC (no stored secrets)
- Separate from main deploy workflow so SRE config can be updated independently

## Parameters

sre-main.bicep will accept:
- resourceGroupName (where existing resources live)
- apiContainerAppId (resource ID)
- postgresServerId
- frontDoorId
- logAnalyticsWorkspaceId
- appInsightsId
- storageAccountId
- alertEmailAddresses (array)
- webhookUri (optional, for Teams/Slack/PagerDuty)
- environment (dev/staging/prod)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] iac/sre/sre-main.bicep deploys cleanly against a live stack
- [ ] All Sev1 alert rules exist and fire in test (via metric override)
- [ ] Action group routes to at least one email target
- [ ] Diagnostic settings land logs in the existing Log Analytics workspace
- [ ] Azure Monitor Workbook has one tab per layer with key metrics
- [ ] deploy-sre.yml workflow uses OIDC, has unique concurrency group
- [ ] SRE Copilot agent knows all resource names and runbook steps
- [ ] No hardcoded secrets anywhere in the IaC or workflow

issue.title: feat: separate web-app, API, admin, and backoffice into independent Container Apps

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Problem

All application layers currently share a single Container App (wawkr-api). This forces coordinated deploys and prevents teams from releasing the frontend, API, admin, and backoffice independently.

## Proposed Architecture

Split into **4 separate Container Apps**, each with its own:
- Container image, deployment workflow, revision strategy
- Managed identity and RBAC scope
- Front Door origin and custom domain
- Health probe and SRE alert rules
- Independent scaling rules

| App | Container Name | Domain | Port |
|---|---|---|---|
| Web (Next.js app) | wawkr-web-app | ^Gpp.pawzum.com | 3000 |
| API (REST/Next.js routes) | wawkr-api (existing) | ^Gpi.pawzum.com | 3000 |
| Admin (service admin) | wawkr-admin | ^Gdmin.pawzum.com | 3000 |
| Backoffice (internal ops) | wawkr-backoffice | backoffice.pawzum.com | 3000 |

## Scope

### IaC changes (iac/)
- Add web-app, ^Gdmin, ackoffice container app resources to main.bicep L6 (Compute)
- Each app gets its own managed identity (wawkr-web-mi, wawkr-admin-mi, wawkr-backoffice-mi)
- Add Front Door origins and routes for each new domain
- Parameterize each app's image URI independently
- SRE alerting module updated for all 4 apps

### Deploy workflows (.github/workflows/)
- deploy-web-app.yml  -  independent deploy for web app container
- deploy-admin.yml  -  independent deploy for admin container  
- deploy-backoffice.yml  -  independent deploy for backoffice container
- Existing deploy-api.yml continues unchanged
- Each uses OIDC, unique concurrency group, cancel-in-progress: false for zero-downtime

### App scaffolding (^Gpps/)
- ^Gpps/admin/  -  new Next.js app for service admin interface (issue #179)
- ^Gpps/backoffice/  -  new Next.js app for internal operations
- Shared packages (packages/types, packages/tokens) consumed by all apps

### Database access
- All apps share the same PostgreSQL instance but connect through separate service connectors with least-privilege roles

### Rollout strategy
- Deploy new container apps alongside existing without removing the current single app
- Switch Front Door routing incrementally, verify, then decommission the old combined app

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] 4 container apps deployed independently in each environment
- [ ] Each app has its own deploy workflow triggered only by changes to its ^Gpps/<name>/ path
- [ ] Zero-downtime cutover: new apps live before old app removed
- [ ] Each app has its own managed identity with least-privilege RBAC
- [ ] SRE alerts cover all 4 apps
- [ ] Turborepo pipeline correctly builds only affected apps on change

issue.title: feat: service admin interface with instance management, federation, and white-label SaaS

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Feature

Build a service-level admin interface for managing a Pawzum deployment instance. This sits above the per-tenant admin (/settings/admin) and manages the full platform: users, content, settings, moderation, usage monitoring, and deployment instances.

## Scope

### Core UI sections (/service-admin)
- Dashboard: usage stats, active users, walk counts, storage, error rates
- Users: list all users, edit profiles, reset passwords, assign credits, suspend/ban
- Content: site-wide content overrides, feature flags, i18n strings
- Moderation: flag/remove bad walks, photos, captions, profiles
- Instances: manage deployment instances (regional, private, white-label)
- Analytics: telemetry, event counts, latency, usage over time

### Instance model
- Each deployment is an "instance" (global, regional, or private/white-label)
- Instances have their own domain, branding, user pool, feature flags
- Federation: instances can be linked so users/feeds are shared across boundaries
- Stamping: create a new private instance for a team (dog walkers, family, etc.)

### White-label SaaS
- Private instance = same app, own domain, own branding, own user pool
- Federation allows plugging one instance into another (shared walk feeds, user directory)
- Instance config stored in DB; IaC provisions the deployment separately

### API surface (/api/service-admin/*)
- Users CRUD with elevated bypass of tenant isolation
- Instances CRUD
- Analytics read endpoints
- Moderation actions (delete content, suspend user)
- Federation management (invite/accept/revoke peer)

### Access control
- New role: service-admin (superuser above owner)
- Proxy guards /service-admin/* to service-admin role only
- Separate layout with its own nav

## Schema additions
- instances table: id, name, type (global/regional/private/white-label), domain, ownerUserId, planTier, settings JSON, isActive, createdAt
- instanceMembers table: instanceId, userId, role, joinedAt
- instanceFederation table: instanceId, peerId, status (pending/active/suspended), createdAt

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] /service-admin only accessible to service-admin role
- [ ] User list with search, filter by role, suspend/unsuspend action
- [ ] Instance list with create/edit/delete
- [ ] Federation invite/accept/revoke flow
- [ ] Content override panel (same functionality as tenant admin but global scope)
- [ ] Moderation queue for flagged content
- [ ] Analytics dashboard with key metrics

issue.title: feat: multi-lingual JSON-backed content framework with admin overrides

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Feature

Add a multi-lingual, JSON-backed content framework so site copy can be managed
without redeployment. Content is stored in locale-namespaced JSON files with
optional DB overrides that admins can edit from the UI.

## Architecture

### Content layers (priority order)
1. DB overrides (admin UI editable, instant, no redeploy)
2. Locale JSON file  apps/web/content/{locale}/{namespace}.json
3. Fallback to en locale file
4. Hardcoded string as last resort

### Namespaces
- common   shared strings, buttons, errors
- nav      navigation labels (sidebar, public nav, footer)
- landing  landing page copy
- gallery  gallery page copy
- dashboard  dashboard section titles and stat labels
- walks    walk UI strings
- pets     pet UI strings
- settings settings page labels

### Schema
- contentOverrides table: locale, namespace, key (dot-notation), value, updatedBy, updatedAt
- userSettings.locale column (default en)

### API
- GET /api/public/content?locale=en&ns=landing  returns merged content, cached 5 min
- PUT /api/v1/admin/content  upsert override for locale+namespace+key

### Server helper  lib/content.ts
- getContent(namespace, locale)  reads JSON file + merges DB overrides
- t(content, dotKey, fallback)  safe dot-notation accessor

### Client hook  hooks/useContent.ts
- useContent(namespace, locale?)  SWR against /api/public/content
- returns { t, content, isLoading }

### Pages to update
- landing/page.tsx  switch to content
- gallery/page.tsx  switch to content
- Sidebar.tsx nav labels
- PublicFooter.tsx link labels
- settings/page.tsx labels

### Admin UI
- New Content Management panel in /settings/admin
- Namespace picker, key/value list, inline edit, save per key
- Shows default value from JSON file alongside the override field

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All landing page copy driven by content/en/landing.json
- [ ] Admin can override any key from /settings/admin without redeployment
- [ ] Adding content/es/ folder enables Spanish with zero code changes
- [ ] User language preference stored in userSettings.locale
- [ ] GET /api/public/content returns 304 with proper cache headers
- [ ] DB unavailable falls back to JSON file gracefully
- [ ] Audit log entry created on every admin content override

issue.title: bug(iac): DNS RBAC cross-RG deploy fails - GH Actions SP lacks roleAssignments/write on rg-core-services
issue.body:
## Root Cause

The GitHub Actions service principal (object id \70d600bd-...\) has Contributor on \wawkr-rg-dev\ but NOT on \g-core-services\. The \ront-door-dns-rbac\ Bicep module deploys cross-RG to \g-core-services\ and requires \Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write\  -  which requires Owner or User Access Administrator.

## Error

\\\
Authorization failed for template resource '...'. The client with object id '70d600bd-...'
does not have permission to perform action 'Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write'
at scope '.../resourceGroups/rg-core-services/providers/Microsoft.Network/dnsZones/pawzum.com/...'
\\\

## Fix Applied (commit 197ada3)

Added \deployDnsRbac bool = false\ parameter to \main.bicep\. The DNS RBAC module is now gated: only deployed when \deployDnsRbac=true\. Normal CI runs leave it false  -  the RBAC was applied manually on 2026-05-22.

## Long-term Fix Needed

Grant the GH Actions SP \User Access Administrator\ on \g-core-services\ (scoped to the DNS zone resource), then set \deployDnsRbac=true\ in the workflow to allow IaC to manage RBAC idempotently.

issue.title: bug(iac): PostgreSQL Flexible Server not supported as Service Linker target
issue.body:
## Root Cause

Azure Service Linker (\Microsoft.ServiceLinker/linkers\) does not support \MICROSOFT.DBFORPOSTGRESQL/FLEXIBLESERVERS\ as a target type. Attempting to create the connector fails with \TargetTypeNotSupported\.

## Error

\\\
TargetTypeNotSupported: Target resource type MICROSOFT.DBFORPOSTGRESQL/FLEXIBLESERVERS is not supported.
\\\

Seen in IaC deploy run 26318685638.

## Fix Applied (commit 197ada3)

Removed \postgresConnector\ resource and \postgresServerId\ param from \iac/backend/service-connectors.bicep\. PostgreSQL DB connectivity is handled via the \database-url\ Key Vault secret injected as a container app secret reference  -  no service linker needed.

## Status: Resolved

issue.title: feat: migrate from Azure AD B2C (EOL) to Microsoft Entra External ID (CIAM)

labels.name: sprint:s1
labels.description: Sprint S1 — Entra External ID + P0 Login fixes

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Summary

Azure AD B2C is end-of-life and must be replaced with Microsoft Entra External ID (CIAM). The B2C tenant \wawkrid\ was never actually provisioned (IaC gated behind \deployB2CTenant=false\), so this is a greenfield migration.

See **[ADR-001](../docs/adr/ADR-001-entra-external-id-replaces-b2c.md)** for the full architecture decision record.

## Why

- Azure AD B2C is EOL  -  no new features, retirement timeline announced
- Entra External ID is the official successor with native Bicep/ARM support
- Unified with the Entra ecosystem (same Graph API, conditional access, MFA, passwordless)
- Simpler integration: standard OIDC, no custom provider required in NextAuth

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] \iac/identity/external-id-tenant.bicep\ deployed and CIAM tenant active (\pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com\)
- [ ] App registration created in CIAM tenant with correct redirect URIs (\https://app.pawzum.com/api/auth/callback/microsoft-entra-id\)
- [ ] \^Guth.ts\ updated  -  \MicrosoftEntraID\ provider configured with \ciamlogin.com\ issuer
- [ ] \untime-config.ts\ updated  -  provider ID \^Gzure-ad-b2c\ replaced with \^[ntra-external-id\
- [ ] Env vars: \AUTH_EXTERNAL_ID_TENANT\, \AUTH_MICROSOFT_ENTRA_ID_ID\, \AUTH_MICROSOFT_ENTRA_ID_SECRET\ set in Key Vault + container app
- [ ] Old B2C env vars removed from container app + Key Vault
- [ ] Sign-up/sign-in user flow configured (email + social: Google, Apple)
- [ ] Login works end-to-end on \^Gpp.pawzum.com\
- [ ] \.env.example\ updated

## Implementation Waves

### Wave 1  -  IaC: Provision CIAM Tenant
- Use \iac/identity/external-id-tenant.bicep\ (already created)
- Resource: \Microsoft.AzureActiveDirectory/ciamDirectories@2023-01-18-preview\
- **Deployment scope: subscription**  -  use \^Gz deployment sub create\

### Wave 2  -  App Registration
- Create app in CIAM tenant with redirect URIs + scopes
- Store in Key Vault: \^[ntra-external-id-client-id\ / \^[ntra-external-id-client-secret\
- Set GitHub secrets: \ENTRA_EXTERNAL_ID_CLIENT_ID\, \ENTRA_EXTERNAL_ID_CLIENT_SECRET\

### Wave 3  -  Auth Integration
- \^Guth.ts\: configure \MicrosoftEntraID\ with CIAM issuer (\{tenant}.ciamlogin.com\)
- \untime-config.ts\: replace B2C provider definition with \^[ntra-external-id\
- Add \AUTH_EXTERNAL_ID_TENANT\ env var

### Wave 4  -  Cleanup
- Remove \AUTH_B2C_*\ env vars and Key Vault secrets
- Archive \B2C-tenant.bicep\
- Update \.env.example\

## IaC Snippet

\\\icep
// iac/identity/external-id-tenant.bicep
resource externalIdTenant 'Microsoft.AzureActiveDirectory/ciamDirectories@2023-01-18-preview' = {
  name: 'pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com'
  location: 'United States'
  properties: {
    displayName: 'Pawzum Identity'
    domainName: 'pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com'
  }
}
// OIDC Issuer: https://pawzumid.ciamlogin.com/pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com/v2.0
\\\

## Notes

- Tenant creator requires \Tenant Creator\ role in Entra ID (elevated  -  may require manual portal step)
- Verify \pawzumid\ name availability before deployment
- If Graph Bicep extension unavailable, use post-deploy Graph API script for app registration

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Summary

Azure AD B2C is end-of-life and must be replaced with Microsoft Entra External ID (CIAM). The B2C tenant \wawkrid\ was never actually provisioned (IaC gated behind \deployB2CTenant=false\), so this is a greenfield migration.

See **[ADR-001](../docs/adr/ADR-001-entra-external-id-replaces-b2c.md)** for the full architecture decision record.

## Why

- Azure AD B2C is EOL  -  no new features, retirement timeline announced
- Entra External ID is the official successor with native Bicep/ARM support
- Unified with the Entra ecosystem (same Graph API, conditional access, MFA, passwordless)
- Simpler integration: standard OIDC, no custom provider required in NextAuth

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] \iac/identity/external-id-tenant.bicep\ deployed and CIAM tenant active (\pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com\)
- [ ] App registration created in CIAM tenant with correct redirect URIs (\https://app.pawzum.com/api/auth/callback/microsoft-entra-id\)
- [ ] \^Guth.ts\ updated  -  \MicrosoftEntraID\ provider configured with \ciamlogin.com\ issuer
- [ ] \untime-config.ts\ updated  -  provider ID \^Gzure-ad-b2c\ replaced with \^[ntra-external-id\
- [ ] Env vars: \AUTH_EXTERNAL_ID_TENANT\, \AUTH_MICROSOFT_ENTRA_ID_ID\, \AUTH_MICROSOFT_ENTRA_ID_SECRET\ set in Key Vault + container app
- [ ] Old B2C env vars removed from container app + Key Vault
- [ ] Sign-up/sign-in user flow configured (email + social: Google, Apple)
- [ ] Login works end-to-end on \^Gpp.pawzum.com\
- [ ] \.env.example\ updated

## Implementation Waves

### Wave 1  -  IaC: Provision CIAM Tenant
- Use \iac/identity/external-id-tenant.bicep\ (already created)
- Resource: \Microsoft.AzureActiveDirectory/ciamDirectories@2023-01-18-preview\
- **Deployment scope: subscription**  -  use \^Gz deployment sub create\

### Wave 2  -  App Registration
- Create app in CIAM tenant with redirect URIs + scopes
- Store in Key Vault: \^[ntra-external-id-client-id\ / \^[ntra-external-id-client-secret\
- Set GitHub secrets: \ENTRA_EXTERNAL_ID_CLIENT_ID\, \ENTRA_EXTERNAL_ID_CLIENT_SECRET\

### Wave 3  -  Auth Integration
- \^Guth.ts\: configure \MicrosoftEntraID\ with CIAM issuer (\{tenant}.ciamlogin.com\)
- \untime-config.ts\: replace B2C provider definition with \^[ntra-external-id\
- Add \AUTH_EXTERNAL_ID_TENANT\ env var

### Wave 4  -  Cleanup
- Remove \AUTH_B2C_*\ env vars and Key Vault secrets
- Archive \B2C-tenant.bicep\
- Update \.env.example\

## IaC Snippet

\\\icep
// iac/identity/external-id-tenant.bicep
resource externalIdTenant 'Microsoft.AzureActiveDirectory/ciamDirectories@2023-01-18-preview' = {
  name: 'pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com'
  location: 'United States'
  properties: {
    displayName: 'Pawzum Identity'
    domainName: 'pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com'
  }
}
// OIDC Issuer: https://pawzumid.ciamlogin.com/pawzumid.onmicrosoft.com/v2.0
\\\

issue.title: Bug: Entra login returns DatabaseUnavailable on app.pawzum.com

labels.name: sprint:s1
labels.description: Sprint S1 — Entra External ID + P0 Login fixes

issue.body:
## Summary
Logging in with **Microsoft Entra** redirects to:
`https://app.pawzum.com/login?error=DatabaseUnavailable`

## Repro
1. Open `https://app.pawzum.com/login`
2. Click **Sign in with Microsoft**
3. Complete Entra auth flow
4. Observe redirect with `error=DatabaseUnavailable`

## Evidence
Container logs show DB failures during auth callbacks:
- `Error: Failed query: select ... from app_config ...`
- `SASL: SCRAM-SERVER-FIRST-MESSAGE: client password must be a string`
- `[auth] signIn callback failed`

## Likely root cause
Runtime database credentials are invalid/malformed for the active revision (`wawkr-api--0000082`), causing auth callback DB reads to fail.

## Acceptance criteria
- Entra login completes and lands authenticated session
- No `DatabaseUnavailable` redirect
- No `client password must be a string` DB errors in logs

issue.title: bug: all login providers broken - DatabaseUnavailable, B2C config, local auth config

labels.name: sprint:s1
labels.description: Sprint S1 — Entra External ID + P0 Login fixes

issue.body: All three login providers fail on app.pawzum.com: Entra returns DatabaseUnavailable (isAuthProviderEnabled hits DB before auth, DATABASE_URL is null/malformed in KV), B2C returns server config error (wawkrid tenant may not exist), Local returns Configuration error. Workaround: AUTH_BYPASS_USER=1 set on container. Fixes needed: 1) Fix database-url KV secret 2) Disable B2C until tenant provisioned 3) Fix local provider config 4) Harden isAuthProviderEnabled to not throw on DB unavailable.

issue.title: Bug: B2C sign-in fails with server configuration error

labels.name: sprint:s1
labels.description: Sprint S1 — Entra External ID + P0 Login fixes

issue.body:
## Summary
Logging in with **Pawzum Account (B2C)** fails with:
> There is a problem with the server configuration.

## Repro
1. Open `https://app.pawzum.com/login`
2. Click **Sign in with Pawzum**
3. Observe auth error page

## Evidence
Container logs include:
- `[auth][error] ... Authorization Server Metadata response (unexpected HTTP status code)`

## Current config context
`/api/auth/providers` now includes `azure-ad-b2c`, but metadata discovery for B2C issuer fails at runtime.

## Likely root cause
Incorrect B2C issuer inputs (tenant name and/or user flow) for `azure-ad-b2c` provider, or B2C policy/tenant endpoint not reachable for configured values.

## Acceptance criteria
- `azure-ad-b2c` sign-in starts successfully and redirects to the correct B2C hosted flow
- No auth metadata response errors in logs
- Callback to `https://app.pawzum.com/api/auth/callback/azure-ad-b2c` completes

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
## Work Item

**Sprint:** S1
**Wave:** 2
**Agent:** infrastructure-deploy
**Priority:** P1
**Parent issue:** #165

### Description
Create the app registration inside the newly-provisioned CIAM tenant and persist the client credentials to Azure Key Vault so the container app can consume them at runtime.

### Dependencies
- **Blocked by:** #166 (CIAM tenant must exist before app can be registered)
- **Blocks:** #167 (auth.ts integration needs client ID and secret from KV)

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] An app registration named \pawzum-web\ (or equivalent) exists in the CIAM tenant
- [ ] Redirect URI \https://app.pawzum.com/api/auth/callback/microsoft-entra-id\ is registered and saved
- [ ] Key Vault secret \^[ntra-external-id-client-id\ holds the new client ID
- [ ] Key Vault secret \^[ntra-external-id-client-secret\ holds a valid client secret (not expiring within 90 days)
- [ ] GitHub Actions secrets \ENTRA_EXTERNAL_ID_CLIENT_ID\ and \ENTRA_EXTERNAL_ID_CLIENT_SECRET\ are set
- [ ] Registration is automated (Bicep \Microsoft.Graph/applications\ resource OR post-deploy Graph API script)  -  no manual portal clicks

### Notes
- Two implementation options: Bicep \Microsoft.Graph/applications\ (preferred) or a post-deploy Graph API script
- If using Graph API script, store it under \scripts/register-ciam-app.sh\ and add it as a step in \deploy-iac.yml\
- Do NOT hard-code the tenant ID  -  read it from the Wave 1 deployment output

issue.title: [S1][Wave 3] Code: Wire auth.ts and runtime-config.ts to Entra External ID (CIAM)

labels.name: sprint:s1
labels.description: Sprint S1 — Entra External ID + P0 Login fixes

issue.body:
## Work Item

**Sprint:** S1
**Wave:** 3
**Agent:** backend-dev
**Priority:** P1
**Parent issue:** #165

### Description
Update the Next.js auth configuration to use the new CIAM tenant instead of Azure AD B2C. This is the code-level switch that makes login work end-to-end once the tenant and app registration are in place.

### Dependencies
- **Blocked by:** #167 (client ID/secret must be in KV before runtime-config can reference them), #166
- **Blocks:** #168 (B2C cleanup should only happen after this is verified working)

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] \^Gpps/web/src/auth.ts\ configures \MicrosoftEntraID\ provider with issuer URL \https://{tenant}.ciamlogin.com/{tenant}.onmicrosoft.com/v2.0\
- [ ] \^Gpps/web/src/lib/runtime-config.ts\ returns an \^[ntra-external-id\ provider entry (replaces \^Gzure-ad-b2c\)
- [ ] Environment variable \AUTH_EXTERNAL_ID_TENANT\ is defined in the container app's Bicep/env config and mapped to the CIAM tenant hostname
- [ ] Signing in with a Microsoft account on \https://app.pawzum.com\ completes the full OAuth flow without errors
- [ ] \/api/auth/session\ returns a valid session object after sign-in
- [ ] No \AUTH_B2C_*\ env vars are read by this code path (they may still exist but must not be required)

### Notes
- CIAM issuer format differs from regular Entra ID  -  use \{tenant}.ciamlogin.com\ not \login.microsoftonline.com\
- NextAuth v5 provider: \import MicrosoftEntraID from 'next-auth/providers/microsoft-entra-id'\
- \AUTH_EXTERNAL_ID_TENANT\ should be the short tenant name (e.g. \pawzumciam\), not the GUID
- Test with a guest/consumer Microsoft account, not an internal Entra ID account

issue.title: [S1][Wave 4] Cleanup: Remove Azure AD B2C config, secrets, and IaC after CIAM cutover

labels.name: sprint:s1
labels.description: Sprint S1 — Entra External ID + P0 Login fixes

issue.body:
## Work Item

**Sprint:** S1
**Wave:** 4
**Agent:** backend-dev
**Priority:** P1
**Parent issue:** #165

### Description
Remove all B2C-specific configuration now that CIAM is live and verified. This prevents the dead B2C config from confusing future contributors and eliminates the stale secrets from the Key Vault.

### Dependencies
- **Blocked by:** #167 (CIAM integration must be verified end-to-end before removing B2C fallback)
- **Blocks:** nothing (terminal wave for this epic)

### Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] \AUTH_B2C_CLIENT_ID\, \AUTH_B2C_CLIENT_SECRET\, \AUTH_B2C_TENANT_NAME\ are removed from container app env config and Bicep
- [ ] Key Vault secrets \B2C-client-id\, \B2C-client-secret\, \B2C-tenant-name\ are deleted (or flagged for manual deletion with a comment)
- [ ] \iac/identity/b2c-tenant.bicep\ is archived (moved to \iac/identity/archived/\) or gated behind a \deployB2c\ parameter defaulting to \alse\
- [ ] \.env.example\ is updated to show \AUTH_EXTERNAL_ID_TENANT\ and remove all \AUTH_B2C_*\ keys
- [ ] A comment is added to \iac/identity/archived/b2c-tenant.bicep\ (or PR description) explaining when and why it was archived
- [ ] CI passes (no references to removed B2C env vars in any active code path)

### Notes
- Do NOT delete the B2C tenant itself from Azure yet  -  keep it for 30 days in case rollback is needed
- Issues #125, #156, #157 can be closed once this wave is merged

issue.title: bug: PostgreSQL service connector missing from IaC - no private link binding for DB

labels.name: sprint:s1
labels.description: Sprint S1 — Entra External ID + P0 Login fixes

issue.body:
## Summary
\iac/backend/service-connectors.bicep\ defines service linkers for Cosmos, Storage, Key Vault, and App Config  -  but **PostgreSQL is completely absent**. The container app has no Service Connector to \wawkr-pg-dev\.

## Current connectors (verified via az CLI)
- cosmos_private_mi Γ£ô
- storage_private_mi Γ£ô
- keyvault_private_mi Γ£ô
- appconfig_private_mi Γ£ô
- **postgres_private_mi Γ£ù MISSING**

## Impact
- No managed service binding between \wawkr-api\ container app and \wawkr-pg-dev\
- DB connection relies entirely on password in \database-url\ KV secret
- If KV secret has empty/wrong password ΓåÆ SASL error ΓåÆ all DB-dependent routes fail
- LOGIN BROKEN: \/api/public/auth-providers\ 500s ΓåÆ login page cannot load providers

## Root Cause Chain
\database-url\ KV secret password is null/empty at runtime ΓåÆ \pg-pool.connect\ fails with \PostgreSQL error (code: UNKNOWN)\ ΓåÆ \getRuntimeAuthProviderConfig()\ throws ΓåÆ \/api/public/auth-providers\ returns 500 ΓåÆ login page broken.

## Fix
1. Add \postgresConnector\ resource to \service-connectors.bicep\ (private link, user-assigned MI)
2. Pass \postgresServerId: postgres.outputs.serverId\ in \main.bicep\
3. Verify/fix \database-url\ KV secret has correct password from \POSTGRES_ADMIN_PASSWORD\

IaC fix committed in this PR.

issue.title: bug: /api/public/auth-providers crashes with 500 when DB unavailable — should read from env vars
issue.body:
## RCA (from App Insights trace)

\GET /api/public/auth-providers\ → \getRuntimeAuthProviderConfig()\ → unconditional DB query → pg.connect fails → 500.

Trace:
- \pg-pool.connect\ span: target \wawkr-pg-dev.postgres.database.azure.com|pawzome\, success=False
- Exception: \PostgreSQL error of type 'Error' occurred (code: UNKNOWN)\
- Query: \select id, auth_provider_toggles from app_config where id = 'global'\

## Root Cause
\getRuntimeAuthProviderConfig()\ in \^Gpps/web/src/lib/runtime-config.ts\ always hits the DB to load admin toggle overrides before computing provider availability. When the DB connection fails (DATABASE_URL secret empty/malformed), the entire function throws — crashing the public auth-providers endpoint that the login page depends on.

The DB row is only needed for **admin-managed overrides**. All provider availability is already expressible via env vars (\AUTH_PROVIDER_LOCAL_ENABLED\, \AUTH_MICROSOFT_ENTRA_ID_ID\, etc.) which are all set on the container app.

## Impact
- Login page cannot load provider list → all login buttons fail to render
- Every sign-in attempt fails with \DatabaseUnavailable\
- Cascades to: Entra sign-in, B2C sign-in, local credentials — all broken

## Fix
Wrap the DB query in try/catch. On failure, use \storedToggles = {}\ (empty) so env-var toggles drive everything. When DB recovers, admin overrides automatically resume.

Fixed in commit referencing this issue.

issue.title: bug: Front Door DNS RBAC was assigned to wrong zone (pawzo.me instead of pawzum.com)
issue.body:
## Summary
Azure Front Door's system-assigned managed identity (\wawkr-fd-dev\) had \Reader\ role on the old \pawzo.me\ DNS zone instead of \pawzum.com\. This prevented AFD from auto-validating TLS certificates and custom domain ownership for the new domain.

## Root Cause
- During the Pawzum domain migration, the Front Door DNS RBAC was manually bootstrapped pointing to \pawzo.me\
- The \ ront-door-dns-rbac.bicep\ module existed in IaC but was **not wired into \main.bicep\** — the comment said 'handled by bootstrap'
- When the domain was migrated to \pawzum.com\, the RBAC was never updated

## Impact
- AFD could not auto-validate \pawzum.com\ custom domain certificates
- TLS cert provisioning/renewal was broken for all \pawzum.com\ subdomains

## Fix
**Live hotfix (commit \9a62ba9\):**

issue.title: bug: PostgreSQL service connector missing from IaC - no private link binding for DB

labels.name: sprint:s1
labels.description: Sprint S1 — Entra External ID + P0 Login fixes

issue.body:
## Summary
\iac/backend/service-connectors.bicep\ defines service linkers for Cosmos, Storage, Key Vault, and App Config  -  but **PostgreSQL is completely absent**. The container app has no Service Connector to \wawkr-pg-dev\.

## Current connectors (verified via az CLI)
- cosmos_private_mi Γ£ô
- storage_private_mi Γ£ô
- keyvault_private_mi Γ£ô
- appconfig_private_mi Γ£ô
- **postgres_private_mi Γ£ù MISSING**

## Impact
- No managed service binding between \wawkr-api\ container app and \wawkr-pg-dev\
- DB connection relies entirely on password in \database-url\ KV secret
- If KV secret has empty/wrong password ΓåÆ SASL error ΓåÆ all DB-dependent routes fail
- LOGIN BROKEN: \/api/public/auth-providers\ 500s ΓåÆ login page cannot load providers

## Root Cause Chain
\database-url\ KV secret password is null/empty at runtime ΓåÆ \pg-pool.connect\ fails with \PostgreSQL error (code: UNKNOWN)\ ΓåÆ \getRuntimeAuthProviderConfig()\ throws ΓåÆ \/api/public/auth-providers\ returns 500 ΓåÆ login page broken.

## Fix
1. Add \postgresConnector\ resource to \service-connectors.bicep\ (private link, user-assigned MI)
2. Pass \postgresServerId: postgres.outputs.serverId\ in \main.bicep\
3. Verify/fix \database-url\ KV secret has correct password from \POSTGRES_ADMIN_PASSWORD\

IaC fix committed in this PR.

issue.title: bug: /api/public/auth-providers crashes with 500 when DB unavailable — should read from env vars
issue.body:
## RCA (from App Insights trace)

\GET /api/public/auth-providers\ → \getRuntimeAuthProviderConfig()\ → unconditional DB query → pg.connect fails → 500.

Trace:
- \pg-pool.connect\ span: target \wawkr-pg-dev.postgres.database.azure.com|pawzome\, success=False
- Exception: \PostgreSQL error of type 'Error' occurred (code: UNKNOWN)\
- Query: \select id, auth_provider_toggles from app_config where id = 'global'\

## Root Cause
\getRuntimeAuthProviderConfig()\ in \^Gpps/web/src/lib/runtime-config.ts\ always hits the DB to load admin toggle overrides before computing provider availability. When the DB connection fails (DATABASE_URL secret empty/malformed), the entire function throws — crashing the public auth-providers endpoint that the login page depends on.

The DB row is only needed for **admin-managed overrides**. All provider availability is already expressible via env vars (\AUTH_PROVIDER_LOCAL_ENABLED\, \AUTH_MICROSOFT_ENTRA_ID_ID\, etc.) which are all set on the container app.

## Impact
- Login page cannot load provider list → all login buttons fail to render
- Every sign-in attempt fails with \DatabaseUnavailable\
- Cascades to: Entra sign-in, B2C sign-in, local credentials — all broken

## Fix
Wrap the DB query in try/catch. On failure, use \storedToggles = {}\ (empty) so env-var toggles drive everything. When DB recovers, admin overrides automatically resume.

Fixed in commit referencing this issue.

When the DB connection fails (DATABASE_URL secret empty/malformed), the entire function throws — crashing the public auth-providers endpoint that the login page depends on.

The DB row is only needed for **admin-managed overrides**. All provider availability is already expressible via env vars (\AUTH_PROVIDER_LOCAL_ENABLED\, \AUTH_MICROSOFT_ENTRA_ID_ID\, etc.) which are all set on the container app.

## Impact
- Login page cannot load provider list → all login buttons fail to render
- Every sign-in attempt fails with \DatabaseUnavailable\
- Cascades to: Entra sign-in, B2C sign-in, local credentials — all broken

## Fix
Wrap the DB query in try/catch. On failure, use \storedToggles = {}\ (empty) so env-var toggles drive everything. When DB recovers, admin overrides automatically resume.

Fixed in commit referencing this issue.

issue.title: bug: Front Door DNS RBAC was assigned to wrong zone (pawzo.me instead of pawzum.com)
issue.body:
## Summary
Azure Front Door's system-assigned managed identity (\wawkr-fd-dev\) had \Reader\ role on the old \pawzo.me\ DNS zone instead of \pawzum.com\. This prevented AFD from auto-validating TLS certificates and custom domain ownership for the new domain.

## Root Cause
- During the Pawzum domain migration, the Front Door DNS RBAC was manually bootstrapped pointing to \pawzo.me\
- The \ ront-door-dns-rbac.bicep\ module existed in IaC but was **not wired into \main.bicep\** — the comment said 'handled by bootstrap'
- When the domain was migrated to \pawzum.com\, the RBAC was never updated

## Impact
- AFD could not auto-validate \pawzum.com\ custom domain certificates
- TLS cert provisioning/renewal was broken for all \pawzum.com\ subdomains

## Fix
**Live hotfix (commit \9a62ba9\):**
- Removed \Reader\ from \pawzo.me\ zone (assignment \16753dbc\)
- Granted \Reader\ on \pawzum.com\ zone for FD principal \ d01e495-dee6-40b4-9497-2709c09fbb18\

**IaC fix (commit \9a62ba9\):**
- Added \dnsZoneResourceGroup\ param to \iac/main.bicep\
- Wired \ ront-door-dns-rbac.bicep\ as a cross-RG module scoped to \dnsZoneResourceGroup\
- RBAC is now fully managed by IaC — no more manual bootstrap required

**Workflow fix (commit \^G111469\):**
- Added \dnsZoneResourceGroup\ param to both \what-if\ and \deploy\ steps in \deploy-iac.yml\
- Set \DNS_ZONE_RESOURCE_GROUP=rg-core-services\ GitHub repo variable

## Lesson
Live RBAC grants that are not in IaC will drift on the next deployment. All identity/RBAC assignments must be managed as code.

issue.title: refactor(bootstrap): strip RG/RBAC/deploy — IaC workflow owns infra
issue.body:
## Summary

Bootstrap `--cloud` was running RG creation, RBAC, ACR wiring, and an inline Bicep deploy.
This caused chicken-egg failures and duplicated what the IaC workflow already owns.

## Changes

`bootstrap.ps1` / `bootstrap.sh` now run 5 steps (was 8):
1. Azure AD app registration
2. Service principal
3. OIDC federated credentials
4. GitHub repository variables (naming conventions only)
5. GitHub production environment

Removed: step 4 (RG create), step 5 (RBAC), step 8 (inline Bicep deploy)

New scripts:
- `scripts/deploy-iac-workflow.ps1` - triggers gh workflow run Deploy Infrastructure
- `scripts/deploy-iac-workflow.sh` - bash equivalent

Fixes the scripts/iac/main.bicep not found error.
Closes #143

issue.title: Split bootstrap: minimal auth wiring + separate IaC deploy trigger
issue.body:
## What changed
- stripped cloud bootstrap to bare minimum (OIDC app/SP + GitHub secrets + production environment)
- removed RG creation, RBAC resource assignments, ACR wiring, and inline Bicep deploy from bootstrap
- made default bootstrap path local-only to avoid cloud side effects
- added separate scripts to trigger the IaC deployment workflow:
  - scripts/deploy-iac-workflow.ps1
  - scripts/deploy-iac-workflow.sh

## Why
Avoid bootstrap chicken-and-egg failures. IaC workflow now owns infrastructure provisioning lifecycle, while bootstrap only prepares auth wiring.

issue.title: sprint: execution plan (auth and reliability)
issue.body:
## Goal
Restore production auth/reliability (DB + sign-in + CI + walk history crash).

## Scope
### Committed
- #126
- #125
- #131
- #127
- #6
- #132

### Stretch
- #134
- #135
- #129

### Deferred
- #133
- #137
- #138
- #139
- #140
- #141
- #5

## Wave plan
### Wave 1 (stabilize foundations)
- #126 (DB baseline + connectivity)
- #125 (auth/sign-in path restore)
- #131 (CI reliability gates)

### Wave 2 (user-critical reliability)
- #127 (walk history crash fix)
- #6 (cross-cutting auth/reliability follow-through)
- #132 (hardening + validation)

### Wave 3 (stretch if capacity remains)
- #134, #135, #129

## Critical path
#126 -> #125 -> #131 -> #127 -> #132
(With #6 tracked in parallel where it does not block the chain.)

## Ownership split
- **Platform/Auth**: #126, #125, #6
- **CI/DevEx**: #131
- **Product reliability**: #127, #132
- **Stretch owners**: #134, #135, #129 (assigned once committed scope is green)

## Risks / mitigations
- **DB/auth sequencing risk**: lock order to Wave 1 and require smoke verification before Wave 2.
- **CI flakiness masking regressions**: enforce stable CI pass criteria before merging Wave 2 fixes.
- **Crash fix regressions**: add targeted reproduction + validation checklist on #127/#132.
- **Capacity squeeze from migration work**: keep #5 explicitly deferred and re-evaluate at sprint midpoint.

issue.title: feat: Add B2C provider configuration bootstrap script

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #147.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/147
Original state: OPEN
Original created: 05/20/2026 01:23:37
Original updated: 05/20/2026 01:23:37

---

## Summary

Created `scripts/bootstrap-b2c.ps1` and `scripts/bootstrap-b2c.sh` to automate Azure AD B2C post-provisioning steps that were previously manual.

## What the script does

1. Registers a web app in the B2C tenant with NextAuth callback URIs
2. Creates the `B2C_1_signup_signin` user flow via Graph API
3. Generates a client secret
4. Sets `B2C_CLIENT_ID` and `B2C_CLIENT_SECRET` in GitHub Secrets
5. Optionally adds social identity providers (Google, Facebook, Apple)

## Usage

```bash
# After running bootstrap.ps1 -Mode Cloud and Deploy Infrastructure:
./scripts/bootstrap-b2c.ps1
./scripts/bootstrap-b2c.sh

# With social providers:
./scripts/bootstrap-b2c.ps1 -AddGoogle -AddFacebook
./scripts/bootstrap-b2c.sh --add-google --add-facebook
```

## Implementation

- PR #146 includes the script
- README updated with Cloud Setup & Identity section
- bootstrap.ps1 updated to reference new script instead of manual comments

## Related Issues

- #141 (Anonymous site requires sign-in)
- #142 (Microsoft sign-in fails)
- #145 (Social providers fail)

## Goal
Restore production auth/reliability (DB + sign-in + CI + walk history crash).

## Scope
### Committed
- #126

- #132

### Stretch
- #134
- #135
- #129

### Deferred
- #133
- #137

- #140
- #141

## Wave plan
### Wave 1 (stabilize foundations)
- #126 (DB baseline + connectivity)

- #131 (CI reliability gates)

### Wave 2 (user-critical reliability)

issue.title: bug: Site outage ΓÇö database tables missing (migrations never ran)
issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #148.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/148
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/20/2026 02:17:13
Original updated: 05/20/2026 02:38:36

---

## Summary
The production site is down because the database has no tables. The app connects to Postgres successfully but queries fail with:

``
error: relation "app_config" does not exist
``

## Root Cause
The Deploy Database workflow (issue #139) has been repeatedly cancelled, so migrations were never applied to the Postgres Flexible Server.

## Evidence
- Health endpoint: `database.connected: false`
- Container App logs: `Failed query: select ... from "app_config" ... [cause]: error: relation "app_config" does not exist`
- Private endpoint is healthy (Approved, DNS resolving correctly)
- Key Vault secret `database-url` is present and referenced by the Container App

## Resolution
Run the Deploy Database workflow successfully (or run migrations manually via `pnpm --filter @wawkr/web db:migrate`) to create the schema.

## Impact
- **Severity:** Critical ΓÇö full site outage
- **Affected:** All authenticated routes, all data-dependent pages

## Related
- #139 (Deploy Database workflow cancelled)

issue.body:

Original state: OPEN

Original updated: 05/20/2026 01:23:37

---

## Summary

Created `scripts/bootstrap-b2c.ps1` and `scripts/bootstrap-b2c.sh` to automate Azure AD B2C post-provisioning steps that were previously manual.

## What the script does

1. Registers a web app in the B2C tenant with NextAuth callback URIs
2. Creates the `B2C_1_signup_signin` user flow via Graph API
3. Generates a client secret
4. Sets `B2C_CLIENT_ID` and `B2C_CLIENT_SECRET` in GitHub Secrets
5. Optionally adds social identity providers (Google, Facebook, Apple)

## Usage

```bash
# After running bootstrap.ps1 -Mode Cloud and Deploy Infrastructure:
./scripts/bootstrap-b2c.ps1
./scripts/bootstrap-b2c.sh

# With social providers:
./scripts/bootstrap-b2c.ps1 -AddGoogle -AddFacebook
./scripts/bootstrap-b2c.sh --add-google --add-facebook
```

## Implementation

- PR #146 includes the script
- README updated with Cloud Setup & Identity section
- bootstrap.ps1 updated to reference new script instead of manual comments

## Related Issues

- #141 (Anonymous site requires sign-in)
- #142 (Microsoft sign-in fails)
- #145 (Social providers fail)

issue.title: fix(auth): CSRF, rate limit, broken logo, multi-tenant login
issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #133.

Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/20/2026 00:21:18
Original updated: 05/20/2026 00:21:44

---

## Bug
- Logo broken in production (Dockerfile missing public/ folder COPY)
- MissingCSRF error on login (trustHost not set behind Front Door)
- Rate limit too aggressive (10 req/min blocks normal login flows)
- Access Denied when DB unavailable (signIn callback crashes without try/catch)
- Microsoft login restricted to single tenant (app reg was single-tenant)

## Fix Applied
- Dockerfile: added COPY public/ for static assets
- auth.ts: trustHost: true, try/catch on signIn, prompt: select_account
- proxy.ts: rate limit 10 -> 60 req/min
- Azure: az ad app update --sign-in-audience AzureADandPersonalMicrosoftAccount
- Commit: 0ddee72

issue.title: feat(data): Migrate from SQLite to Azure Cosmos DB / Postgres Flexible Server

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #129.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/129
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 19:04:03
Original updated: 05/19/2026 19:34:41

---

## Problem

The web app currently uses SQLite via better-sqlite3 + Drizzle ORM with a local file (wawkr.db). This is fundamentally incompatible with production:

- **Ephemeral filesystem**: Container Apps don't persist file state across restarts/replicas
- **No shared state**: Multiple replicas can't share a SQLite file
- **No backups**: No point-in-time recovery or geo-redundancy

## Current State

- apps/web/src/db/index.ts uses better-sqlite3 with local file
- apps/web/src/db/schema.ts uses Drizzle ORM SQLite dialect (sqliteTable)
- IaC already provisions Cosmos DB (SQL API) with a service connector, but app code never uses it

## Recommendation

**Option B (Postgres Flexible Server)** - Drizzle ORM migration path is clean (sqliteTable to pgTable), and Postgres is the standard relational choice for Next.js apps.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Add Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server to IaC
- [ ] Migrate Drizzle schema from sqliteTable to pgTable
- [ ] Update apps/web/src/db/index.ts to use drizzle-orm/node-postgres
- [ ] Connection string via App Configuration or service connector
- [ ] Seed script works against Postgres
- [ ] All tests pass with Postgres backend
- [ ] Remove better-sqlite3 dependency

issue.title: feat(config): implement tenant config via App Configuration

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #128.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/128
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 17:24:44
Original updated: 05/19/2026 18:31:29

---

Move tenant ID configuration from IaC params to Azure App Configuration for runtime flexibility.

## Design (from #116)
- App Config key: 'auth:tenant-id' with label per environment
- App Config feature flag: 'tenant-mode' (single/multi/personal)
- TenantService reads config at app startup
- Fallback to env var TENANT_ID for backward compatibility

## Scope
- Create TenantService in apps/web/src/lib/tenant.ts
- Read tenant-id from App Config (via existing service connector)
- Seed App Config with default tenant-id in bootstrap
- Update auth.ts to use TenantService for issuer URL
- Feature flag for multi-tenant mode (future, just wire the flag)

## Acceptance Criteria
- App reads tenant ID from App Config
- Changing tenant-id in App Config takes effect without redeploy
- Bootstrap seeds the default tenant config
- Existing single-tenant flow unchanged

Closes: #116

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #127.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/127
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 17:24:42
Original updated: 05/19/2026 18:26:10

Deploy the landing page and activate custom domain bindings on Front Door.

## Scope
- Activate custom domains: pawzo.me, www.pawzo.me, app.pawzo.me, api.pawzo.me, admin.pawzo.me
- Configure Front Door routing rules (root -> landing, app.* -> container app)
- TLS certificates via Front Door managed certs
- Update AUTH_URL to app.pawzo.me

- https://pawzo.me shows landing page
- https://app.pawzo.me shows the app (login)
- https://api.pawzo.me/health returns 200
- TLS valid on all domains
- Auth flow works end-to-end with new domain

issue.title: design: Landing page + app separation architecture (subdomain vs subpath)

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #120.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/120
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 15:07:57
Original updated: 05/19/2026 17:16:10

---

## Context
WawkR needs a public landing page (marketing, features, pricing) separate from the authenticated app. Two options evaluated:

## Decision: Subdomain `app.wawkr.tld` (recommended)

### Rationale
1. **Security isolation** ΓÇö auth cookies scoped to `app.` subdomain, landing page has zero attack surface
2. **Independent deploys** ΓÇö marketing ships without touching app pipeline
3. **Simpler Next.js** ΓÇö no `basePath: '/app'` which complicates assets, images, auth callbacks
4. **Front Door routing** ΓÇö already have `wawkr-fd-dev`; add second origin group for landing
5. **Mobile deep links** ΓÇö `app.wawkr.tld/walks/123` maps cleanly

### Implementation Plan
- [ ] Landing page: Static site (Astro or Next.js export) on Azure Static Web Apps
- [ ] DNS: `wawkr.tld` ΓåÆ Static Web App, `app.wawkr.tld` ΓåÆ Container App (via Front Door)
- [ ] Update AUTH_URL to `https://app.wawkr.tld`
- [ ] Update Entra ID app registration redirect URIs
- [ ] Front Door: two endpoint/origin groups (landing + app)
- [ ] Landing page content: hero, features, screenshots, CTA ΓåÆ sign in

### Alternative Considered
Subpath `/app/` ΓÇö rejected due to coupled deploys, basePath complexity, shared cookie scope.

issue.title: bug: Privacy telemetry toggle defaults to Enabled ΓÇö should be Disabled
issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #119.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/119
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 14:59:16
Original updated: 05/19/2026 15:01:20

---

## Summary
The privacy setting defaults to Enabled. Per privacy-by-design, telemetry opt-in should default to Disabled.

issue.title: bug: Data pack loading fails ΓÇö EACCES on container filesystem fallback
issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #118.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/118
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 14:59:14
Original updated: 05/19/2026 17:15:33

---

## Summary
The Load Data Pack button on /settings fails with:
``
EACCES: permission denied, open '/app/apps/web/public/uploads/demo-avatar-demo-user-marcus.jpg'
``

## Root Cause
`blob-storage.ts` falls back to writing to `public/uploads/` when `AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING` is not set. In the container, the filesystem is read-only.

## Fix
Provision Azure Blob Storage account via IaC and set `AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING` on the container app.

issue.title: feat(auth): add local/credentials auth option for development and self-hosted

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #117.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/117
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 14:06:13
Original updated: 05/19/2026 17:15:36

---

## Problem

No local authentication option exists. Users who want to run WawkR self-hosted or in development without OAuth provider setup have no way to sign in.

## Expected

A local credentials-based auth provider (username/password) that can be enabled via feature flag for:
- Local development without OAuth setup
- Self-hosted deployments without cloud identity providers
- Demo/staging environments

## Design

1. **Provider**: Auth.js Credentials provider with bcrypt-hashed passwords
2. **Storage**: Users table with \passwordHash\ column (nullable ΓÇö only set for local auth users)
3. **Gating**: Feature flag \^Guth.local-credentials\ (disabled in production by default)
4. **Registration**: Simple signup form when local auth is enabled
5. **Security**:
   - Rate limiting on login attempts
   - Password complexity requirements
   - Account lockout after N failed attempts
   - Feature flag MUST be explicitly enabled (never auto-enabled in prod)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Credentials provider added to \^Guth.ts\ (conditional on feature flag)
- [ ] User registration endpoint (\/api/auth/register\)
- [ ] Password hashing with bcrypt (cost factor 12+)
- [ ] Login rate limiting (max 5 attempts per minute)
- [ ] Feature flag \^Guth.local-credentials\ in App Configuration (default: false)
- [ ] Works in dev without any external provider configured
- [ ] Disabled by default in production

issue.title: design(auth): tenant ID should come from App Configuration, not IaC params ΓÇö support single/multi-tenant

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #116.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/116
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 14:06:11
Original updated: 05/19/2026 18:31:20

---

## Problem

The OIDC issuer tenant ID is currently passed as an IaC parameter (\	enantId\) and baked into the container app env var (\AZURE_TENANT_ID\). This is wrong ΓÇö tenant configuration is a runtime concern, not an infrastructure concern.

## Expected

Tenant ID (and issuer URLs) should be stored in **App Configuration** so they can be changed without redeployment. This also enables:
- **Single-tenant mode**: issuer locked to one tenant ID
- **Multi-tenant mode**: issuer set to \common\ with dynamic issuer validation
- Runtime switching between modes via feature flag

## Design Considerations

1. App Configuration settings:
   - \^Guth:tenant-mode\ ΓåÆ \single\ | \multi\
   - \^Guth:tenant-id\ ΓåÆ specific tenant ID (for single-tenant)
   - \^Guth:org-issuer\ ΓåÆ computed from mode + tenant-id
   - \^Guth:personal-issuer\ ΓåÆ \consumers/v2.0\ (always)

2. Multi-tenant requires custom issuer validation in Auth.js callback (compare token issuer against allowed tenants list)

3. Feature flag: \^Guth.multi-tenant\ to toggle between modes

4. Remove \	enantId\ from IaC params once App Config handles it

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Design doc: single vs multi-tenant auth architecture
- [ ] App Configuration settings for tenant mode
- [ ] Auth.ts reads issuer from App Config at startup (with env var fallback)
- [ ] Feature flag gates multi-tenant behavior
- [ ] Remove \	enantId\ IaC param once migration complete

issue.title: bug(auth): Only Microsoft Entra ID provider active ΓÇö Google, Apple, Email (local) not configured
issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #115.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/115
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 13:55:19
Original updated: 05/19/2026 17:13:39

---

## Problem

Only Microsoft (Work/School) and Microsoft (Personal) auth providers are active. The app supports 5 providers but 3 are missing credentials:

| Provider | Status | Missing |
|----------|--------|---------|
| Microsoft (Work or School) | Γ£à Active | ΓÇö |
| Microsoft (Personal) | Γ£à Active | ΓÇö |
| Google | Γ¥î Inactive | \GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID\, \GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET\ |
| Apple | Γ¥î Inactive | \APPLE_CLIENT_ID\, \APPLE_CLIENT_SECRET\ |
| Email (local) | Γ¥î Inactive | \EMAIL_SERVER\, \EMAIL_FROM\ |

## Code References

- \src/auth.ts\ ΓÇö Provider registration (conditional on env vars)
- \src/lib/runtime-config.ts\ ΓÇö Provider availability checks

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Google OAuth app registration created, credentials stored in KV
- [ ] Apple Sign-In service ID created, credentials stored in KV
- [ ] Email provider configured (SMTP server + from address in KV)
- [ ] All providers show as available in \/api/public/auth-providers\
- [ ] Container app env vars wired from KV for each provider
- [ ] Bootstrap scripts updated to create Google/Apple app registrations

## Notes

- Google requires a Google Cloud project with OAuth consent screen configured
- Apple requires an Apple Developer account with Sign in with Apple service ID
- Email requires an SMTP relay (e.g. Azure Communication Services, SendGrid, or Office 365 SMTP)
- Each provider's credentials should follow the same KV secret pattern as Microsoft

- Each provider's credentials should follow the same KV secret pattern as Microsoft

issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #114.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/114
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 08:46:42
Original updated: 05/19/2026 09:58:20

---

## Problem

Code analysis reveals the app has working SDK integration (\src/lib/app-configuration.ts\, \src/instrumentation.ts\) but App Configuration has **zero key-values provisioned**. Multiple code paths depend on settings and feature flags that don't exist.

## Required Feature Flags (consumed via \isFeatureEnabled()\)

| Flag Key | Used In | Purpose | Default |
|----------|---------|---------|---------|
| \web.stats-api\ | \^Gpi/v1/stats/route.ts\ | Gates the stats/dashboard API | \	rue\ |
| \live-tracking\ | walk tracking flow | Real-time GPS walk tracking | \	rue\ |
| \	eam-invites\ | team invite flow | Team member invite feature | \	rue\ |
| \premium-walks\ | premium features | Extended routes, pet camera | \ alse\ |
| \offline-mode\ | offline sync | Walk recording without connectivity | \ alse\ |

## Required Settings (consumed via \getRuntimeSetting()\)

| Key | Purpose | Suggested Value |
|-----|---------|-----------------|
| \walk:max-duration-minutes\ | Max walk length before auto-stop | \180\ |
| \walk:max-pets-per-walk\ | Pet limit per walk session | \6\ |
| \	eam:max-members\ | Max caretakers per team | \10\ |

## Auth Provider Env Toggles (consumed via \untime-config.ts\)

These are read from env vars (not App Config) but should be documented:
- \AUTH_PROVIDER_GOOGLE_ENABLED\
- \AUTH_PROVIDER_APPLE_ENABLED\
- \AUTH_PROVIDER_MICROSOFT_ORG_ENABLED\
- \AUTH_PROVIDER_MICROSOFT_PERSONAL_ENABLED\
- \AUTH_PROVIDER_EMAIL_ENABLED\

## App Insights Integration

\src/lib/telemetry.ts\ + \src/instrumentation.ts\ are wired ΓÇö \initTelemetry()\ is called on server startup. Needs \APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING\ env var (already deployed via KV ref). Verify telemetry is actually flowing in portal.

## Current IaC State

Bicep now provisions feature flags and settings in \iac/config/app-configuration.bicep\ (committed but not yet deployed with the \web.stats-api\ flag). Missing: \web.stats-api\ flag which is the only one actively gating production behavior today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All feature flags listed above exist in App Configuration with correct labels
- [ ] All runtime settings listed above exist in App Configuration
- [ ] \/api/health\ endpoint shows \^GppConfig.connected: true\ with correct flag values
- [ ] \web.stats-api\ flag added to IaC (currently missing ΓÇö will cause stats endpoint to return 503)
- [ ] App Insights telemetry confirmed flowing in Azure Portal (Live Metrics or Transaction Search)

issue.title: bug(app): Feature flags not provisioned in App Configuration
issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #113.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/113
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 08:42:37
Original updated: 05/19/2026 09:58:18

---

## Problem

Azure App Configuration has no feature flags defined. The app needs feature flags for progressive rollout of features (e.g., live tracking, team invites, premium features).

## Expected

- Feature flags defined in App Configuration with proper labels
- App reads feature flags at runtime via the App Config SDK
- Flags can be toggled without redeployment

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Core feature flags defined in App Configuration (via IaC or bootstrap)
- [ ] Feature flag values seeded: e.g. \live-tracking\, \	eam-invites\, \premium-walks\
- [ ] App evaluates feature flags at runtime
- [ ] Flags use \.appconfig.featureflag/\ key prefix (standard convention)

## Learnings

- App Configuration feature flags use a specific key prefix and JSON format
- Can be provisioned via Bicep (\Microsoft.AppConfiguration/configurationStores/keyValues\) or CLI

issue.title: bug(app): Application Insights not connected ΓÇö no telemetry flowing
issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #112.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/112
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 08:42:35
Original updated: 05/19/2026 09:58:16

---

## Problem

App Insights resource exists and \APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING\ is set as an env var, but the application does not have the App Insights SDK instrumented. No telemetry (requests, exceptions, dependencies, traces) is flowing.

## Expected

- Application Insights SDK initialized on app startup
- Request telemetry, dependency tracking, exception logging active
- Custom events/metrics available for walk tracking, auth flows

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] App Insights SDK integrated (\^Gpplicationinsights\ or \@azure/monitor-opentelemetry\)
- [ ] Verify telemetry appears in Azure Portal > App Insights > Live Metrics
- [ ] Request tracking, dependency tracking, exception tracking confirmed
- [ ] Connection string consumed from env var at startup

## Learnings

- Setting the connection string env var does NOT auto-instrument Node.js apps
- Need explicit SDK setup (unlike .NET which has auto-instrumentation)

issue.title: bug(app): App Configuration service not integrated ΓÇö app not reading config from Azure App Config
issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #111.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/111
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 08:42:34
Original updated: 05/19/2026 08:47:31

---

## Problem

The Azure App Configuration resource exists and the container app has \AZURE_APPCONFIG_ENDPOINT\ and \AZURE_APPCONFIG_USE_MANAGED_IDENTITY\ env vars set, but the application code does not actually read configuration from App Configuration at runtime. No SDK integration exists.

## Expected

- App reads key-values from Azure App Configuration at startup
- Configuration refresh is wired (sentinel key pattern or polling)
- Feature flags are consumed from App Configuration

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] App Configuration SDK integrated in the web app (e.g. \@azure/app-configuration\ or \@azure/app-configuration-provider\)
- [ ] Runtime config reads from App Config using managed identity
- [ ] Configuration values are available to the app (auth settings, feature flags, etc.)
- [ ] Feature flags section populated in App Configuration

## Learnings

- Having env vars pointing to App Config is not the same as integrating with it
- Need SDK + provider setup in the app code, not just IaC

issue.title: bug(iac): provision Entra ID admin security group for resource administration
issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #110.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/110
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 07:52:29
Original updated: 05/19/2026 08:22:42

---

## Problem

There is no admin security group provisioned for managing Azure resources. Individual user accounts or the deploy SP are the only principals with access, which violates least-privilege and makes operational access management difficult.

## Expected

An Entra ID security group (e.g. sg-wawkr-admins-dev) should be provisioned via IaC or bootstrap with appropriate RBAC role assignments on the resource group. Team members are added to this group for operational access rather than granting individual role assignments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Entra ID security group created via bootstrap (chicken-egg: group must exist before IaC can reference it)
- [ ] Group object ID stored as GH variable (e.g. ADMIN_GROUP_OBJECT_ID)
- [ ] IaC assigns appropriate roles to the group on the resource group (Contributor or Reader + targeted elevated roles)
- [ ] Key Vault grants Key Vault Secrets Officer to the admin group for operational secret management
- [ ] App Configuration grants App Configuration Data Owner to the admin group
- [ ] No individual user RBAC assignments in IaC ΓÇö all human access via group membership
- [ ] Bootstrap outputs instructions for adding members to the group

There is no admin security group provisioned for managing Azure resources. Individual user accounts or the deploy SP are the only principals with access, which violates least-privilege and makes operational access management difficult.

## Expected

An Entra ID security group (e.g. sg-wawkr-admins-dev) should be provisioned via IaC or bootstrap with appropriate RBAC role assignments on the resource group. Team members are added to this group for operational access rather than granting individual role assignments.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Entra ID security group created via bootstrap (chicken-egg: group must exist before IaC can reference it)
- [ ] Group object ID stored as GH variable (e.g. ADMIN_GROUP_OBJECT_ID)
- [ ] IaC assigns appropriate roles to the group on the resource group (Contributor or Reader + targeted elevated roles)
- [ ] Key Vault grants Key Vault Secrets Officer to the admin group for operational secret management
- [ ] App Configuration grants App Configuration Data Owner to the admin group
- [ ] No individual user RBAC assignments in IaC ΓÇö all human access via group membership
- [ ] Bootstrap outputs instructions for adding members to the group

issue.title: bug(iac): Application Insights not configured for all services
issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #109.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/109
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 07:50:23
Original updated: 05/19/2026 08:22:40

---

## Problem

Application Insights instrumentation is not wired to all services in the IaC. Telemetry, distributed tracing, and monitoring are incomplete ΓÇö some services are flying blind in production.

## Expected

All deployed services (container app, Front Door, App Configuration) should emit telemetry to a shared Application Insights instance via IaC:

- Container app: APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING env var from KV or direct output
- Front Door: diagnostic settings sending to Log Analytics / App Insights workspace
- App Configuration: diagnostic settings for audit and request logs

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Application Insights resource deployed via Bicep (with Log Analytics workspace)
- [ ] Container app receives APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING env var via KV secret ref
- [ ] Front Door has diagnostic settings sending to the workspace
- [ ] App Configuration has diagnostic settings enabled
- [ ] No instrumentation keys hardcoded ΓÇö connection string sourced from IaC outputs or KV
- [ ] Deploy pipeline passes end-to-end including smoke tests

issue.title: bug(iac): App Configuration requires RBAC role assignment for managed identity
issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #108.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/108
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 07:46:42
Original updated: 05/19/2026 08:22:38

---

## Problem

The deploy pipeline fails because the container app's managed identity does not have the required RBAC role on the App Configuration instance. The service connector or direct access pattern needs a role assignment (e.g., App Configuration Data Reader) granted to the user-assigned managed identity.

## Expected

IaC should assign the appropriate RBAC role on the App Configuration resource to the managed identity used by the container app, following the same pattern as Key Vault and Cosmos DB.

## Root Cause

iac/config/app-configuration.bicep does not include a role assignment for the container app's managed identity. The Key Vault and Cosmos modules both grant RBAC ΓÇö App Configuration must do the same.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] App Configuration Data Reader role assigned to the managed identity on the App Configuration resource via Bicep
- [ ] No connection strings or access keys used ΓÇö RBAC only
- [ ] Deploy pipeline passes end-to-end including smoke tests

issue.title: bug(auth): provider endpoints return 500 due sqlite path in Container App
issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #103.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/103
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 06:01:41
Original updated: 05/19/2026 06:21:56

---

## Problem
Front Door endpoint now serves `/` and `/login` with 200, but auth provider endpoints still fail with 500:
- `/api/public/auth-providers`
- `/api/auth/providers`

## Evidence
Container logs show `SqliteError: unable to open database file` when auth routes execute.

## Requested fix
1. Define a writable production `DATABASE_URL` path for Container App runtime.
2. Codify the setting in IaC (not manual runtime mutation).
3. Add deployment health checks for `/api/public/auth-providers` and `/api/auth/providers`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Both auth provider endpoints return 200 in dev Front Door endpoint
- [ ] No sqlite file-open errors in Container App logs for auth route requests
- [ ] Setting is represented in IaC and deployment workflow validation

issue.title: bug(iac): service connectors not provisioned from IaC deployment
issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #102.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/102
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 06:01:18
Original updated: 05/19/2026 06:21:45

---

## Problem
Service Connectors are expected by deployment validation, but they are not present after IaC deployment in `wawkr-rg-dev`.

## Evidence
- `deploy-iac.yml` reaches `Validate Service Connector readiness` with notice: no Service Connector resources found.
- This causes follow-on validation failures when connector outputs are empty.
- Current IaC path does not reliably produce the expected `Microsoft.ServiceLinker/linkers` resources for the Container App.

## Requested fix
1. Ensure `iac/backend/service-connectors.bicep` reliably provisions all required linkers.
2. Ensure `iac/main.bicep` exports stable connector IDs/names when provisioned.
3. Align workflow validation behavior with `REQUIRE_SERVICE_CONNECTORS` so optional mode does not fail.
4. Add a post-deploy assertion that verifies expected connector count and provisioning state when required.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Service Connector resources are created via IaC in dev
- [ ] Deployment outputs include non-empty `serviceConnectorIds` when required
- [ ] `deploy-iac.yml` passes connector validation in required mode
- [ ] Documentation updated with connector prerequisites and expected outputs

issue.title: security: remove AUTH_SECRET deployment fallback and enforce Key Vault + MI
issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #101.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/101
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/19/2026 06:00:32
Original updated: 05/19/2026 07:10:18

---

## Problem
Current IaC/deploy path includes a fallback where `AUTH_SECRET` can be passed from GitHub secret into deployment parameters. This keeps deployments unblocked, but it is not the desired long-term security model.

## Why this matters
- RBAC controls **who can access** resources, not the secret value itself.
- `AUTH_SECRET` is still required as an app signing key value.
- Preferred model is: Key Vault stores secret, Container App reads via managed identity, no deployment-time secret fallback.

## Requested change
1. Remove deployment-time `authSecret` fallback parameter from IaC/workflows.
2. Enforce Key Vault-only `auth-secret` reference in Container App config.
3. Add bootstrap/preflight check to ensure `auth-secret` exists in Key Vault before deploy.
4. Fail deploy with clear message if MI/KV access is missing.
5. Document the RBAC + Key Vault provisioning path.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `iac/main.bicep` and `backend/container-app.bicep` no longer accept raw `authSecret` parameter
- [ ] `.github/workflows/deploy-iac.yml` no longer passes `secrets.AUTH_SECRET` into template params
- [ ] Deploy succeeds when KV secret + MI permissions are present
- [ ] Deploy fails fast with actionable error when KV secret is missing
- [ ] Docs updated with required RBAC roles and KV secret setup

issue.title: bug: AUTH_SECRET not provisioned in IaC or bootstrap (NEXTAUTH_SECRET name mismatch)
issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #90.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/90
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/18/2026 10:09:30
Original updated: 05/19/2026 06:03:52

---

## Bug Description
\AUTH_SECRET\ (Auth.js v5 required env var) is never provisioned end-to-end:

1. **Variable name mismatch**: \scripts/bootstrap.sh\ and \scripts/bootstrap.ps1\ generate \NEXTAUTH_SECRET\ (Auth.js v4 name). Auth.js v5 requires \AUTH_SECRET\. Local dev environments set the wrong variable.

2. **IaC gap**: \iac/backend/container-app.bicep\ wires \cosmos-endpoint\ and \cosmos-database\ from Key Vault but never adds \^Guth-secret\. \AUTH_SECRET\ is never set as a Container App environment variable via IaC.

3. **No Key Vault provisioning**: Bootstrap scripts only write to \.env.local\. There is no step that provisions \^Guth-secret\ into Azure Key Vault for production deployments.

## Impact
- Local dev: Auth.js session signing fails silently or uses wrong variable
- Production: Container App starts without \AUTH_SECRET\ ΓåÆ \/api/auth/*\ returns 500 ΓåÆ all auth broken

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] \container-app.bicep\ references \^Guth-secret\ from Key Vault and sets \AUTH_SECRET\ env var
- [ ] \ ootstrap.sh\/\ ootstrap.ps1\ generate \AUTH_SECRET\ (not \NEXTAUTH_SECRET\) for local dev
- [ ] Bootstrap scripts provision \^Guth-secret\ to Key Vault when \--provision-azure\ flag / \AZ_KV_NAME\ env var is set
- [ ] \^Gpps/web/.env.example\ documents \AUTH_SECRET\
- [ ] Bicep validates clean; Next.js build passes

issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #83.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/83
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/18/2026 05:42:13
Original updated: 05/18/2026 08:23:50

---

## Problem
The repo layout is hard to navigate because responsibilities are split across `ui-spec/`, `feature-specs/`, `iac/`, and `apps/` without a clear contributor-facing map, and there are many root-level files that look ad-hoc.

## Expected
A clear top-level information architecture that distinguishes:
- product design artifacts
- feature requirements/specs
- deployable application code

issue.title: [Bug] Login/Home alignment off at Front Door endpoint

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #82.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/82
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/17/2026 23:32:41
Original updated: 05/18/2026 09:25:45

---

## Summary
Login/home alignment is off in production-like endpoint; card is anchored low/left instead of expected centered layout.

## Affected URL
`https://wawkr-fd-dev-endpoint-c9gwggevbacscnfp.b01.azurefd.net/login?callbackUrl=%2F`

## Observed
- The login card appears shifted toward the lower-left area.
- Expected visual centering/viewport alignment is not maintained.

## Evidence
Screenshot captured locally:
`C:\Users\ivega\AppData\Local\Temp\copilot-image-0ff4ba.png`

## Expected
- Login container remains centered vertically and horizontally across common viewport sizes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Login layout is consistently centered on desktop/laptop widths
- [ ] No unintended offset from wrapper/container styles
- [ ] Verified at the affected Front Door endpoint

issue.title: [Feature] Config-managed auth provider enable/disable

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #80.

Source issue: https://github.com/ivegamsft/wawkr/issues/80
Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/17/2026 23:32:39
Original updated: 05/18/2026 09:59:59

---

## Summary
Use centralized configuration management to enable/disable login providers without code changes.

## Why
Current auth behavior is tightly coupled to env wiring and static UI assumptions. We need operational control to turn providers on/off per environment.

## Scope
- Add provider toggle flags in config management (Azure App Configuration / Key Vault-backed settings)
- Support independent toggles for Google, Apple, Microsoft Org, Microsoft Personal, and Email
- Update login page to render only currently enabled providers
- Add deploy preflight to validate provider toggle + credential consistency

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Provider toggles are stored in config management and read at runtime
- [ ] Login UI reflects enabled providers only
- [ ] Invalid toggle/credential combos fail preflight and block release
- [ ] Changes can be made without redeploying app code

Original created: 05/17/2026 23:32:39
Original updated: 05/18/2026 09:59:59

## Summary
Use centralized configuration management to enable/disable login providers without code changes.

## Why
Current auth behavior is tightly coupled to env wiring and static UI assumptions. We need operational control to turn providers on/off per environment.

## Scope
- Add provider toggle flags in config management (Azure App Configuration / Key Vault-backed settings)
- Support independent toggles for Google, Apple, Microsoft Org, Microsoft Personal, and Email
- Update login page to render only currently enabled providers
- Add deploy preflight to validate provider toggle + credential consistency

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Provider toggles are stored in config management and read at runtime
- [ ] Login UI reflects enabled providers only
- [ ] Invalid toggle/credential combos fail preflight and block release
- [ ] Changes can be made without redeploying app code

issue.body:
Migrated from $sourceRepo issue #79.

Original state: CLOSED
Original created: 05/17/2026 23:28:41
Original updated: 05/18/2026 08:31:38

---

## Summary
Production deployment does not enforce auth provider readiness. Releases can ship with mismatched or missing provider configuration, resulting in broken login buttons and failed auth flows.

## Impact
Auth regressions reach production without an explicit release block.

## Problem details
- No preflight step verifies required auth env vars/secrets for configured providers.
- Login page can present unavailable providers.
- There is no post-deploy probe for `/api/auth/providers` consistency.

## Expected
Deploy pipeline should block when auth provider configuration is incomplete or inconsistent.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Add preflight checks for auth provider env vars/secrets (Google, Apple, Microsoft, Email).
- [ ] Add post-deploy probe that compares `/api/auth/providers` with intended provider matrix.
- [ ] Fail release before cutover if auth provider checks fail.
